RunwayProtectArea.d: An area situated in the vicinity of a runway or provided to protect aircraft during manoeuvring, take-off and landing operations.

width.d: The physical width of the protection area.

length.d: The physical length of the protection area.

lighting.d: The availability of a lighting system that visually identifies the Protection Area in low visibility conditions.

obstacleFree.d: Indicates if the protection area is obstacle free.

surfaceProperties.d: Identifies the Surface Characteristics that describe the Airport Heliport Protection Area.

extent.d: Identifies the surface area of the Airport Heliport Protection Area.

type.d: A type of runway protect area.

status.d: The operational status of an airport/heliport movement area, as a category.

protectedRunwayDirection.d: (DO272/ED99) Each RunwayDisplacedArea feature?s attribute idthr shall provide the idthr object identifier value of the operationally corresponding RunwayThreshold (Rule 7). ()DO272/ED99)Each Stopway feature?s attribute idthr shall provide the idthr object identifier value of the operationally corresponding RunwayThreshold (Rule 8).

RunwayDirection.d: One of the two landing and take-off directions of a runway or a Final Approach and Takeoff Area (FATO).

designator.d: A designator for one of the two possible landing and/or take-off directions of a runway or Final Approach and Take-off Area (FATO).

trueBearing.d: The measured angle between the runway direction and True North at a given position.

trueBearingAccuracy.d: Accuracy of the measured angle between the runway direction and True North at a given position.

magneticBearing.d: The measured angle between the runway direction and Magnetic North at a given position.

patternVFR.d: The direction, i.e. left or right, of the Visual Flight Rules (VFR) flight pattern at an airport/heliport for a runway direction.

slopeTDZ.d: Touchdown zone longitudinal slope (slope of 1/3 of the runway length from threshold or first 3000 feet for runways longer than 9000 feet) for a runway direction.

elevationTDZ.d: The highest elevation of the runway Touch Down Zone (TDZ) for a runway direction.

elevationTDZAccuracy.d: The accuracy of the reported Touch Down Zone elevation

approachMarkingType.d: The type of runway direction marking related to landing categories such as precision, non-precision and basic.

approachMarkingCondition.d: The quality of the runway direction marking such as good, fair, poor and other.

classLightingJAR.d: A classification of the approach lighting system for a runway direction using as criteria Joint Aviation Requirements JAR-OPS 1 - Subpart E, Appendix 1 to 1.430.

precisionApproachGuidance.d: Degree to which navigation aids provide accurate approach guidance. Precision approaches utilize both lateral (course) and vertical (glideslope) information

usedRunway.d: (DO272/ED99) Each FinalApproachAndTakeOff feature?s attribute idthr shall provide the idrwy object identifier value of the corresponding HelipadThreshold (Rule 15).

startingElement.d: The runway element is the start of the runway direction. Typically used to indicate the location of a displaced area.

availability.d: The operational status of the RunwayDirection.

slope.d: The average slope of the physical runway from approach end to departure end.

approachGuidance.d: Classification of the runway based on the availability of visual and non-visual aids intended for landing operations.

RunwayCentrelinePoint.d: An operationally significant position on the centre line of a runway direction. A typical example is the runway threshold.

role.d: The role of an operationally significant position on the centre line of a runway direction.

designator.d: The designator of a runway centreline point, used to uniquely identify it at an airport/heliport.

location.d: Identifies the geographical position of the runway centreline point.

onRunway.d: Location of the runway centreline point.

associatedDeclaredDistance.d: Identifies the ruwnay declared distance for which the runway centreline point ensures.

navaidEquipment.d: A Navaid Equipment that is located near the runway and for which the relative position from a centreline point is defined.

relativeDistance.d: The distance from the physical start of the RunwayDirection to the point. E.g. displaced threshold distance.

onRunwayDirection.d: Identifies the runway direction on which the runway centreline point is located.

Runway.d: A defined rectangular area on a land or a water aerodrome/heliport prepared for the landing and take-off of aircraft. Note: this includes the concept of Final Approach and Take-Off Area (FATO) for helicopters.

designator.d: The designator of a runway, used to uniquely identify it at an airport/heliport.

type.d: The type can be either runway for airplanes or Final Approach and Take-off Area (FATO) for helicopters.

nominalLength.d: The declared longitudinal extent of the runway for operational (performance) calculations.

lengthAccuracy.d: Accuracy of the value of the physical length of the runway.

nominalWidth.d: The declared transversal extent of the runway for operational (performance) calculations.

widthAccuracy.d: Accuracy of the value of the physical width of the runway.

lengthStrip.d: The physical length of the strip. Where a strip is a defined area including the runway and, if applicable, the stopway.

widthStrip.d: The physical width of the strip. Where a strip is a defined area including the runway and, if applicable, the stopway.

lengthOffset.d: A value specifying the longitudinal offset of the strip, when it is not symmetrically extended beyond the two runway ends. Where a strip is a defined area including the runway and, if applicable, the stopway.

widthOffset.d: A value specifying the lateral offset of the strip, when it is not symmetrically extended beyond the two runway edges. Where a strip is a defined area including the runway and, if applicable, the stopway.

abandoned.d: An indicator that the surface is no longer in operational use, but is still physically present and visible, although usually in a degraded state.

surfaceProperties.d: Identifies the surface characteristics of the runway.

associatedAirportHeliport.d: Identifies the Airport where the Runway is situated.

overallContaminant.d: Identifies the contaminant of the runway.

referenceCodeFieldLength.d: The highest value of the aeroplane reference field lengths of the aeroplanes for which the runway is intended.

referenceCodeWingspan.d: The greatest wingspan of the aeroplanes for which the facility is intended.

depth.d: The depth of the water measured at low water level in the water runway should not be less than 1.8 m (6 ft.) or less than 0.3 m below the hull or floats when the seaplane is stationary and loaded to maximum takeoff weight.

ArrestingGear.d: A series of devices, namely engaging or catching devices and energy absorption devices used to stop an aircraft by absorbing its momentum in a routine, emergency landing or aborted take-off.

status.d: The operational status of the arresting gear device.

length.d: The overall length of a runway's arresting system, which consists of a series of devices used to stop an aircraft by absorbing its momentum.

width.d: The physical width of a runway's arresting system, which consists of a series of devices used to stop an aircraft by absorbing its momentum.

engageDevice.d: The type of device that is used to engage an aircraft upon landing on a runway in order to immediately stop the aircraft by absorbing its momentum.

absorbType.d: The type of energy absorber by which a runway's arresting system rapidly dissipates the kinetic energy of a moving aircraft that engages the arresting system, bringing the aircraft to a stop.

bidirectional.d: An indicator of whether or not both runway directions utilize arresting gear which, consists of a series of devices used to stop an aircraft by absorbing its momentum.

location.d: The distance from an identified runway's threshold to the runway's arresting system, which consists of a series of devices used to stop an aircraft by absorbing its momentum.

runwayDirection.d: Identifies the runway direction on which the arresting gear is used.

surfaceProperties.d: Describes the surface characteristics of the arresting gear.

extent_curveExtent.d: Identifies the shape of the arresting gear.

extent_surfaceExtent.d: Identifies the shape of the arresting gear.

extent_pointExtent.d: Identifies the shape of the arresting gear.

RunwayElement.d: Runway element may consist of one ore more polygons not defined as other portions of the runway class.

type.d: The type of runway element.

length.d: The length of the runway element.

width.d: The width of the runway element.

gradeSeparation.d: An indicator of the placement of the element at a different height from another element.

surfaceProperties.d: Identifies the surface characteristics of the runway element.

associatedRunway.d: Indicates which runways the Runway Element belongs to. Note that Runway Intersection elements will belong to more than one Runway. (DO272/ED99) Each RunwayElement feature?s attribute idrwy shall provide the idrwy object identifier value corresponding to the name of the real world runway (Rule 1). (DO272/ED99)Each RunwayIntersection feature?s attribute idrwi shall provide an idrwi object identifier value that corresponds to the names of the real world intersection runways (idrwy) (Rule 2). (DO272/ED99)Each RunwayShoulder feature?s attribute idrwy shall provide the idrwy object identifier value of the real world runway (Rule 3).

extent.d: Identifies the extent of the Ruwnay Element.

availability.d: The operational status of the RunwayElement.

VisualGlideSlopeIndicator.d: A visual guidance system that provides 'below/above glidepath' information to an aircraft executing an approach to a specific runway direction.

emergencyLighting.d: The availability of a back-up lighting system to be used in case of failure of the main lighting system.

intensityLevel.d: An indication of the relative intensity of the ground lighting system.

colour.d: An indication of the global colour of the ground lighting system.

element.d: Identifies the Light Elements that make up the Ground Light System

availability.d: The operational status of the GroundLightSystem.

type.d: The type of visual glide slope indicator system installed, based upon the number, colour, and/or position of various components. Where a visual glide slope indicator system provides 'below/above glide path' information to an aircraft executing an approach to a specific runway direction.

position.d: A location, relative to a runway centreline, of the visual approach slope indicator for a final approach and take off area (FATO)/runway direction. Where a visual glide slope indicator system provides 'below/above glide path' information to an aircraft executing an approach to a specific runway direction.

numberBox.d: The number of units that compose the visual glide slope indicator system, which provides 'below/above glide path' information to an aircraft executing an approach to a specific runway direction.

portable.d: An indicator of whether or not a runway's visual glide slope indicator system is capable of being transported or conveyed. Where a visual glide slope indicator system provides 'below/above glide path' information to an aircraft executing an approach to a specific runway direction.

slopeAngle.d: A descent angle determined by a visual glide slope indicator system for visual vertical guidance during the final approach of an aircraft. Where a visual glide slope indicator system provides 'below/above glide path' information to an aircraft executing an approach to a specific runway direction.

minimumEyeHeightOverThreshold.d: The minimum height of the aircraft cockpit over the threshold when the aircraft glide slope indicator is showing an on-slope indication.

runwayDirection.d: Identifies the Runway Direction for which the Visual Glide Slope Indicator provides guidance for.

thresholdDistance.d: The distance from the runway reference point (RRP) to the runway threshold.

displacementAngle.d: The angle of displacement of the axis of the VGSI relative to the runway centreline.

finalApproachRunwayOccupancySignal.d: An indication of the presence of a FAROS system that alerts pilots that the approaching runway is occupied.

RunwayVisualRange.d: A meteorological equipment providing information about the distance over which the pilot of an aircraft on the centre line of a runway can see the runway surface markings or the lights delineating the runway or identifying its centre line.

readingPosition.d: The position along the runway direction for which the reading is provided.

location.d: Location of the Runway Visual Range.

RunwayBlastPad.d: Specially prepared surface placed adjacent to the end of a runway to eliminate the erosive affect of the high wind forces produced by airplanes at the beginning of their takeoff rolls.

length.d: The overall length of a barrier used to divert and/or dissipate jet and/or propeller blast.

status.d: The operational status of an airport/heliport movement area, as a category. Where this movement area relates directly to the Runway Blast Pad.

usedRunwayDirection.d: Identifies the runway direction on which the blast pad is used.

extent.d: Identifies the extent of the runway blast pad.

surfaceProperties.d: Identifies the surface characteristics of the runway blast pad.

TaxiHoldingPosition.d: A designated position intended for traffic control at which taxiing aircraft and vehicles shall stop and hold until further cleared to proceed, when so instructed by the airport/heliport control tower.

landingCategory.d: Type of landing operations for which that holding position is relevant. For example, precision instrument approach category I, precision instrument approach category II, precision instrument approach category III.

status.d: An indication of the operational status of the taxi holding position. For example, normal, unserviceable, downgraded, work in progress, etc.

associatedGuidanceLine.d: (DO272/ED99) The value of a TaxiwayHoldingPosition feature?s attribute idlin shall be identical to the value of the corresponding TaxiwayElement feature?s attribute idlin (Rule 12).

protectedRunway.d: (DO272/ED99) The value of a TaxiwayHoldingPosition feature?s attribute idp shall be identical to the idrwy object identifier value of the protected real world runway (Rule 6). (DO272/ED99) The value of a TaxiwayHoldingPosition feature?s attribute idp shall be identical to the value of the operationally corresponding RunwayThresholds feature?s attribute idthr (Rule 20).

location.d: The location of the TaxiHoldingPosition.

type.d: The type of taxi holding positions based on the position along the taxiway.

Taxiway.d: A defined path at an airport/heliport established for the taxiing of aircraft/helicopters and intended to provide a link between one part of the airport/heliport and another, including aircraft/helicopter stand taxi-lines, apron taxiways, rapid exit taxiways, air taxiways etc.

designator.d: The textual designator of the taxiway.

type.d: An indication of a type of taxiway. For example: air taxiway, ground taxiway, exit/turnoff, rapid exit/turnoff, stub, turn around, etc.

width.d: The value of the physical width of the taxiway.

widthShoulder.d: The value of the taxiway shoulder width.

length.d: The value for the length of the taxiway.

abandoned.d: An indicator that a taxiway is no longer in operational use, but it is still physically present and visible, although usually in a degraded state.

surfaceProperties.d: Identifies the surface characteristics of the taxiway.

associatedAirportHeliport.d: Identifies the Airport where the Taxiway is situated.

contaminant.d: Identifies the contaminant of the taxiway.

availability.d: The operational status of the Taxiway.

diameter.d: A diameter measured at low water level of not less than twice the specified minimum width of the corresponding water turning basin .

depth.d: The depth of the water measured at low water level in the water taxiway should not be less than 1.8 m (6 ft.) or less than 0.3 m below the hull or floats when the seaplane is stationary and loaded to maximum takeoff weight.

type.d: The type of taxiway element.

length.d: The length of the taxiway element.

width.d: The width of the taxiway element.

gradeSeparation.d: An indication of the placement of the taxiway element at a different height from another element.

surfaceProperties.d: Identifies the surface characteristics of the taxiway element.

associatedTaxiway.d: (DO272/ED99) Each TaxiwayElement feature?s attribute idlin shall provide the idlin object identifier value corresponding to the name of the real world taxiway (Rule 9).

extent.d: Identifies the extent of the taxiway element.

availability.d: The operational status of the TaxiwayElement.

GuidanceLine.d: A line used to guide aircraft on and between airport movement areas.

designator.d: The identifier of a guidance line on a taxiway.

type.d: The type of guidance line on a taxiway.

usageDirection.d: Indicates the direction in which the guidance line can be used with reference to the start and end points of the associated ElevatedCurve.

connectedTouchDownLiftOff.d: Identifies the touch down lift off area that the guidance line connects to.

connectedRunwayCentrelinePoint.d: (OD272/ED99) The value of a RunwayExitLine feature?s attribute idthr shall be identical to the value of the operationally corresponding RunwayThresholds feature?s attribute idthr (Rule 21).

connectedApron.d: Identifies the apron that the guidance line connects to.

connectedStand.d: (DO272/ED99) Each StandGuidanceLine feature?s attribute idstd shall provide object identifier values for all corresponding ParkingStandLocations (Rule 22).

extent.d: Identifies the extent of the guidance line.

connectedTaxiway.d: Identifies the taxiway that the guidance line connects to.

availability.d: Information about usage permissions and/or constraints that apply to the GuidanceLine.

Apron.d: A defined area, on a land airport/heliport, intended to accommodate aircraft/helicopters for purposes of loading and unloading passengers, mail, or cargo, and for fueling, parking, or maintenance.

name.d: The name or designator used to identify an apron at an airport/heliport which has more than one apron.

abandoned.d: An indicator that an apron is no longer in operational use, but it is still physically present and visible, although usually in a degraded state.

surfaceProperties.d: Identifies the surface characteristics of which the Apron is described by.

associatedAirportHeliport.d: Identifies the Airport where the Apron is situated.

contaminant.d: Identifies the contaminant of the apron.

availability.d: The operational status of the Apron.

ApronElement.d: Parts of a defined apron area. ApronElements may have functional characteristics defined in the ApronElement type. ApronElements may have jetway, fuel, towing, docking and ground power services.

type.d: The type of an apron based upon its location on an airport/heliport and its general purpose.

jetwayAvailability.d: An indicator of the availability of jetway at an apron element.

towingAvailability.d: Availability of towing service at an apron element.

dockingAvailability.d: An indicator of the availability of docking station system at an apron element.

groundPowerAvailability.d: An indicator of the availability of ground power at an apron element.

length.d: The length of the apron element.

width.d: The width of the apron element.

associatedApron.d: (DO272/ED99) The value of a ParkingStandArea feature?s attribute idapron shall be identical to the value of the operationally corresponding ApronElement feature?s attribute idapron (Rule 23). (DO272/ED99) The value of a DeicingArea feature?s attribute idbase shall be identical to the value of the underlying ApronElement feature?s attribute idapron (Rule 26).

surfaceProperties.d: Identifies the surface characteristics of which the Apron Element is described by.

extent.d: Identifies the extent of the apron element.

supplyService.d: The AirportSupplyService provided at the ApronElement.

availability.d: The operational status of the ApronElement.

AircraftStand.d: A designated area on an apron intended to be used for parking an aircraft.

designator.d: The designator of the gate/stand. For example, 13, 84 A, etc.

type.d: An indicator identifying the characteristics of an aircraft stand. Examples: parking position on the apron, isolated aircraft stand, terminal building gate.

visualDockingSystem.d: A device used at the aircraft stand in order to help a pilot align and position an aircraft.

surfaceProperties.d: Identifies the Surface Characteristics for which the Gate Stand is described by.

location.d: The geographical reference position for the parking position.

apronLocation.d: (DO272/ED99) Each ParkingStandArea feature?s attribute idstd shall provide an idstd object identifier value that holds the idstd object identifier values of all corresponding ParkingStandLocations (Rule 13)

extent.d: Identifies the surface area of the Gate Stand.

contaminant.d: Identifies the contaminant of the gate stand.

availability.d: The operational status of the AircraftStand.

Road.d: An established surface route on the airport/heliport meant for the exclusive use of authorized vehicles and personnel.

designator.d: The designator or name of the service road.

status.d: An indicator of the operational status of a service road. For example, serviceable, unserviceable, work in progress, etc.

type.d: Type of road at an airport/heliport.

abandoned.d: An indicator that a road is no longer in operational use, but it is still physically present and visible, although usually in a degraded state.

associatedAirport.d: Identifies the Airport where the Road is situated.

surfaceProperties.d: Identifies the Surface Characteristics of the Road.

accessibleStand.d: Identifies the Gate Stand(s) for which the Road gives access.

surfaceExtent.d: Identifies the surface area of the Road.

DeicingArea.d: An area comprising an inner area for the parking of an aircraft to receive de-icing treatment and an outer area for the manoeuvring of two or more mobile de-icing equipment.

associatedApron.d: Identifies the Apron on which the Deicing Area is located on.

taxiwayLocation.d: Identifies the taxiway where the deicing area is located.

standLocation.d: Identifies the Gate Stand at which the Deicing Area is located.

surfaceProperties.d: Identifies the surface characteristics of which the Deicing Area is described by.

extent.d: Identifies the extent of the deicing area.

availability.d: The operational status of the DeicingArea.

designator.d: The textual designator of the deicing area.

PassengerLoadingBridge.d: Bridge for loading/unloading access to airplanes for passengers and crew.

type.d: Type of bridge used by passengers and crew to board and deplane an aircraft.

extent.d: Identifies the surface area of the Passenger Loading Bridge.

associatedStand.d: Identifies the gate stand associated with the passenger loading bridge.

annotation.d: A free text annotation concerning the feature/object or one of its properties

TouchDownLiftOffSafeArea.d: An obstacle free zone area situated in the vicinity of a touch down and lift-off area, provided to protect helicopters during manoeuvring, take-off and/or landing operations.

width.d: The physical width of the protection area.

length.d: The physical length of the protection area.

lighting.d: The availability of a lighting system that visually identifies the Protection Area in low visibility conditions.

obstacleFree.d: Indicates if the protection area is obstacle free.

surfaceProperties.d: Identifies the Surface Characteristics that describe the Airport Heliport Protection Area.

extent.d: Identifies the surface area of the Airport Heliport Protection Area.

protectedTouchDownLiftOff.d: Identifies the Touch Down Lift Off area that is protected by the Safe Area.

TouchDownLiftOff.d: A load bearing area on which a helicopter may touch down or lift-off.

designator.d: The designator of the touch down and lift-off area.

length.d: The value of the physical length of the touchdown and lift-off area.

width.d: The value of the physical width of the touchdown and lift-off area.

slope.d: The slope (rate of upward inclination of the surface from the horizontal) of the surface of a touch down and lift-off area.

helicopterClass.d: The class of a helicopter based on its performance during a critical power unit failure after take-off.

abandoned.d: An indicator that the touch down and lift-off area is no longer in operational use, but it is still physically present and visible, although usually in a degraded state.

aimingPoint.d: Aiming point for the TouchDownLiftOff zone.

extent.d: Identifies the surface area of the Touch Down Lift Off area.

surfaceProperties.d: Identifies the Surface Characteristics that describe the Touch Down Lift Off area.

associatedAirportHeliport.d: Identifies the Airport where the Touch Down Lift Off is situated.

approachTakeOffArea.d: Only for runways of type FATO (DO272/ED99) Each FinalApproachAndTakeOff feature?s attribute idrwy shall provide the idrwy object identifier value of the corresponding TouchDownAndLiftOff (Rule 14).

contaminant.d: Identifies the contaminant of the touch down lift off area.

availability.d: The operational status of the TouchDownLiftOff area.

aircraft.d: A combination of aircraft characteristics that are required to use TLOF area.

geometricCentre.d: The geographical location of the geometric centre of the TLOF.

ApronLightSystem.d: The lighting system provided for illuminating apron areas of an airport/heliport.

emergencyLighting.d: The availability of a back-up lighting system to be used in case of failure of the main lighting system.

intensityLevel.d: An indication of the relative intensity of the ground lighting system.

colour.d: An indication of the global colour of the ground lighting system.

element.d: Identifies the Light Elements that make up the Ground Light System

availability.d: The operational status of the GroundLightSystem.

position.d: An indication of the part of the apron served by the lighting system.

lightedApron.d: Identifies the Apron for which the Lighting System is provided.

TaxiwayLightSystem.d: The lighting system provided for a taxiway at an airport/heliport.

emergencyLighting.d: The availability of a back-up lighting system to be used in case of failure of the main lighting system.

intensityLevel.d: An indication of the relative intensity of the ground lighting system.

colour.d: An indication of the global colour of the ground lighting system.

element.d: Identifies the Light Elements that make up the Ground Light System

availability.d: The operational status of the GroundLightSystem.

position.d: A indication of the part of the taxiway surface the lighting system is serving. For example, centre line, edge, etc..

lightedTaxiway.d: Identifies the Taxiway for which the Lighting System is provided.

RunwayDirectionLightSystem.d: The lighting system provided for a landing and take-off direction, including the stopway lights.

emergencyLighting.d: The availability of a back-up lighting system to be used in case of failure of the main lighting system.

intensityLevel.d: An indication of the relative intensity of the ground lighting system.

colour.d: An indication of the global colour of the ground lighting system.

element.d: Identifies the Light Elements that make up the Ground Light System

availability.d: The operational status of the GroundLightSystem.

position.d: A indication of the part of the runway served by the runway direction lighting system.

associatedRunwayDirection.d: Identifies the Runway Direction for which the Lighting System is provided.

type.d: The type of lighting system present on the runway.

length.d: The length of the runway direction light system.

spacing.d: The spacing of light elements forming the runway direction light system.

group.d: The light group representing an array of light elements.

TouchDownLiftOffLightSystem.d: The lighting system provided for a Touch Down and Lift-Off (TLOF) surface at an airport/heliport.

emergencyLighting.d: The availability of a back-up lighting system to be used in case of failure of the main lighting system.

intensityLevel.d: An indication of the relative intensity of the ground lighting system.

colour.d: An indication of the global colour of the ground lighting system.

element.d: Identifies the Light Elements that make up the Ground Light System

availability.d: The operational status of the GroundLightSystem.

position.d: A indication of the part of the touch down and lift-off surface the lighting system is serving. For example, aiming point, edge, etc..

lightedTouchDownLiftOff.d: Identifies the Touch Down Lift Off area for which the Lighting System is provided.

GuidanceLineLightSystem.d: The lighting system for the centreline guidance line.

emergencyLighting.d: The availability of a back-up lighting system to be used in case of failure of the main lighting system.

intensityLevel.d: An indication of the relative intensity of the ground lighting system.

colour.d: An indication of the global colour of the ground lighting system.

element.d: Identifies the Light Elements that make up the Ground Light System

availability.d: The operational status of the GroundLightSystem.

lightedGuidanceLine.d: Identifies the Guidance Line for which the Lighting System is provided.

RunwayProtectAreaLightSystem.d: The lighting for the runway protect area.

emergencyLighting.d: The availability of a back-up lighting system to be used in case of failure of the main lighting system.

intensityLevel.d: An indication of the relative intensity of the ground lighting system.

colour.d: An indication of the global colour of the ground lighting system.

element.d: Identifies the Light Elements that make up the Ground Light System

availability.d: The operational status of the GroundLightSystem.

position.d: An indication of the part of the runway served by the runway protect area lighting system.

lightedArea.d: Identifies the Runway Protect Area for which the Lighting System is provided.

length.d: The length of the runway protection area light system.

TaxiHoldingPositionLightSystem.d: Lighting system for a taxiway hold position.

emergencyLighting.d: The availability of a back-up lighting system to be used in case of failure of the main lighting system.

intensityLevel.d: An indication of the relative intensity of the ground lighting system.

colour.d: An indication of the global colour of the ground lighting system.

element.d: Identifies the Light Elements that make up the Ground Light System

availability.d: The operational status of the GroundLightSystem.

type.d: The kind of lighting aid provided for the taxiway holding position.

taxiHolding.d: Identifies the Taxi Holding Position for which the Lighting System is provided.

ApproachLightingSystem.d: An airport lighting facility which provides visual guidance to landing aircraft by radiating light beams in a directional pattern by which the pilot aligns the aircraft with the final approach path for landing.

emergencyLighting.d: The availability of a back-up lighting system to be used in case of failure of the main lighting system.

intensityLevel.d: An indication of the relative intensity of the ground lighting system.

colour.d: An indication of the global colour of the ground lighting system.

element.d: Identifies the Light Elements that make up the Ground Light System

availability.d: The operational status of the GroundLightSystem.

classICAO.d: Classification of the approach lighting system using as criteria the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Annex 14 standards and recommended practices.

type.d: A regional or organisation specific classification of the approach lighting system equipment.

length.d: The overall length of the approach lighting system.

sequencedFlashing.d: An indication that sequenced flashing is available for the approach lighting system.

alignmentIndicator.d: An indication that a runway alignment indicator is available for the approach lighting system.

servedRunwayDirection.d: Identifies the Runway Direction that the ALS serves.

TaxiwayMarking.d: A symbol or group of symbols displayed on the surface of the taxiway.

markingICAOStandard.d: Indicates the airport/heliport protection area surface marking is in accordance with International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) standard as described in Annex 14.

condition.d: The quality of airport/heliport protection area surface marking such as good, fair, poor and other.

element.d: Identifies the Marking Elements of which the Marking is made.

markingLocation.d: An indication of the location of the marking relative to the surface of a taxiway.

markedTaxiway.d: (DO272/ED99) The value of a TaxiwayGuidanceLine feature?s attribute idlin shall be identical to the value of the corresponding TaxiwayElement feature?s attribute idlin (Rule 10). (DO272/ED99) The value of a TaxiwayIntersectionMarking feature?s attribute idlin shall be identical to the value of the corresponding TaxiwayElement feature?s attribute idlin (Rule 11).

markedElement.d: Identifies the taxiway element that is marked.

type.d: the type of marking present on the taxiway

ApronMarking.d: A symbol or group of symbols displayed on the surface of an apron of an airport/heliport.

markingICAOStandard.d: Indicates the airport/heliport protection area surface marking is in accordance with International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) standard as described in Annex 14.

condition.d: The quality of airport/heliport protection area surface marking such as good, fair, poor and other.

element.d: Identifies the Marking Elements of which the Marking is made.

markingLocation.d: An indication of the location of the marking relative to the surface of an apron.

markedApron.d: Identifies the Apron on which the Apron Marking is marked.

AirportProtectionAreaMarking.d: A symbol or group of symbols displayed on the edge of the landing protection area at an airport/heliport.

markingICAOStandard.d: Indicates the airport/heliport protection area surface marking is in accordance with International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) standard as described in Annex 14.

condition.d: The quality of airport/heliport protection area surface marking such as good, fair, poor and other.

element.d: Identifies the Marking Elements of which the Marking is made.

markingLocation.d: The location of the marking on the airport protection area.

markedProtectionArea.d: Identifies the Airport Heliport Protection Area that is marked.

TouchDownLiftOffMarking.d: A symbol or group of symbols displayed on the surface of the touch down and lift-off area at an airport/heliport.

markingICAOStandard.d: Indicates the airport/heliport protection area surface marking is in accordance with International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) standard as described in Annex 14.

condition.d: The quality of airport/heliport protection area surface marking such as good, fair, poor and other.

element.d: Identifies the Marking Elements of which the Marking is made.

markingLocation.d: An indication of the location of the marking relative to the surface of a touch down and lift-off area.

markedTouchDownLiftOff.d: Identifies the Touch Down Lift Off area that is marked.

RunwayMarking.d: A symbol or group of symbols displayed on the surface of the runway.

markingICAOStandard.d: Indicates the airport/heliport protection area surface marking is in accordance with International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) standard as described in Annex 14.

condition.d: The quality of airport/heliport protection area surface marking such as good, fair, poor and other.

element.d: Identifies the Marking Elements of which the Marking is made.

markingLocation.d: An indication of the location of the marking relative to the surface of a runway.

markedRunway.d: The runway having the runway markings. (DO272/ED99) Each RunwayMarking feature?s attribute idrwy shall provide the idrwy object identifier value of the real world runway (Rule 4).

GuidanceLineMarking.d: A symbol or group of symbols displayed as the guidance line.

markingICAOStandard.d: Indicates the airport/heliport protection area surface marking is in accordance with International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) standard as described in Annex 14.

condition.d: The quality of airport/heliport protection area surface marking such as good, fair, poor and other.

element.d: Identifies the Marking Elements of which the Marking is made.

markedGuidanceLine.d: Identifies the Guidance Line on which the Guidance Marking Line is marked.

DeicingAreaMarking.d: A symbol or group of symbols displayed on the surface of a Deicing Area

markingICAOStandard.d: Indicates the airport/heliport protection area surface marking is in accordance with International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) standard as described in Annex 14.

condition.d: The quality of airport/heliport protection area surface marking such as good, fair, poor and other.

element.d: Identifies the Marking Elements of which the Marking is made.

markedDeicingArea.d: Identifies the Deicing Area that is marked.

TaxiHoldingPositionMarking.d: A symbol or group of symbols displayed on the surface of a Taxiway indicating the location of the Taxi Holding Position.

markingICAOStandard.d: Indicates the airport/heliport protection area surface marking is in accordance with International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) standard as described in Annex 14.

condition.d: The quality of airport/heliport protection area surface marking such as good, fair, poor and other.

element.d: Identifies the Marking Elements of which the Marking is made.

markedTaxiHold.d: Identifies the Taxi Holding Position that is marked.

StandMarking.d: A symbol or group of symbols displayed on the surface of the Aircraft Stand.

markingICAOStandard.d: Indicates the airport/heliport protection area surface marking is in accordance with International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) standard as described in Annex 14.

condition.d: The quality of airport/heliport protection area surface marking such as good, fair, poor and other.

element.d: Identifies the Marking Elements of which the Marking is made.

markedStand.d: Identifies the Gate Stand at which the Gate Stand Markings are marked.

FloatingDockSite.d: Floating facility which can serve as a mooring place for vessels or as a floating dry dock.

extent.d: Identifies the extent of the floating dock site.

MarkingBuoy.d: A floating marker, for a seaplane landing area, which is moored to the bottom at a specific known location, which is used as an aid to navigation or for other special purposes.

designator.d: Official number of the marking buoy at a seaplane landing area.

type.d: The type of the marking buoy at a seaplane landing area.

colour.d: Colour of the marking buoy at a seaplane landing area.

theSeaplaneLandingArea.d: The seaplane landing area which is marked by the buoy

location.d: Identifies the geographical location of the marking buoy.

SeaplaneLandingArea.d: Area on water specifically designated for take-offs and landings of seaplanes.

rampSite.d: Identifies the ramp site associated to the seaplane landing area.

dockSite.d: Identifies the dock site(s) associated with the seaplane landing area.

extent.d: Identifies the extent of the seaplane landing area.

availability.d: The operational status of the SeaplaneLandingArea.

assignedGangway.d: The gangway the seaplane landing area is associated with.

associatedAirportHeliport.d: The airport/heliport the seaplane landing area is associated with.

SeaplaneRampSite.d: Ramps specifically designed to transit seaplanes from land to water and vice versa.

extent.d: Identifies the extent of the ramp site.

centreline.d: Identifies the centreline of the ramp site.

WorkArea.d: Part of an airport/heliport movement area that is under construction.

type.d: The type of work performed in the work area.

plannedOperational.d: Date when the activities in the construction area are expected to be operational.

associatedAirportHeliport.d: Identifies the Airport where the Work Area is situated.

extent.d: The extent of the WorkArea.

activation.d: Time period during which the building site is active or not.

SurveyControlPoint.d: A monumented survey control point. Or A surveying reference point marked by a permanently fixed marker.

designator.d: The identifier of the survey control point (a surveying reference point marked by a permanently fixed marker).

associatedAirportHeliport.d: Identifies the Airport at which the Survey Control Point is located.

location.d: Identifies the geospatial location of the Survey Control Point.

NonMovementArea.d: Area where aircraft cannot be seen by a control tower and therefore are restricted to move.

associatedAirportHeliport.d: Indicates the Airport where the Non-movement Area is situated.

extent.d: Identifies the surface area of the Non-movement Area.

AirportHeliportCollocation.d: The sharing by two airport/heliports of some or all of their ground facilities.

type.d: An indication of the extent of the collocation situation of the two airport/heliports.

dependentAirport.d: This is the dependant airport which is using the facilities of the host airport.

AirportHeliport.d: A defined area on land or water (including any buildings, installations and equipment) intended to be used either wholly or in part for the arrival, departure and surface movement of aircraft/helicopters.

designator.d: A designator for an airport/heliport.

name.d: The primary official name of an airport/heliport as designated by an appropriate authority.

locationIndicatorICAO.d: The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) location indicator of the airport/heliport, as listed in ICAO DOC 7910.

designatorIATA.d: The identifier that is assigned to a location in accordance with rules (resolution 767) governed by the International Air Transport Association (IATA).

type.d: The type of airport/heliport. For example, aerodrome only, combined aerodrome/heliport or simple landing site.

certifiedICAO.d: The airport/heliport conformity to applicable ICAO safety regulatory requirements.

privateUse.d: An airport or heliport not open for the public. Only for the use of the owners.

controlType.d: The primary organization type in terms of civil or military, which controls the airport/heliport.

fieldElevation.d: The vertical distance above Mean Sea Level (MSL) of the highest point of the landing area.

fieldElevationAccuracy.d: The vertical distance from the stated elevation within which there is a defined confidence of the true position falling.

verticalDatum.d: A reference surface with respect to which elevations and/or depths are specified at the airport/heliport.

magneticVariation.d: The angular difference between True North and Magnetic North measured at a given position and date.

magneticVariationAccuracy.d: The accuracy of the Magnetic Variation in angle degrees.

dateMagneticVariation.d: The date on which an associated magnetic variation was measured at the airport/heliport.

magneticVariationChange.d: The annual rate of change of the magnetic variation at a specified airport/heliport.

referenceTemperature.d: The monthly mean of the daily maximum temperatures for the hottest month of the year at an airport/heliport.

altimeterCheckLocation.d: The availability of a point or area designated at an airport/heliport where the checking of an altimeter system can be accomplished.

secondaryPowerSupply.d: The availability of emergency power supply for the airport/heliport.

windDirectionIndicator.d: The availability of a device, at the airport/heliport, that indicates the direction and the intensity of the wind.

landingDirectionIndicator.d: The availability of a device that indicates visually the direction currently designated for landing and for take-off.

transitionAltitude.d: The altitude at or below which the vertical position of an aircraft is controlled by reference to altitudes at the airport/heliport.

transitionLevel.d: The lowest flight level available for use above the transition altitude at the airport/heliport.

lowestTemperature.d: The monthly mean of the daily minimum temperatures for the coldest month of the year at an airport/heliport.

abandoned.d: An indicator that the airport/heliport is no longer in operational use, but it's infrastructure is still present and visible from the air.

certificationDate.d: The date when the airport/heliport certification has been issued by the supervising authority.

certificationExpirationDate.d: The date when the airport/heliport certification will become invalid.

servedCity.d: Identifies the Cities that the Airport serves.

responsibleOrganisation.d: The organisation which is responsible for managing the airport/heliport.

altimeterSource.d: Indicates the Altimeter Source(s) located at a particular AirportHeliport.

availability.d: Information about the operational status of the airport/heliport.

timeZone.d: The indication of the time reference system in which an airport/heliport resides.

segmentedCircleMarker.d: The indication of the presence of a segmented circle marker system at an airport/heliport.

AltimeterSource.d: An instrument that measures and indicates the elevation at which an object, such as an airplane, is located

isRemote.d: Indications if the Altimeter is Remote or Local.

isPrimary.d: Indicates if the Altimeter is Primary or Secondary.

availability.d: Information about the operational status of the AltimeterSource.

AirportHotSpot.d: A location on airport/heliport movement area with a history or potential risk of collision or runway incursion, and where heightened attention by pilots/drivers is necessary.

designator.d: An identifier by which the hot spot is labelled on airport maps.

instruction.d: Action to be taken by the crew and/or vehicle drivers when approaching a hot spot at the airport/heliport.

area.d: The area on the airport/heliport that has been identified as a hot spot

affectedAirport.d: The AirportHeliport where the hot spot has been identified.

AuthorityForAirspace.d: The responsibility that one organisation has for an airspace.

type.d: A categorisation of the role that one organisation has for an airspace.

responsibleOrganisation.d: The organisation responsible for the airspace.

assignedAirspace.d: The airspace that the OrganizationAuthority has assigned authority over.

Airspace.d: A defined three dimensional region of space relevant to air traffic.

type.d: An indicator of the general structure or characteristics of a particular airspace. Where airspace is a defined three dimensional region of space relevant to air traffic.

designator.d: A published sequence of characters allowing the identification of the airspace. Where airspace is a defined three dimensional region of space relevant to air traffic.

localType.d: A type designator used locally (inside a State or a Region) for a particular airspace sub-category. Where airspace is a defined three dimensional region of space relevant to air traffic.

name.d: The name given to an airspace by a responsible authority. It should be written as published, with no significance to upper or lower case letters. Where airspace is a defined three dimensional region of space relevant to air traffic.

designatorICAO.d: An indicator of whether an Airspace Designator is recorded in ICAO Doc. 7910, 'Location Indicators'. Where airspace is a defined three dimensional region of space relevant to air traffic.

controlType.d: The primary organization type in terms of civil or military, providing air traffic services within a designated airspace. Where airspace is a defined three dimensional region of space relevant to air traffic.

upperLowerSeparation.d: A flight level (e.g., 18000 feet MSL) that indicates the division of airspace between lower and upper airspace.

class.d: A block of airspace with a specific class.

protectedRoute.d: The route protected by the airspace.

geometryComponent.d: An portion of airspace that contributes to the defintion of an Airspace geometry.

activation.d: The operational status of the Airspace.

GeoBorder.d: A physical or political border. In general, it will be the border between two countries or States but could also be a coastline, the description of the bank of an important river, or any other geographical shape which can be named and used to describe the border of an airspace. If two countries/States have more than one common border, each one will be an occurrence of this entity.

name.d: A label for a physical or political border. If the two countries (States) have more than one common border, each one will have a different name. In general, it will be the border between two countries or States but could also be a coastline, the description of the bank of an important river, or any other geographical shape which can be named and used to describe the border of an airspace. If two countries/States have more than one common border, each one will be an occurrence of this entity.

type.d: An indicator of the type of physical or political border. In general, it will be the border between two countries or States but could also be a coastline, the description of the bank of an important river, or any other geographical shape which can be named and used to describe the border of an airspace. If two countries/States have more than one common border, each one will be an occurrence of this entity. The most common situation is the political boundary between two countries.

PrecisionApproachRadar.d: Primary radar equipment used to determine the position of an aircraft during final approach, in terms of lateral and vertical deviations relative to a nominal approach path, and in range relative to touchdown.

name.d: Textual name of the equipment.

range.d: The applicable range of the equipment to detect aircraft.

rangeAccuracy.d: Accuracy of the applicable range of the equipment to detect aircraft.

dualChannel.d: Indicates whether the component has dual frequency.

movingTargetIndicator.d: Indicates whether a Moving Target Indicator (MTI) is available for the component. The MTI function eliminates ground clutter.

standbyPower.d: Indicates how the component is powered if the primary power fails.

digital.d: Indicates if the radar equipment is digital or analogue.

militaryUseOnly.d: Indicates the equipment is for military use only.

specialUseOnly.d: Indicates the equipment is for special use procedures only such as Helipads, etc.

specialAircraftOnly.d: Indicates the equipment is to be only used for certain type of aircraft that are capable of using it. In some instances, the slope angle or procedure can only be flown by high performance aircraft.

magneticVariation.d: The angular difference between True North and Magnetic North measured at a given position and date.

dateMagneticVariation.d: The date on which the magnetic variation had this value.

contact.d: Identifies the contact information of the group or individual associated with the Radar Equipment. This will be a contact who is outside of the associated Organisation Authority for the Radar System. It could be the maintenance technician for the radar system.

location.d: The geographical point at which the radar is located.

precisionApproachRadarType.d: Denotes the type of Precision Approach Radar.

slope.d: The glideslope angle at which the PAR provides landing assistance.

slopeAccuracy.d: The accuracy of the glideslope angle at which the PAR provides landing assistance.

reflector.d: Identifies the Reflectors utilized with a PAR.

PrimarySurveillanceRadar.d: Primary Surveillance Radar is a radar system which detects the position of all the objects within its coverage that can reflect its transmitted radio signals.

name.d: Textual name of the equipment.

range.d: The applicable range of the equipment to detect aircraft.

rangeAccuracy.d: Accuracy of the applicable range of the equipment to detect aircraft.

dualChannel.d: Indicates whether the component has dual frequency.

movingTargetIndicator.d: Indicates whether a Moving Target Indicator (MTI) is available for the component. The MTI function eliminates ground clutter.

location.d: The geographical point at which the radar is located.

verticalCoverageAltitude.d: Altitude for which the Radar provides vertical coverage.

verticalCoverageDistance.d: Distance for which the Radar provides vertical coverage.

verticalCoverageAzimuth.d: Azimuth for which the Radar provides vertical coverage.

antennaTiltFixed.d: Indicates whether the antenna tilt is Variable or Fixed.

tiltAngle.d: Angle at which the antenna is tilted.

automatedRadarTerminalSystem.d: The Automated Radar Terminal System (ARTS) is a system in the air traffic control system using radar intelligence to detect and display pertinent data such as flight identification, altitude, and position of aircraft operating in the terminal area. A Radar with this attribute automatically tracks controlled aircraft and presents alpha-numeric information adjacent to their targets. It may even automatically calculate the separation between different aircrafts and provide an alert if that separation is compromised as per the set standards.

groundStation.d: The ground station where the Radar Scope is utilized.

type.d: Defines the type of Primary Surveillance Radar (i.e. ASR or ARSR).

RadarSystem.d: One or more Radar Equipment providing radar services.

type.d: Defines the type of service for the Radar System.

model.d: Model of the equipment ( ASR-11, etc)

generalTerrainMonitor.d: General Terrain Monitors (GTM) monitor aircraft clearance above the highest terrain and obstacles in a general area

broadcastIdentifier.d: The Identifier broadcasted for a Secondary Radar.

radarEquipment.d: The equipment that make up the component(s) of a Radar System.

office.d: Defines the Offices that manage the Radar Equipment.

airportHeliport.d: Identifies the Airport Heliport at whicht the system is located or is near.

PARRunway.d: Indicates what runway(s) the radar services.

location.d: This is the location used when the radar system acts as a significant point. This location is usually the location of one of the radar equipments.

SecondarySurveillanceRadar.d: Secondary Surveillance Radar (SSR aka Secondary Radar (SECRA)) is a radar system in which the object to be detected is fitted with the cooperative equipment in the form of a radio receiver/transmitter (transponder). Radar pulses transmitted from the searching transmitter/receiver (interrogator) site are received in the cooperative equipment and used to trigger a distinctive transmission from the transponder. This reply transmission, rather than a reflected signal, is then received back at the transmitter/receiver site for processing and display at an air traffic control facility.

name.d: Textual name of the equipment.

range.d: The applicable range of the equipment to detect aircraft.

rangeAccuracy.d: Accuracy of the applicable range of the equipment to detect aircraft.

dualChannel.d: Indicates whether the component has dual frequency.

movingTargetIndicator.d: Indicates whether a Moving Target Indicator (MTI) is available for the component. The MTI function eliminates ground clutter.

standbyPower.d: Indicates how the component is powered if the primary power fails.

specialUseOnly.d: Indicates the equipment is for special use procedures only such as Helipads, etc.

specialAircraftOnly.d: Indicates the equipment is to be only used for certain type of aircraft that are capable of using it. In some instances, the slope angle or procedure can only be flown by high performance aircraft.

dateMagneticVariation.d: The date on which the magnetic variation had this value.

contact.d: Identifies the contact information of the group or individual associated with the Radar Equipment. This will be a contact who is outside of the associated Organisation Authority for the Radar System. It could be the maintenance technician for the radar system.

location.d: The geographical point at which the radar is located.

verticalCoverageAltitude.d: Altitude for which the Radar provides vertical coverage.

verticalCoverageDistance.d: Distance for which the Radar provides vertical coverage.

verticalCoverageAzimuth.d: Azimuth for which the Radar provides vertical coverage.

antennaTiltFixed.d: Indicates whether the antenna tilt is Variable or Fixed.

tiltAngle.d: Angle at which the antenna is tilted.

automatedRadarTerminalSystem.d: The Automated Radar Terminal System (ARTS) is a system in the air traffic control system using radar intelligence to detect and display pertinent data such as flight identification, altitude, and position of aircraft operating in the terminal area. A Radar with this attribute automatically tracks controlled aircraft and presents alpha-numeric information adjacent to their targets. It may even automatically calculate the separation between different aircrafts and provide an alert if that separation is compromised as per the set standards.

groundStation.d: The ground station where the Radar Scope is utilized.

transponder.d: Mode S, or mode select, despite also being called a transponder radar system replacement for Air Traffic Control Radar Beacon System (ATCRBS), is actually a data packet protocol which can be used to augment ATCRBS transponder positioning equipment (radar and TCAS). Mode S is designed to fully interface with ATCRBS systems: mode S SSRs can interrogate ATCRBS transponders, and AIS-P transponders will also reply to older ATCRBS and TCAS interrogations.

autonomous.d: Indicates the SRR is autonomous or independent.

monopulse.d: Monopulse radar is an adaptation of conical scanning radar which sends additional information in the radar signal in order to avoid problems caused by rapid changes in signal strength. The system also makes jamming more difficult. Most radars designed since the 1960s are monopulse systems.

HoldingAssessment.d: The geometry of surfaces that define altitude levels and the structure of an area used to evaluate obstacles for determining holding patterns.

upperLimit.d: Max altitude allowed for all aircraft categories at all defined speeds

upperLimitReference.d: A code indicating the reference for a vertical distance. Two series of values exist: 1) real distance: from GND, from the MSL, from the WGS-84 ellipsoid 2) pressure distance.

lowerLimit.d: Minimum altitude allowed for all aircraft categories at all defined speeds

lowerLimitReference.d: A code indicating the reference for a vertical distance. Two series of values exist: 1) real distance: from GND, from the MSL, from the WGS-84 ellipsoid 2) pressure distance.

speedLimit.d: Restricted speed for containment in a smaller pattern

legLengthToward.d: Leg length for when holding is toward the navaid

legLengthAway.d: Leg length for when holding is away the navaid

holdingPoint.d: Identifies the point for which safe holding id designed for.

unplannedHolding.d: Identifies the Unplanned Holding determined by the Holding Assessment.

assessedHoldingPattern.d: The HoldingPattern assessed by the HoldingAssessment.

StandardLevelTable.d: A table of consecutive cruising levels described under vertical separation criteria limited by an upper and lower level and used by General Air Traffic.

name.d: A code identifying the table of discrete cruising levels. For example, ICAO IFR, ICAO VFR, ICAO IFR RVSM, etc.

standardICAO.d: An indication whether the table is according to the ICAO SARPS.

StandardLevelSector.d: The general rule by which standard level columns are used in a national airspace or within a region. For example, in France, IFR odd RVSM levels are used between 0 and 179 degrees.

flightRule.d: A code indicating the flight rules observed by the aircraft. For example IFR or VFR.

fromTrack.d: The start angle of the sector relative to the North.

toTrack.d: The end angle of the sector relative to the North.

angleType.d: A code indicating the direction of the zero bearing. For example, magnetic north or true north.

applicableAirspace.d: The airspace into which the standard level sector applies.

applicableLevelColumn.d: The StandardLevelColumn for which the StandardLevelSector applies.

StandardLevelColumn.d: A column of consecutive cruising levels within a standard level table.

series.d: A code identifying the column. For example, ODD or EVEN.

unitOfMeasurement.d: The unit of measurement used by the column.

separation.d: A code indicating that reduced vertical separation minima is applied in the column.

levelTable.d: The StandardLevelTable that the StandardLevelColumn belongs to.

RadioFrequencyArea.d: A limitation, such as coverage, usability, etc., of a navaid equipment or Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), service frequency or service volume.

type.d: A code indicating the type of radio navigation aid or Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) limitation.

angleScallop.d: The value of the scalloping angle, which may affect the radial reading of a VOR or TACAN in plus or minus.

signalType.d: The type of signal that is affected by the usage limitation.

equipment_navaidEquipment.d: Identifies a choice of a radio communication channel, a navigational aid or a special navigation station.

equipment_frequency.d: Identifies a choice of a radio communication channel, a navigational aid or a special navigation station.

equipment_specialNavigationStation.d: Identifies a choice of a radio communication channel, a navigational aid or a special navigation station.

equipment_precisionApproachRadar.d: Identifies a choice of a radio communication channel, a navigational aid or a special navigation station.

equipment_radar.d: Identifies a choice of a radio communication channel, a navigational aid or a special navigation station.

sector.d: Identifies the Circle Sector defined by a Radio Frequency Area.

extent.d: Designated part of a surface movement area where a specific frequency is required by air traffic control or ground control

equipment_augmentationService.d: Identifies a choice of a radio communication channel, a navigational aid or a special navigation station.

SpecialDate.d: A calendar date that has a special meaning for a particular State/organisation and which may be referred to in the description of the schedules associated with various aeronautical features.

type.d: An indication of the kind of the special dates.

dateYear.d: The year concerned. If no year is indicated, then the same date will be concerned every year.

name.d: The name by which the date is known by the public (especially for public holidays).

authority.d: The State or organisation that observes the special date.

RadioCommunicationChannel.d: A radio frequency band of sufficient width and associated identification data used for one- or two-way communication from or to a transmitter on the ground or in the air.

rank.d: A code indicating the role of the communication channel, in terms of primary, alternate, emergency, etc.

frequencyTransmission.d: The value of the transmission frequency.

frequencyReception.d: The value of the reception frequency.

channel.d: The identifier of the radio channel on which the communication takes place.

logon.d: A specified code used for data link, such as used for logon to an ATS unit.

emissionType.d: A code indicating the type of emission, as defined at the 1979 ITU World Administrative Radio Conference. For example, A3E, etc..

selectiveCall.d: A code indicating if whether or not a frequency treats "selective call".

flightChecked.d: Indicates if the communication channel has been flight checked.

trafficDirection.d: Indicates the eventual directionality of the communication channel.

location.d: The location from where the radio are transmitted.

availability.d: The operational status of the RadioCommunicationChannel.

PilotControlledLighting.d: Service providing airborne control of lights by keying the aircraft's microphone. Often available at locations without specified hours for lighting and where there is no control tower or Flight Service Station (FSS); or when the tower or FSS is closed (locations with part-time tower or FSS).

type.d: Type of pilot controlled lighting service - standard or non-standard.

duration.d: The length of time the lighting is illuminated, normally 15 minutes.

intensitySteps.d: The number of intensity steps/levels for a particular type of lighting system.

standByIntensity.d: The intensity step/level of the lighting system when not in use.

radioFrequency.d: The radio frequency to be used by the pilot for the activation of the system.

activationInstruction.d: Operational instructions for controlling the lighting systems.

controlledLightIntensity.d: Identifies the Light Activation that the Pilot Controlled Lighting controls.

activatedGroundLighting.d: Identifies the Ground Light System that the Pilot Controlled Lighting activates.

InformationService.d: A kind of service that consists in the provision of aeronautical, meteorological, traffic and related information to aircraft crew and other actors involved in flight operations, in flight or on the ground.

flightOperations.d: The destination (arriving, departing, etc.) of the flights for which the information is provided.

rank.d: The order of priority of the service, such as "primary" or "alternate".

compliantICAO.d: A code indicating whether the service is compliant with the ICAO standards and recommended practices specified for this type of service.

name.d: A free text name by which the service is identified.

location.d: The location from where the service is provided.

serviceProvider.d: Identifies the Unit for which Services are provided.

call-sign.d: In aeronautical radio communication the Unit providing a Service is identified by its CALL SIGN.

radioCommunication.d: The radio frequency on which the service is provided.

groundCommunication.d: The point of contact on the ground for the service.

SDF.d: Simplified Directional Facility (SDF) provides a final approach course similar to that of the ILS localizer although is not as precise as Localizer. It does not provide glide slope information. The SDF transmits signals within the range of 108.10 to 111.95 MHz. The approach techniques and procedures used in an SDF instrument approach are essentially the same as those employed in executing a standard localizer approach except the SDF course may not be aligned with the runway and the course may be wider, resulting in less precision. Usable off-course indications are limited to 35 degrees either side of the course centreline. Instrument indications received beyond 35 degrees should be disregarded. This angle is generally not more than 3 degrees. The SDF signal is fixed at either 6 degrees or 12 degrees as necessary to provide maximum flyability and optimum course quality.

DesignatedPoint.d: A geographical location not marked by the site of a radio navigation aid, used in defining an ATS route, the flight path of an aircraft or for other navigation or ATS purposes.

designator.d: The coded designator of the point. For example, the five-letter ICAO name of the point, etc..

aimingPoint.d: The DesignatedPoint is located above the centre of the TLOF.

runwayPoint.d: The DesignatedPoint is over a centreline point.

Note: for points located on the border between two countries, the ICAO Country Code of the State having formally registered the five-letter code in the ICAO ICARD system is expected to used.

OrganisationAuthority.d: A group of people, businesses, administrative concerns, or other entities that are systematically structured and managed to meet a need or to pursue collective goals on a continuing basis. This group has the ability to delegate roles, responsibilities, and authority over cognizant areas. For example: ATS Organisations, Aircraft Operating Agencies, States, Groups of States, companies, government entities, etc.

name.d: The full official name of the State, Organisation, Authority, aircraft operating agency, handling agency, etc.

type.d: An indicator of the nature of an authority in terms of its status or business role in air traffic management. For example: State, group of States, organisation within a State, aircraft operating agency, etc.

contact.d: Identifies the contact for the Organisation.

relatedOrganisationAuthority.d: The related organisation, authority or agency.

name.d: The full textual name of a unit. This name must be established according to the rules specified by International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO), and specifically in the official language of the country, transposed into the Latin Alphabet where necessary.

type.d: An indicator of the type of Unit, usually related to the standard type of services provided by it. For example: area control centre, advisory centre, aeronautical information services office.

compliantICAO.d: An indicator that the Unit is setup according to the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) Standards and Recommended Practices (SARPS).

designator.d: A distinguishing label, term, abbreviation or acronym used to identify, or associated with, the Unit. For example, the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) Location Indicator of an Area Control Centre (ACC), as listed in ICAO DOC 7910.

military.d: An indicator of the operational nature of the Unit. For example: civil, military or joint operational nature.

position.d: Identifies the geographical point of the Unit.

airportLocation.d: Identifies the Airport of Heliport where the Unit is located.

ownerOrganisation.d: Identifies the Organisation that supervises the Unit.

contact.d: Contact details for the unit (phone, postal address, e-mail, etc.)

availability.d: The operational status of the Unit.

obstructionIdSurfaceCondition.d: Obstruction identification surface that obstructing area represents

reference_ownerRunwayDirection.d: Identifies the feature for which the Obstacle Area has been defined.

type.d: An indication of the type of vertical structure, such as building, tower, cable, etc.

lighted.d: A simple indication that the vertical surface is lighted, when no further details are available.

markingICAOStandard.d: An indication that vertical structure markings comply with the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) standard, as described in Annex 14.

group.d: An indication that the vertical structure consists of a number of closely situated similar objects.

length.d: The overall length of the vertical structure.

width.d: The overall width of the obstruction.

radius.d: The overall length of the radius of an obstacle that has a relatively circular shape

lightingICAOStandard.d: An indication that the lighting of a vertical structure used as criteria the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) standard as described in Annex 14.

synchronisedLighting.d: An Indication that the flashing light elements that compose the lighting of the vertical structure (could be a group) are synchronised (flash in unison).

marker.d: Identifies the Marker Beacon associated to the Vertical Structure.

part.d: Identifies a part(s) that makes up the Vertical Structure.

hostedPassengerService.d: Identifies the passenger service hosted by the vertical structure.

supportedGroundLight.d: Identifies the ground light system supported by the vertical structure.

hostedNavaidEquipment.d: Identifies the Navigation Aid Equipment hosted by the Vertical Structure.

hostedSpecialNavStation.d: Identifies the Special Navigation Station hosted by the vertical structure.

hostedUnit.d: Identifies the unit hosted by the vertical structure.

hostedOrganisation.d: Identifies the OrganisationAuthority hosted by the vertical structure.

supportedService.d: Identifies the service supported by the vertical structure.

marked.d: A simple indication that the vertical structure is marked, when no further details are available.

placeName.d: A description of the geographical location where the vertical structure is situated.

dataAssessmentStatus.d: An indication if the data provided for the feature was not subject to the regular data quality assurance process.

arrestingDevice.d: The VerticalStructure is an arresting device.

approach.d: Circling is used on approach procedure to safely provide visual guidance to other runways.

multipleIdentification.d: One character code for multiple approaches of the same approach type; Z-A

minimumBaroVnavTemperature.d: [FAA-H-8261-1] The temperature at which a Baro-VNAV is noted NA. It is the minimum temperature limitation published for each procedure for which Baro-VNAV minimums are published. This temperature represents the airport temperature below which the use of Baro-VNAV is not authorized to the LNAV/VNAV DA. For example, the note Baro-VNAV NA below -20 deg. C (-5 deg. F) implies that the approach may not be flown at all using Baro-VNAV when the temperature is below -20 deg. Celsius. However, Baro-VNAV may be used for approach guidance down to the published LNAV MDA. Note: Used in the LNAV final segment.

rnpDMEAuthorized.d: Applies to RNAVguidance. Indicates if DME/DME RNP 0.3 is allowed. Specific DME facilities may be required, for example, "DME/DME RNP-0.3 Authorized, ABC, XYZ required." Note: Used on RNAV final segment.

courseOffsetSide.d: Final Approach Course Offset Side. Indicates on which side of the extended runway centreline that the final approach course lies, when viewed from the Final Approach Fix.

courseCentrelineDistance.d: Final Approach Course Centre Line Distance. Indicates the distance from the Landing Threshold Point (LTP) to the point where the extended runway centreline intersects the final approach course.

courseOffsetDistance.d: Final Approach Course Offset Distance. Indicates the distance between the final approach course and extended runway centreline at a point located 3000 ft from the Landing Threshold Point (LTP), measured perpendicular to the extended runway centreline

courseCentrelineIntersect.d: Indicates if the intersection of the final approach course with the extended runway centreline is located before or after the Landing Threshold Point (LTP).
