arcCentre.d: An segment known as an Arc can be defined as a radius and distance around a center point.

angle.d: The angle defined to limit aircraft trajectory.

distance.d: The distance defined to limit aircraft trajectory.

aircraftCategory.d: Classification of aircraft based on 1.3 times stall speed in landing configuration at maximum certified landing mass.

holding.d: Established holding used on a procedure.

designSurface.d: An evaluation area used when designing a procedure segment to insure safety of aircraft

approach.d: Approaches have defined segments (Initial, Intermediate, etc.) that can have stepdown legs.

requiredNavigationPerformance.d: [ICAO] Required navigation performance (RNP). [ICAO] Specifies the minimum navigation performance accuracy required in an airspace. It is the navigation performance accuracy of all the user and navigation system combinations within an airspace. Note: It is a tolerance factor for flying. The factor is taken into consideration when determining protected airspace for aircraft.

upperLimit.d: The upper limit of a procedure altitude/height as defined by ICAO PANS-OPS: “A published altitude/height used in defining the vertical profile of a flight procedure, at or above the minimum obstacle clearance altitude/height where established.” Note: May also be a flight level.

lowerLimit.d: The lower limit of a procedure altitude/height as defined by ICAO PANS-OPS: “A published altitude/height used in defining the vertical profile of a flight procedure, at or above the minimum obstacle clearance altitude/height where established.” Note: May also be a flight level.

verticalLimitsInterpretation.d: A code indicating how the vertical limit attributes of a procedure leg should be interpreted.

additionalEquipment.d: A ground service or equipment either required or that can be used as an alternative to an on-board navigation capability in order to fly the procedure leg.

minimumObstacleClearanceAltitude.d: (MOCA) The minimum altitude for the segment that provides the required obstacle clearance.

minimumObstacleClearanceHeight.d: The minimum height for the segment that provides the required obstacle clearance.

aircraftCapability.d: A segment leg can be established for specific aircraft characteristics.

altitudeCondition.d: An altitude condition associated with the segment leg or its end point.

limitingDistance.d: Aircraft trajectory must not cross this distance indication.

limitingAngle.d: Aircraft trajectory must not cross the angle indication.

MissedApproachLeg.d: A type of SegmentLeg designed in accordance with the rules for missed approach segments having the properties specific to a missed approach segment.. The missed approach segment begins at DA and ends at the clearance limit.

endConditionDesignator.d: An indication of the event that allows identifying the end of the leg and the start of the next leg on the procedure. For example, reaching an altitude or outbound timing.

legPath.d: A code defining a specific type of flight path such as arc, base turn outbound, base turn inbound, track, proc turn, hold in lieu.

legTypeARINC.d: A comprehensive description of the 'path and terminator' concept is given in ARINC Specification 424, Attachment 5, Path and Terminator.

course.d: The value of the course angle in degrees.

courseType.d: A code indicating the type of course to be observed. E.g. true track, magnetic track, heading, VOR radial, true bearing, magnetic bearing.

courseDirection.d: Indicates flight direction to/from the navaid providing the course guidance.

turnDirection.d: A code indicating the direction of the turn.

speedLimit.d: The value of the speed limit on the procedure leg.

speedReference.d: A code indicating the reference system for a speed value.

speedInterpretation.d: A code indicating how the speed attributes of a procedure leg should be interpreted.

bankAngle.d: The recommended bank angle of the aircraft on the turn.

length.d: Length of the segment

procedureTurnRequired.d: Indicates if a procedure turn is required at the end of the segmentleg. Default is No.

upperLimitAltitude.d: The value of the upper altitude used with codeDescrDistVer: At or below the higher altitude. Between the lower and the upper altitude.

upperLimitReference.d: A code indicating the reference for the upper limit of a procedure altitude/height.

lowerLimitAltitude.d: The lower limit altitude. used with codeDescrDistVer: At or above the lower altitude. At the lower altitude Between the lower and the upper altitude. Lower altitude is recommended. Expect lower altitude by ATC.

lowerLimitReference.d: A code indicating the reference for the lower limit of a procedure altitude/height.

altitudeInterpretation.d: A code indicating how the altitude attributes of a procedure leg should be interpreted.

altitudeOverrideATC.d: Alternate lowerLimit (depending on the value of the verticalLimitsInterpretation) which has to be authorised by Air Traffic Control.

altitudeOverrideReference.d: A code indicating the reference for the alternate altitude of a procedure altitude/height.

verticalAngle.d: The value of the vertical climb angle of the aircraft on the procedure leg. A negative value means descent.

startPoint.d: determines the starting point of the segment

endPoint.d: determines the ending point of the segment

trajectory.d: Segment Leg is depicted by the trajectory

arcCentre.d: An segment known as an Arc can be defined as a radius and distance around a center point.

angle.d: The angle defined to limit aircraft trajectory.

distance.d: The distance defined to limit aircraft trajectory.

aircraftCategory.d: Classification of aircraft based on 1.3 times stall speed in landing configuration at maximum certified landing mass.

holding.d: Established holding used on a procedure.

designSurface.d: An evaluation area used when designing a procedure segment to insure safety of aircraft

approach.d: Approaches have defined segments (Initial, Intermediate, etc.) that can have stepdown legs.

type.d: The types of missed approach.

thresholdAfterMAPT.d: Indicates if MAP is before or after the Threshold

heightMAPT.d: Elevation of the missed approach surface at the missed approach point.

requiredNavigationPerformance.d: [ICAO] Required navigation performance (RNP). [ICAO] Specifies the minimum navigation performance accuracy required in an airspace. It is the navigation performance accuracy of all the user and navigation system combinations within an airspace. Note: It is a tolerance factor for flying. The factor is taken into consideration when determining protected airspace for aircraft.

condition.d: A particular set of final approach conditions that must be met for the assessed missed approach

upperLimit.d: The upper limit of a procedure altitude/height as defined by ICAO PANS-OPS: “A published altitude/height used in defining the vertical profile of a flight procedure, at or above the minimum obstacle clearance altitude/height where established.” Note: May also be a flight level.

lowerLimit.d: The lower limit of a procedure altitude/height as defined by ICAO PANS-OPS: “A published altitude/height used in defining the vertical profile of a flight procedure, at or above the minimum obstacle clearance altitude/height where established.” Note: May also be a flight level.

verticalLimitsInterpretation.d: A code indicating how the vertical limit attributes of a procedure leg should be interpreted.

additionalEquipment.d: A ground service or equipment either required or that can be used as an alternative to an on-board navigation capability in order to fly the procedure leg.

minimumObstacleClearanceAltitude.d: (MOCA) The minimum altitude for the segment that provides the required obstacle clearance.

minimumObstacleClearanceHeight.d: The minimum height for the segment that provides the required obstacle clearance.

aircraftCapability.d: A segment leg can be established for specific aircraft characteristics.

altitudeCondition.d: An altitude condition associated with the segment leg or its end point.

limitingDistance.d: Aircraft trajectory must not cross this distance indication.

limitingAngle.d: Aircraft trajectory must not cross the angle indication.

ProcedureDME.d: DME facilities that are used for a particular segments for DME/DME navigation.

criticalDME.d: An indication that the DME is critical for navigation on a procedure segment.

satisfactory.d: Specifies whether the critical DME passed satisfactory or unsatisfactory.

DME.d: Identifies the DME used for a procedure.

segmentLeg.d: Identifies the Segment Leg used for evaluating the Distance Measuring Equipment

SafeAltitudeArea.d: A set of Minimum Sector Altitudes which completely describe an area centred on a significant point, usually contained within a sector of 46km (25NM) radius.

safeAreaType.d: Indicates the type of area, either MSA or ESA

centrePoint_fixDesignatedPoint.d: A selected point that may have references (distance and/or angle indications)

centrePoint_navaidSystem.d: A navaid used as significant point.

centrePoint_aimingPoint.d: The point at the centre of the TLOF.

centrePoint_runwayPoint.d: A designated point on the runway centreline.

centrePoint_airportReferencePoint.d: the point designated as the center of the airport.

centrePoint_position.d: An unnamed point designated only with a latitude/longitude.

sector.d: A subdivision of the Safe Altitude Area designed to provide the lowest altitude possible and maintain safety.

location.d: Indicates the localisation of the safe altitudes area at a specific airport

HoldingPattern.d: A predetermined manoeuvre which keeps an aircraft within a specified airspace while awaiting further clearance.

type.d: An indicator of the type of holding procedure (e.g., en-route holding, terminal area holding).

outboundCourse.d: Information about the HoldingPattern outbound course.

outboundCourseType.d: The type of course to be observed. E.g. true track, magnetic track, heading, VOR radial, true bearing, magnetic bearing

inboundCourse.d: Information about the HoldingPattern inbound course.

turnDirection.d: An indicator of the turn direction (such as left, right or either) in an aerial manoeuvre performed by aircraft during holding operations.

upperLimit.d: The maximum vertical distance (measured from a specified reference) allowed for all aircraft categories, at all defined speeds, operating in a holding pattern.

upperLimitReference.d: The reference surface (Mean Sea Level, Ground, standard pressure, etc.) used for determining the value of the upper limit of a holding pattern.

lowerLimit.d: The minimum vertical distance (measured from a specified reference) allowed for all aircraft categories, at all defined speeds, operating in a holding pattern.

lowerLimitReference.d: The reference surface (Mean Sea Level, Ground, standard pressure, etc.) used for determining the value of the lower limit of a holding pattern.

speedLimit.d: Restricted speed for containment in a smaller pattern during holding operations.

instruction.d: Operational instructions that must be observed when flying the holding pattern.

nonStandardHolding.d: An indication that the holding pattern is non-standard (for example, because it uses left-hand turns).

outboundLegSpan_endTime.d: Span of the holding pattern as duration, length, or outbound to a significant point.

outboundLegSpan_endDistance.d: Span of the holding pattern as duration, length, or outbound to a significant point.

outboundLegSpan_endPoint.d: Span of the holding pattern as duration, length, or outbound to a significant point.

extent.d: A race track pattern depicts a holding pattern.

designCriteria.d: Standard applied in the design of the holding pattern.

UnplannedHolding.d: Holding requested at an en route fix on airway or route radials, bearings, or courses.

unplannedHolding.d: Indicates if the holding pattern is used as an unplanned holding. Note: Enroute use only.

authorizedAltitude.d: value of the altitude approved based on unplanned holding assessment.

altitudeReference.d: A code indicating the vertical reference system for the authorised altitude.

controlledAirspace.d: Indicates unplanned holding is completely contained within controlled airspace.

holdingPoint.d: Identifies the point used to clear safe holding.

AirspaceBorderCrossing.d: A type of traffic flow condition element which consist of crossing the common border between two adjacent airspace, when flying directly from one airspace into the other airspace.

exitedAirspace.d: The airspace the aircraft crosses from

FlightRestriction.d: A rule meant to regulate the use of the route network, by identifying a set of flights which fulfil a combination of elementary flow conditions and either forbidding them on a particular routing or obliging them to follow one routing out of a set of mandatory alternatives.

designator.d: A coded value which identifies the restriction.

type.d: A code indicating if the restriction is an interdiction or a mandatory routing.

instruction.d: Some free text to describe the operational instructions which form the FlightRestriction.

flight.d: The Flight affected by the Flight Restriction.

regulatedRoute.d: The Route regulated by the Flight Restriction.

RouteSegment.d: A portion of a route to be flown usually without an intermediate stop, as defined by two consecutive significant points.

level.d: A code indicating if the route segment is in the upper airspace, the lower airspace or both.

upperLimit.d: The vertical position of the route segment ceiling.

upperLimitReference.d: The reference surface used for the value of the upper limit. For example, Mean Sea Level, Ground, standard pressure, etc..

lowerLimit.d: The vertical position of the route segment floor.

lowerLimitReference.d: The reference surface used for the value of the lower limit. For example, Mean Sea Level, Ground, standard pressure, etc..

minimumObstacleClearanceAltitude.d: Minimum obstacle clearance altitude (MOCA). The minimum altitude for a defined segment of flight that provides the required obstacle clearance.

pathType.d: The type of segment path. For example, great circle, rhumbline, geodesic line, etc.

length.d: The length of the path (depending on the type of the path).

widthLeft.d: The distance from the centreline of the route segment to the left edge, when considering the direction from the start point to the end point.

widthRight.d: The distance from the centreline of the route segment to the right edge, when considering the direction from the start point to the end point.

turnDirection.d: Indicates the turn direction (if any) at the end of the current segment, in order to continue on to the next segment of the same route.

signalGap.d: indicates a signal gap in the segment

minimumEnrouteAltitude.d: The lowest published altitude for an en-route segment that provides adequate reception of relevant navigation facilities and ATS communications, complies with the airspace structure and provides the required obstacle clearance.

minimumCrossingAtEnd.d: The lowermost vertical position at the end point, when flying on the route portion in the direction indicated in the RoutePortionUsage.

minimumCrossingAtEndReference.d: The reference surface used for the value of the minimumCrossingAtEnd. For example, Mean Sea Level, Ground, standard pressure, etc..

maximumCrossingAtEnd.d: The uppermost vertical position at the end point, when flying on the route portion in the direction indicated in the RoutePortionUsage.

maximumCrossingAtEndReference.d: The reference surface used for the value of the maximumCrossingAtEnd. For example, Mean Sea Level, Ground, standard pressure, etc..

navigationType.d: Classification of the Route Portion for navigational purposes. Examples: conventional, RNAV.

requiredNavigationPerformance.d: A code indicating the required navigation performance for the route portion

designatorSuffix.d: A suffix for the route designator (according ICAO Annex 11), indicating whether advisory service only is available on that portion, or the RNP status of the route portion.

start.d: The start EnRouteSegmentPoint for the Route Segment

routeFormed.d: The route formed by the Route Segments.

evaluationArea.d: The obstacle evaluation area for the route segment.

curveExtent.d: The extent of the route segment.

end.d: The end EnRouteSegmentPoint for the Route Segment

availability.d: The operational availability of the RouteSegment.

cardinalDirectionLeft.d: The cardinal direction left side in relation to the route segment when considering the direction from the start point to the end point.

cardinalDirectionRight.d: The cardinal direction right side in relation to the route segment when considering the direction from the start point to the end point.

aircraftCapability.d: A combination of aircraft characteristics, equipment and capabilities that are required on the Route Segment.

airspaceClass.d: Information about the airspace classification on the route segment.

RouteDME.d: DME facilities that are used for a particular route for DME/DME navigation.

criticalDME.d: An indication that the DME is critical for navigation on the route portion.

satisfactory.d: Specifies whether the critical DME passed satisfactory or unsatisfactory.

referencedDME.d: The DME referenced on the Route.

applicableRoutePortion.d: The route portion that the routeDME applies to.

Route.d: A specified route designed for channelling the flow of traffic as necessary for the provision of air traffic services, from the end of the take-off and initial climb phase to the commencement of the approach and landing phase.

designatorPrefix.d: A prefix for the route designator, indicating whether the route is upper ATS, reserved for helicopters or reserved for supersonic flights.

designatorSecondLetter.d: The letter of the route designator. Depending on the region, letters may have special significance with regard to the route usage limitations.

designatorNumber.d: The number of the route designator.

multipleIdentifier.d: A suffix for the route designator, indicating alternates for homonymous routes (especially for military training routes).

locationDesignator.d: A textual description of the area in which a designated route is situated.

name.d: A free text name by which the route is known.

type.d: Route classification.

flightRule.d: A code indicating the flight rules to be observed by aircraft. For example, VFR and/or IFR.

internationalUse.d: A code indicating if the route segment is international or domestic.

militaryUse.d: A code indicating whether the route is for exclusive use by military aircraft.

militaryTrainingType.d: A code indicating the type of military training activity for which the route has been designed.

userOrganisation.d: Indicates the Organisation normally originating activity on a military training route.

designCriteria.d: Standard applied in the design of the route.

availability.d: The operational availability of the Route.

aircraftCapability.d: A combination of aircraft characteristics, equipment and capabilities that ensure Route classification/

ChangeOverPoint.d: The distance from the start of the route portion to the position where change over occurs for VOR defined routes.

distance.d: The distance from the start of the route portion to position of the change over point.

location_fixDesignatedPoint.d: A selected point that may have references (distance and/or angle indications)

location_navaidSystem.d: A navaid used as significant point.

location_aimingPoint.d: The point at the centre of the TLOF.

location_runwayPoint.d: A designated point on the runway centreline.

location_airportReferencePoint.d: the point designated as the center of the airport.

location_position.d: An unnamed point designated only with a latitude/longitude.

applicableRoutePortion.d: The Route Portion that the change over point applies to.

AerialRefuelling.d: A procedure used by the military to transfer fuel from one aircraft to another during flight.

designatorPrefix.d: An affix placed before a route designator used to identify an aerial refuelling route.

designatorNumber.d: A designator that identifies the aerial refuelling route.

designatorSuffix.d: An affix placed after a route designator used to qualify an aerial refuelling route.

designatorDirection.d: An indicator of the general cardinal direction of the aerial refuelling procedure

name.d: An identifier by which the aerial refuelling route is known.

type.d: The type of aerial refuelling procedure based on its configuration.

radarBeaconSetting.d: The setting to be used by the airborne navigation radar beacon during aerial refuel operations.

xbandRadarSetting.d: The setting to be used by the Airborne Identification Radar beacon during aerial refuel operations.

tankerChannel.d: The Tactical Air Navigation System (TACAN) UHF channel assigned to the tanker aircraft to provide omnidirectional course and distance navigational information during air refuelling operations.

receiverChannel.d: The Tactical Air Navigation System (TACAN) UHF channel assigned to an aircraft receiving fuel to provide omnidirectional course and distance navigational information during air refuelling operations.

helicopterRoute.d: An indication that the aerial refuelling procedure is designed only for helicopter usage.

specialRefuelling.d: An indication that the aerial refuelling procedure supports special missions/sortie.

bidirectionalUse.d: An indication that the aerial refuel track supports simultaneous opposite direction aerial refuelling

reverseDirectionTurn.d: An indicator of the turn direction in an aerial manoeuvre (referred to as the Direction of Course Reversal Turn) performed by aircraft during aerial refuelling, where it can reverse its direction of course by turning around either right or left. It only applies to bi-directional routes

availability.d: The operational availability of the AerialRefuelling.

protectingAirspace.d: Indicates either the airspace that protects or airspace that are crossed by the Aerial Refuelling procedure.

track.d: AerialRefuellingLeg may be either an anchor or a track. In either case, the points that make up an anchor or track are defined in the AerialRefuellingPoint. The Anchor class provides additional anchoring data related to only AR anchors. The geometry of a track is represented by the Curve object and geometryof an anchor is represented by Surface object.

anchor.d: The definition of the AerialRefuelling anchor.

managingOrganisation.d: The OrganisationAuthority that manages the AerialRefuelling.

RulesProcedures.d: The definition of an instruction or regulation that needs to be considered by personnel involved in flight operations in relation with an airport/heliport or an airspace.

category.d: An indication of the purpose of the rule or procedure

title.d: A general heading by which the rule or procedure is usually identified in the Aeronautical Information Publications (AIP) or similar/related documents.

content.d: The definition of the actual content of the rule or procedure

affectedLocation.d: Airport/Heliport where the rule or procedure is effective.

affectedArea.d: Airspace within which the rule or procedure is applicable.

WaterBody.d: Water body close to the aerodrome movement area.

extent.d: Extent of the water body.

location.d: The AirportHeliport and its movement area that is situated close to the water body.

WeatherSource.d: Information about a weather sensor or a device that can be used to asses meteorological conditions at its location and that is used to provide information to aviation users.

designator.d: A name or a code that can be used to identify the weather source.

sensorType.d: The type of data that the sensor provides.

position.d: The geographical position of the resource.

availability.d: Information about the operational status of the resource.

RunwayVisualRangeEquipment.d: A meteorological equipment providing information about the distance over which the pilot of an aircraft on the centre line of a runway can see the runway surface markings or the lights delineating the runway or identifying its centre line.

readingPosition.d: The position along the runway direction for which the Runway Visual Range (RVR) reading is provided.

location.d: Location of the Runway Visual Range.

Gangway.d: A movable walkway where people board and disembark such as platforms, and piers. Gangways shall be painted red or signage provided indicating seaplane access only.

width.d: The physical width of the Gangway.

length.d: The physical length of the Gangway.

type.d: The type of gangway assigned to a seaplane landing area.

mobility.d: Defines whether a Gangway is mobile or stationary.

AirportSign.d: Refers to a complete assembly that includes the sign housing, the retro reflective panel, the legend, the associated electrical components, and the sign mounting components.

type.d: Specifies the applicability of the associated sign.

frontMessageText.d: The text and graphics appearing in the front inscription of the sign.

backMessageText.d: The text and graphics appearing in the back inscription of the sign.

frontSignBearing.d: The bearing from true north which the front message side of the sign faces.

height.d: Maximum height of top of vertical structure.

lighted.d: A simple indication that an airport sign is lighted.

direction.d: The arrow direction that points to the warning area.

side.d: Sign location from users’ perspective (indicates left side or right side of runway).

location.d: Location of the component.

signStatus.d: Information about the operational status of an airport sign.

associatedAirport.d: The airport associated with Airport signs.

AltimeterCheckpoint.d: A point established to test the altimeter readings in the aircraft.

category.d: Indicates the position of the checkpoint; airborne or ground

upperLimit.d: Indicating the upper limit of the block in which the check should be conducted.

upperLimitReference.d: A code indicating the reference for a vertical distance. Two series of values exist: 1) real distance: from GND, from the MSL, from the WGS-84 ellipsoid 2) pressure distance: QFE, QNH, STD.

lowerLimit.d: Indicating the lower limit of the block in which the check should be conducted.

lowerLimitReference.d: A code indicating the reference for a vertical distance. Two series of values exist: 1) real distance: from GND, from the MSL, from the WGS-84 ellipsoid 2) pressure distance: QFE, QNH, STD.

altitudeInterpretation.d: Indicates how the upper and/or lower altitude values should be interpreted.

distance.d: The value of the distance from the checkpoint to the navaid.

angle.d: The indication of a bearing (at a given point) by the measurement of the angle between the checkpoint and the navaid equipment (VOR)

position.d: Identifies the point of he checkpoint.

airportHeliport.d: Identifies the airport for which the checkpoint is established.

locationOnRunway.d: The altimeter checkpoint latitude and longitude coordinates, which are the same as for the runway threshold (runway centreline point).

locationOnApron.d: The altimeter checkpoint latitude and longitude coordinates, which are the same as for the Apron position.

locationOnStand.d: The altimeter checkpoint latitude and longitude coordinates, which are the same as for the aircraft parking stand position.

GBAS.d: Ground-based augmentation system (GBAS). An augmentation system in which the user receives augmentation information directly from a ground-based transmitter.

designator.d: A coded designator, usually an ICAO location indicator, that identifies the GBAS station.

name.d: The name by which the GBAS system or its location is known.

maximumUseDistance.d: (Dmax) The maximum distance (slant range) from the GBAS reference point within which pseudo-range corrections are applied by the aircraft element.

flightChecked.d: An indication whether the system was flight checked.

operator.d: The entity operating the GBAS facility.

augmentedSystem.d: The core GNSS system or SBAS for which the augmented information is provided.

antenna.d: Information about the GBAS transmitting antenna.

availability.d: The availability of the GBAS.

referencePoint.d: The reference geographical location of the GBAS system.

servedAirport.d: An airport/heliport at which the GBAS service is provided.

GBASService.d: An operation supported by the GBAS facility within the GBAS coverage area.

name.d: The name by which the GBAS Service or its location is known.

approachServiceType.d: GBAS approach service type (GAST). Designates the GBAS service types (A-D) that are supported for the approach by the ground subsystem.

positioningService.d: An indication that positioning service is provided within the GBAS Service.

channelRSDS.d: The GBAS channel identifier for the positioning service (using the Reference Station Data Selector - RSDS), if provided.

regionalService.d: An indication that the service is provided as a ground-based regional augmentation system (GRAS).

approachServicePoint.d: Indicates a service volume by means of named location along the nominal approach and/or along the runway for which GBAS performance for the supported service type(s) has been verified.

minimumDecisionHeight.d: Indicates a service volume by means of a numerical value in feet corresponding to the minimum decision height.

augmentationSystem.d: The GBAS station that provides the service.

flightInspectionArc.d: An arc of circle at a predefined distance and altitude from the GBAS reference point used for flight inspection.

availability.d: The availability of the GBAS service.

area.d: The geographical extent of the GBAS service area on the surface of the Earth.

centrePoint.d: The centre of the sectors of circle associated with the RadioFrequencyArea, when different from the location of the equipment for which the area is defined.

servedApproach.d: The runway landing direction(s) for which the service is provided with the indicated service level.

SatelliteService.d: The definition of a satellite navigation service type and of the locations where it is approved for operations.

serviceType.d: A type of aircraft operation (such as en-route navigation, initial approach, APV-I, etc.) supported by the satellite service in a specified service area.

satelliteSystem.d: The satellite constellation for which the service is specified.

serviceArea.d: The geographical area where the satellite service is available and authorised for use.

approachLocation.d: The airport/heliport where the satellite service is used for approaches.

SatelliteSystem.d: A satellite constellation that provides a worldwide position and time determination system and/or augmentation information for a wide coverage area.

type.d: Indicates the type of the service, allowing to distinguish between core GNSS systems and wide area augmentation systems.

name.d: The official name of the satellite constellation.

designator.d: An acronym by which the system is known to the public.

augmentedSystem.d: The GNSS system for which the augmented information is provided.

operator.d: The entity operating the satellite constellation.

emission.d: A radio communication frequency on which the satellite signal is provided.

MinimumAltitudeArea.d: A specified area within which a set of minimum altitudes is prescribed for specific flight operations, such as instrument approach, radar vectoring, enroute navigation, etc.

type.d: The type of flight operations to which the minimum altitude specified for the area is applicable.

lowestTemperature.d: The seasonal or annual minimum temperature considered for altitude correction at cold temperatures, if applicable.

designCriteria.d: Standard applied in the design of the safe altitude area.

sector.d: Safe Altitude area may be subdivided into sectors.

centrePoint_fixDesignatedPoint.d: Safe Altitude Area references a significant point as its base.

centrePoint_navaidSystem.d: Safe Altitude Area references a significant point as its base.

centrePoint_position.d: Safe Altitude Area references a significant point as its base.

centrePoint_runwayPoint.d: Safe Altitude Area references a significant point as its base.

centrePoint_aimingPoint.d: Safe Altitude Area references a significant point as its base.

centrePoint_airportReferencePoint.d: Safe Altitude Area references a significant point as its base.

concernedAirspace.d: The ATS airspace within which the flight operations associated with the minimum altitude take place.

location.d: Indicates the localisation of the safe altitudes area at a specific airport

AirTrafficFlowManagementService.d: A kind of service that provides flight planning and flow management operations.

flightOperations.d: The destination (arriving, departing, etc.) of the flights for which the information is provided.

rank.d: The order of priority of the service, such as "primary" or "alternate".

compliantICAO.d: A code indicating whether the service is compliant with the ICAO standards and recommended practices specified for this type of service.

name.d: A free text name by which the service is identified.

location.d: The location from where the service is provided.

serviceProvider.d: Identifies the Unit for which Services are provided.

call-sign.d: In aeronautical radio communication the Unit providing a Service is identified by its CALL SIGN.

radioCommunication.d: The radio frequency on which the service is provided.

groundCommunication.d: The point of contact on the ground for the service.

availability.d: The operational status of the Service.

type.d: The type of air traffic flow management service provided.

clientSegment.d: The route segment for which the flight planning and air traffic flow management services is provided.

clientRoute.d: The route protion for which the flight ploanning and air traffic flow management services is provided.

clientAirspace.d: The Airspace for which the flight planning and air traffic management service is provided.

clientAirportHeliport.d: The AirportHeliport for which the air traffic management service is provided.

clientAerialRefuelling.d: The Aerial Refuelling for which the scheduling service is provided.

NavaidEquipmentDistance.d: Captures the distances between various Runway Centreline Points and Navaid Equipment.

distance.d: The measured or calculated distance between a Runway Centreline Point and a Navaid Equipment.

operation.d: An indicator of how the component participates in the aggregation, such as addition, subtraction or intersection.

operationSequence.d: An indicator of the order of the component in an aggregation.

theAirspaceVolume.d: An portion of airspace that contributes to the defintion of an Airspace geometry.

AirspaceVolume.d: A defined volume in the air, described as horizontal projection with vertical limits.

upperLimit.d: The vertical distance of the upper bound (ceiling) of an airspace volume. The vertical distance is measured relative to a separately specified upper limit reference. An airspace volume is a defined volume in air described as horizontal projection with vertical limits.

upperLimitReference.d: The reference surface (Mean Sea Level, Ground, standard pressure, etc.) used for the value of the upper limit of an airspace volume. Where airspace volume is a defined volume in air described as horizontal projection with vertical limits.

maximumLimit.d: The vertical distance of the maximum limit of an airspace volume. The vertical distance is measured relative to a separately specified maximum limit reference. An airspace volume is a defined volume in air described as horizontal projection with vertical limits. The maximum limit overrides the upper limit, in those parts of the airspace where the upper limit is situated below the maximum limit.

maximumLimitReference.d: The reference surface (Mean Sea Level, Ground, standard pressure, etc.) used for determining the value of the maximum limit of an airspace volume. Where airspace volume is a defined volume in air described as horizontal projection with vertical limits.

lowerLimit.d: The vertical distance of the lower bound (floor) of an airspace volume. The vertical distance is measured relative to a separately specified lower limit reference. An airspace volume is a defined volume in air described as horizontal projection with vertical limits.

lowerLimitReference.d: The reference surface (Mean Sea Level, Ground, standard pressure, etc.) used for determining the value of the lower limit of an airspace volume. Where airspace volume is a defined volume in air described as horizontal projection with vertical limits.

minimumLimit.d: The vertical distance of the minimum limit of an airspace volume. The vertical distance is measured relative to a separately specified minimum limit reference. An airspace volume is a defined volume in air described as horizontal projection with vertical limits. The minimum limit overrides the lower limit, in those parts of the airspace where the lower limit is situated below the minimum limit.

minimumLimitReference.d: The reference surface (Mean Sea Level, Ground, standard pressure, etc.) used for the value of the minimum limit of an airspace volume. Where airspace volume is a defined volume in air described as horizontal projection with vertical limits.

width.d: The width of the corridor, in case the AirspaceVolume has been originally defined as having a corridor shape.

horizontalProjection.d: The surface defining the horizontal shape of the AirspaceVolume.

centreline.d: The line passing through the centre of an airspace volume having a corridor shape.

contributorAirspace.d: A (parent) Airspace, whose geometry has an impact on the geometry of the AirspaceVolume.

name.d: The free text identifier or name of the the airspace volume.

location.d: A single position used as geographical reference for the AirspaceVolume, in particular when a precise horizontalProjection is not provided.

associatedLevels.d: The airspace layer associated with the airspace class.

dependency.d: An indicator of the type of dependency between the geometry of the AirspaceVolume and the geometry of the contributor Airspace.

theAirspace.d: A (parent) Airspace, whose geometry has an impact on the geometry of the AirspaceVolume.

Curve.d: A one-dimensional geometric primitive, representing the continuous image of a line.

horizontalAccuracy.d: The difference between the recorded horizontal coordinates of a curve and its true position referenced to the same geodetic datum expressed as a circular error corresponding to the confidence level specified in the ICAO PANS-AIM (DOC 10066) for the specific subject/property.

ElevatedCurve.d: A one-dimensional geometric primitive, representing the continuous image of a line which is extended with properties that represent the vertical position (elevation, datum, accuracy).

elevation.d: The vertical distance at the curve level, measured from Mean Sea Level (MSL).

geoidUndulation.d: The distance of the geoid above (positive) or below (negative) the mathematical reference ellipsoid at the location of the curve.

verticalDatum.d: The set of reference points or a mathematical model of the Earth's surface (a datum) against which vertical position measurements of a curve, are made as basis for measuring elevations.

verticalAccuracy.d: The difference between the recorded elevation of a feature and its true elevation referenced to the same vertical datum expressed as a linear error at 95 percent probability.

horizontalAccuracy.d: The difference between the recorded horizontal coordinates of a curve and its true position referenced to the same geodetic datum expressed as a circular error corresponding to the confidence level specified in the ICAO PANS-AIM (DOC 10066) for the specific subject/property.

ElevatedPoint.d: A zero-dimensional object that specifies geometric location which includes elevation and vertical extent and is used in obstacles, navaids, etc.

elevation.d: The vertical distance of the point measured from Mean Sea Level (MSL).

geoidUndulation.d: The distance of the geoid above (positive) or below (negative) the mathematical reference ellipsoid at the location of the point.

verticalDatum.d: The set of reference points or a mathematical model of the Earth's surface (a datum) against which vertical position measurements of a point, are made as basis for measuring elevations.

verticalAccuracy.d: The difference between the recorded elevation of a feature and its true elevation referenced to the same vertical datum expressed as a linear error at 95 percent probability.

horizontalAccuracy.d: The difference between the recorded horizontal coordinates of a point and its true position referenced to the same geodetic datum expressed as a circular error corresponding to the confidence level specified in the ICAO PANS-AIM (DOC 10066) for the specific subject/property.

elevation.d: The vertical distance of the surface level measured from Mean Sea Level (MSL).

geoidUndulation.d: The distance of the geoid above (positive) or below (negative) the mathematical reference ellipsoid at the location of the surface.

verticalDatum.d: The set of reference points or a mathematical model of the Earth's surface (a datum) against which vertical position measurements of a surface, are made as basis for measuring elevations.

verticalAccuracy.d: The difference between the recorded elevation of a feature and its true elevation referenced to the same vertical datum expressed as a linear error at 95 percent probability.

horizontalAccuracy.d: The difference between the recorded horizontal coordinates of a surface and its true position referenced to the same geodetic datum expressed as a circular error corresponding to the confidence level specified in the ICAO PANS-AIM (DOC 10066) for the specific subject/property.

horizontalAccuracy.d: The difference between the recorded horizontal coordinates of a point and its true position referenced to the same geodetic datum expressed as a circular error corresponding to the confidence level specified in the ICAO PANS-AIM (DOC 10066) for the specific subject/property.

Surface.d: A 2-dimensional primitive and is composed of one or more surface patches as specified in ISO 19107:2003, 6.3.17.1. The surface patches are connected to one another.

horizontalAccuracy.d: The difference between the recorded horizontal coordinates of a surface and its true position referenced to the same geodetic datum expressed as a circular error corresponding to the confidence level specified in the ICAO PANS-AIM (DOC 10066) for the specific subject/property.

ObstacleAssessmentArea.d: The geometry of surfaces used to define the altitude the length of a segment, holding pattern, etc., in function of the obstructions located in the area.

type.d: Indicated the type of area being assessed such as 40:1, 72:1, MA, Final, etc

sectionNumber.d: a sequence number indicating a part of an assessment area.

slope.d: The slope value of the extent

assessedAltitude.d: Highest of the minimum altitudes in controlling obstacles plus the altitude adjustments (operational factors)

slopeLowerAltitude.d: The altitude at the bottom of the assessment area

gradientLowHigh.d: Low to high gradient within the airspace

surfaceZone.d: Specifies zones within obstruction identification surfaces (OIS)

safetyRegulation.d: Identifier for the safety regulations in effect within the zone

aircraftCategory.d: Classification of aircraft based on 1.3 times stall speed in landing configuration at maximum certified landing mass.

significantObstacle.d: The obstacle that controls the altitude definition of the assessment area would penetrate the 40:1 OCS

surface.d: The geographical representation of the Assessment Area.

startingCurve.d: The curve that starts the ObstacleAssessmentArea.

Obstruction.d: [FAA 8260.3] The highest airspace, obstacle or terrain relative to a prescribed plane within a specified area. NOTE: In precision approach procedures where obstacles penetrate the approach surface, the controlling obstacle is the one which results in the requirement for the highest decision height (DH).

requiredClearance.d: Required altitude adjustment above any obstacle or terrain within a defined safety buffer region. The safety buffer allows for errors in the air and in the accuracy of data such as obstacle accuracy. This together with other adjustments (human factor adjustments, lighting adjustments, altimeter adjustments, etc). give the minimum altitude.

minimumAltitude.d: The value of the minimum obstacle clearance altitude.

surfacePenetration.d: A code indicating whether the controlling obstacle penetrates the assessment surfaces. Rule: if surfacePenetration is "NO", then slopePenetration will not have a value.

slopePenetration.d: A value calculated by dividing 102.0 (a constant) with the angle of the glidepath

controlling.d: Indication whether it is a "controlling obstruction" for the associated ObstacleAssessmentArea.

closeIn.d: "Close-In Obstacles" are those that would penetrate the 40:1 OCS and would require a climb gradient to 200 feet or less above the departure end of runway. So if an aircraft climbs at the minimum standard 200 feet per NM, "Close-In Obstacles" are those within 1 NM from the end of the runway.

adjustment.d: Operational factors applied to obstacle clearance altitudes to produce the safest usable altitude.

obstaclePlacement.d: location of obstacle in relation to a given point.

AltitudeAdjustment.d: Operational factors applied to obstacle clearance altitudes to produce the safest usable altitude.

altitudeAdjustmentType.d: Ability to adjust the segment altitude

primaryAlternateMinimum.d: Adjustments applicable to either local altimeter or secondary altimeter. Applicable to the final minimums based on altimeter settings. Set to Y if primary altimeter. Not applicable for TAA or MSA.

localRemoteCode.d: Indication if the altitude adjustment is based on a local or a remote altimeter.

ObstaclePlacement.d: Provides the location relative to a given point.

obstacleBearing.d: Used only for MSA/ESA. The bearing from a given point to the obstruction.

obstacleDistance.d: The distance from a given point to the obstruction.

pointType.d: The type of point referenced when determining the bearing and distance to the obstruction. Example MSA/ESA centre point, DER

obstaclePlacement.d: Indicates the obstacle position relative to the centreline

StandardLevel.d: A specified cruising level, part of a column within a table of discrete cruising levels used by General Air Traffic.

verticalDistance.d: The value of the cruising level.

ContactInformation.d: Information required to enable contact with the responsible person and/or organisation.

name.d: The official name of the contact.

title.d: The official title of the contact.

address.d: A postal address for the contact.

networkNode.d: A direct link for the contact, over a data communication network.

phoneFax.d: A phone or fax number for the contact.

OnlineContact.d: On-line or Network information that can be used to contact the individual or organisation, including eMail address and web site page.

specialDateAuthority.d: Indicates that the SpecialDates associated with the related OrganisationAuthority are applicable to the schedule definition.

network.d: The official name of the telecommunication network on which a contact's online resource is located.

linkage.d: A contact's location (address) for on-line access using a Uniform Resource Locator address or similar addressing scheme such as http://www.statkart.no/isotc211 .

protocol.d: The connection protocol to be used for accessing an contact's online resource.

eMail.d: The address of the electronic mailbox of the responsible organisation or individual.

PostalAddress.d: Physical address at which the organization or individual may be contacted.

specialDateAuthority.d: Indicates that the SpecialDates associated with the related OrganisationAuthority are applicable to the schedule definition.

deliveryPoint.d: The street address portion of the physical address for an organisation or individual.

city.d: The city portion of the physical address for an organisation or individual.

administrativeArea.d: The state or province of an organisation's or individual's physical address.

postalCode.d: The ZIP or other postal code portion of the physical address for an organisation or individual.

country.d: The country name portion of the physical address for an organisation or individual.

TelephoneContact.d: Telephone numbers at which the organisation or individual may be contacted.

specialDateAuthority.d: Indicates that the SpecialDates associated with the related OrganisationAuthority are applicable to the schedule definition.

voice.d: The telephone number by which individuals can speak to the responsible organisation or individual.

facsimile.d: The telephone number of a facsimile machine for the responsible organisation or individual.

type.d: The technology that enables the telephone voice communication.

AircraftCharacteristic.d: Classification, properties, and equipment capabilities of aircraft, such as airplane, balloon, helicopter, etc.

type.d: Indicating the type of an aircraft.

engine.d: An indication of the type of aircraft engine.

numberEngine.d: An indication for the number of engines of an aircraft.

typeAircraftICAO.d: A coded aircraft type designator assigned by ICAO to all aircraft heavier than micro-/ultra-light.

aircraftLandingCategory.d: Classification of aircraft based on 1.3 times stall speed in landing configuration at maximum certified landing mass.

wingSpan.d: The distance between the wing tips of the aircraft.

wingSpanInterpretation.d: Indicates whether the Aircraft Characteristic concerns aircraft with larger or smaller wingspan.

classWingSpan.d: A classification of aircraft by wing span dimension. It can be used to indicate the size of aircraft that a taxiway can handle.

weightInterpretation.d: Indicates whether the Aircraft Characteristic concerns aircraft with bigger or smaller weight.

passengers.d: The maximum number of passengers carried on an aircraft.

passengersInterpretation.d: Indicates whether the Aircraft Characteristic concerns aircraft with larger or smaller number of passengers.

speed.d: An Indicated Air Speed (IAS) that can be maintained by the aircraft.

speedInterpretation.d: Indicates whether the Indicated Air Speed that can be maintained by an aircraft is a maximum or minimum imposed value.

wakeTurbulence.d: The wake turbulence category of the aircraft.

navigationEquipment.d: An indication of the aircraft capability to use a certain ground based, satellite based or on-board system for aerial navigation.

navigationSpecification.d: A set of aircraft and flight crew requirements needed to support performance-based navigation operations.

verticalSeparationCapability.d: An indication of the aircraft capability to maintain a specified vertical separation.

antiCollisionAndSeparationEquipment.d: An indication of the aircraft equipment with collision avoidance systems.

communicationEquipment.d: An indication of the aircraft equipment with voice and data communication devices.

surveillanceEquipment.d: An indication of the aircraft capability for operating with a certain surveillance system.

category.d: An indication of the category of aircraft.

navigationType.d: An indication if performance based navigation or conventional navigation is required.

navigationAccuracy.d: The navigation accuracy value associated with the navigation specification.

dualFrequency.d: Simultaneous radio communication capability on two different frequencies, such as dual VHF.

helicopterPerformanceClass.d: A code indicating the performance class of a helicopter.

radioNavigationEquipment.d: Radio navigation equipment available on the aircraft. Note: multiple occurrences in relation with the same AircraftCharacteristics are interpreted with an ‘and’ operator.

FlightCharacteristic.d: A specific flight type, such as Instrument Flight Rules(IFR)/Visual Flight Rules(VFR), national/international, Operational Air Traffic(OAT)/General Air Traffic(GAT), etc.

type.d: An indication of a specified type of a flight, such as Operational Air Traffic(OAT)/General Air Traffic(GAT).

rule.d: An indication a specific flight rule, such as Instrument Flight Rule or Visual Flight Rule.

status.d: The designation of a special status for a flight (e.g., Head of State, State aircraft other than Head of State, etc.)

military.d: An indication of the military and/or civilian status of a flight.

origin.d: An indication of the origin of the flight with regard to the national borders.

purpose.d: An indication of the purpose of the flight.

LightElement.d: An elementary light source, part of a lighting system.

colour.d: An indication of the colour of the lights in a light element group.

intensityLevel.d: An indication of the relative intensity of the lights in a light element group.

intensity.d: The exact value of the intensity of the lights in a light element group.

type.d: An indication of the type of light source.

location.d: Identifies the geospatial location of the Light Element.

availability.d: The operational status of the LightElement.

direction.d: An indication of the light emission direction.

lightingTechnology.d: An indication of the lighting technology used to emit light.

LightElementStatus.d: The description of the operational status of the Light Element.

specialDateAuthority.d: Indicates that the SpecialDates associated with the related OrganisationAuthority are applicable to the schedule definition.

status.d: An indication of the operational status of the light element.

AirspaceLayer.d: The portion of airspace between two specified vertical levels.

upperLimit.d: The vertical distance, measured relative to a separately specified upper limit reference, of the upper bound of an airspace layer or block. Where airspace layer is the portion of airspace between two specified vertical levels.

upperLimitReference.d: The reference surface (Mean Sea Level, Ground, standard pressure, etc.) used for determining the value of the lower limit of an airspace Layer or block. Where airspace layer is the portion of airspace between two specified vertical levels.

lowerLimit.d: The vertical distance, measured relative to a separately specified lower limit reference, of the lower bound of an airspace layer or block. Where airspace layer is the portion of airspace between two specified vertical levels.

lowerLimitReference.d: The reference surface (Mean Sea Level, Ground, standard pressure, etc.) used for determining the value of the lower limit of an airspace Layer or block. Where airspace layer is the portion of airspace between two specified vertical levels.

altitudeInterpretation.d: Indicates how the upper and/or lower altitude values should be interpreted.

discreteLevelSeries.d: Restriction of the AirspaceLayer to a number of standard IFR or VFR levels.

CircleSector.d: A group of properties that help describe a 3D pattern based on start angle, stop angle, inner distance, outer distance and upper/lower altitude.

angleType.d: A code indicating the type of angle: magnetic, bearing, VOR radial.

angleDirectionReference.d: A code indicating a direction with regard to a reference point.

upperLimit.d: The uppermost altitude or level that is included in the sector.

upperLimitReference.d: The reference surface used for the value of the upper limit. For example, Mean Sea Level, Ground, standard pressure, etc..

lowerLimit.d: The lowermost altitude or level that is included in the sector.

lowerLimitReference.d: The reference surface used for the value of the lower limit. For example, Mean Sea Level, Ground, standard pressure, etc.

zeroAxisRotation.d: Rotation of the zero axis from the magnetic of true North, allowing to specify a zero axis that is parallel to a runway centreline.

Timesheet.d: The definition of a single time interval, that occurs repeatedly as part of a schedule.

timeReference.d: An indicator of the time reference system or reference system offset (for example, Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), or UTC minus 7 hours), applied to the time, day and date values specified in the timesheet.

startDate.d: The start date of the validity of a timesheet. Used together with a timesheet's 'EndDate' to express repetitive time periods like 15 May to 15 November.

endDate.d: The end date of the validity of a timesheet. Used together with a timesheet's 'StartDate' to express repetitive time periods like 15 May to 15 November.

day.d: An indicator of the day the timesheet is referring to.

dayTil.d: An indicator of the days affected by a timesheet, as follows: if the value of this attribute is left blank, the 'EndTime', 'EndEvent', 'EndTimeRelativeEvent' and 'endEventInterpretation' values of a timesheet must be considered as occurring on the day specified.

startTime.d: The time of the day (specified in the timesheet's 'day' attribute) when the period described in the timesheet starts.

startEvent.d: A reference to an event (like sunset or sunrise), the occurrence of which indicates when the period described in a timesheet starts.

startTimeRelativeEvent.d: The number of minutes before or after the event referred to by the timesheet's 'StartEvent' when the period described in the timesheet starts.

startEventInterpretation.d: When both the 'StartTime' and 'StartEvent' values of a timesheet are not blank, this explains how the combination of the two values should be interpreted, i.e. which of the two moments in time is the beginning of the period described by the timesheet.

endTime.d: The time of the day when the period described in the timesheet ends.

endEvent.d: A reference to an event (like sunset or sunrise), the occurrence of which indicates when the period described in a timesheet ends.

endTimeRelativeEvent.d: The number of minutes before or after an event, referred to by the timesheet's 'EndEvent', when the period described in the timesheet ends.

endEventInterpretation.d: When both the 'EndTime' and 'EndEvent' values of a timesheet are not blank, this attribute explains how the combination of the two attributes should be interpreted, i.e. which of the two moments in time is the end of the period described by the timesheet.

daylightSavingAdjust.d: Indicates that the 'StartTime' and 'EndTime' values of a timesheet have to be decreased by one hour when Daylight Saving is in force (summer time).

excluded.d: An indicator that the time block indicated by a timesheet is excluded (subtracted) from the total time interval(s) defined by one or more additional timesheet(s).

Meteorology.d: A specific set of meteorological conditions.

flightConditions.d: An overall indication whether the meteorological conditions allow visual or instrumental operations.

visibility.d: The greatest distance at which lights of 1,000 candelas can be seen and identified against an unlit background (as reported by the airport/heliport).

visibilityInterpretation.d: Indicates whether the meteorology visibility is a minimum or a maximum value.

runwayVisualRange.d: The distance over which a pilot of an aircraft on the centreline of the runway can see the runway surface markings or the lights delineating the runway or identifying its centre line.

runwayVisualRangeInterpretation.d: Indicates whether the Meteorology Runway Visual Range is a minimum or maximum value.

CallsignDetail.d: Information about the operational identifier by which the provider of the service is called and the language used.

callSign.d: The full textual service provider identification or call-sign.

language.d: A code indicating the language in which the service is provided, as associated with a particular call-sign.

category.d: A code indicating a type of fuel for aircraft and helicopters (e.g. OCT73, OCT80-87, AVGAS, OCT100-130, OCT115-145, MOGAS, JET, A1, A1+, B, JP4, JP5).

type.d: The type of nitrogen supplies for aviation usage.

category.d: A code indicating a category of oil used in aircraft (e.g. TURBO, AVIA, HYD).

type.d: The type of oxygen supplies for aviation usage.

specialDateAuthority.d: Indicates that the SpecialDates associated with the related OrganisationAuthority are applicable to the schedule definition.

operationalStatus.d: Indicates the operational capability of the service.

RadioCommunicationOperationalStatus.d: Radio communication channel operational status information.

specialDateAuthority.d: Indicates that the SpecialDates associated with the related OrganisationAuthority are applicable to the schedule definition.

operationalStatus.d: Indicates the operational capability of the operational channel.

PointReference.d: Defines the location of a designated point using a combination of angles and distances based on the guidance service. The set of angles and distances must not under specify the location. The indications that are part of the PointReference must locate the same designated point.

role.d: Describes the role of the defined point reference. Example: DME, INT, recommended navaid, fix tolerance

priorFixTolerance.d: Because the fix may be received early, protection against obstacles must be provided from a line perpendicular to the flight course. PriorFixTolerance indicates the error distance (from the fix to the earliest point where the fix may be received along the flight course.

postFixTolerance.d: Indicates the error distance (from the fix to the latest point where the fix may be received along the flight course.

point.d: A point defined by a latitude and longitude and/or a combination of angle and/or distance indications.

facilityAngle.d: Angle from the facility to the Significant Point.

facilityDistance.d: Distance from the facility to the Significant Point.

fixToleranceArea.d: The dimensions of the fix tolerance area are determined by the system use accuracy of the navigation aid(s) on which the fix is based, and the distance from the facility.

minimumReceptionLimit.d: The lowest vertical distance required to receive adequate signals from navigational aids used to locate a significant point.

minimumReceptionLimitReference.d: A code which defines the reference surface for the minimum reception limit.

maximumAuthorisedLimit.d: The highest vertical distance where a point reference may be used to locate a significant point.

maximumAuthorisedLimitReference.d: A code which defines the reference surface for the maximum authorised limit.

distanceReference.d: Indicates the distance from the navigation aid(s) or designated point on which the fix is based.

angleReference.d: Angle from the facility to the Significant Point.

reportingATC.d: An indicator of the type of position report (e.g., compulsory or on request ) required by an ATC Unit.

flyOver.d: Indicates if the aircraft is required to fly directly over the fix. If code is Yes, then it is a 'fly-over' waypoint. If the code is No, then the associated fix is a 'fly-by' waypoint. [ICAO] Waypoints are identified as either flyover or fly-by. Fly-by waypoint. A waypoint which requires turn anticipation to allow tangential interception of the next segment of a route or procedure Flyover waypoint. A waypoint at which a turn is initiated in order to join the next segment of a route or procedure.

radarGuidance.d: Radar guidance is possible for reaching an associated point.

facilityMakeup.d: Segment point is located using specific makeup known as a reference.

extendedServiceVolume.d: An approved and flight checked extension to the standard service volume of a navaid

role.d: Identifies the function or position the point plays in the approach procedure.

leadRadial.d: The lead radial provides information for aircraft with single receiving equipment to change the receiver to the localizer or other facility providing the course guidance and to ensure the aircraft is within the clearance coverage area of LOC facilities before changing frequency or accepting on-course indication.

leadDME.d: The lead DME , like the lead Radial, provides information for aircraft with single receiving equipment to change the receiver to the localizer or other facility providing the course guidance and to ensure the aircraft is within the clearance coverage area of LOC facilities before changing frequency or accepting on-course indication.

indicatorFACF.d: Indicates the point is also a Final Approach Course Fix (FACF).

EnRouteSegmentPoint.d: Indicates a point associated with a defined EnRoute segment.

pointChoice_position.d: Segments use a significant point as a point segment.

extendedServiceVolume.d: An approved and flight checked extension to the standard service volume of a navaid

roleFreeFlight.d: Free flight is a an air traffic control method that uses no centralized control (e.g. air traffic controllers). Instead, parts of airspace are reserved dynamically and automatically in a distributed way using computer communication to ensure the required separation between aircraft

roleRVSM.d: A code indicating that the point has a specific role in the reduced vertical separation minima (RVSM) context.

turnRadius.d: The recommended turn radius when continuing on the previous segment of the route (start point) or when continuing on the next segment of the route(end point).

roleMilitaryTraining.d: A code indicating the usage of the point in the case of a military training route.

AngleUse.d: Indicates the role of the AngleIndication in the PointReference (for example, along track versus intersecting).

alongCourseGuidance.d: Defines if the angle indication provides the course guidance for the segment.

theAngleIndication.d: Angle from the facility to the Significant Point.

AuthorityForNavaidEquipment.d: Provides details about the level of responsibility of an OrganisationAuthority for a Navaid Equipment.

type.d: The type of relationship between the NavaidEquipment and the OrganisationAuthority.

theOrganisationAuthority.d: The organization responsible for the equipment (could be owner or operator).

AuthorityForSpecialNavigationStation.d: Provides details about the level of responsibility of an OrganisationAuthority for a Special Navigation System Station.

type.d: The type of responsibility of the OrganizationAuthority for the Special Navigation System Station.

theOrganisationAuthority.d: The organization responsible for the equipment.

AuthorityForSpecialNavigationSystem.d: Provides details about the level of responsibility of an OrganisationAuthority for a Special Navigation System.

type.d: The type of responsibility of the OrganisationAuthority for the Special Navigation System.

theOrganisationAuthority.d: The organization responsible for the equipment.

NavaidComponent.d: Indicates navigation use of a NavaidEquipment as a component of the navigation service provided by a Navaid. For example the DME NavaidEquipment is a NavaidComponent of an ILS system. The DME may be collocated with the Localizer and the DME may provide the navigable location for the Navaid service.

collocationGroup.d: An indication that the NavaidEquipment is collocated with one or more other NavaidEquipments (that have the same collocation number).

markerPosition.d: A code indicating the position, in a navaid landing system, of the markers situated on the centreline of a runway. For example: outer, middle, etc..

providesNavigableLocation.d: Indicates the navaid equipment used to specify the navigable location of the Navaid when the navaid is used as significant point

theNavaidEquipment.d: the component of the navaid system

specialDateAuthority.d: Indicates that the SpecialDates associated with the related OrganisationAuthority are applicable to the schedule definition.

operationalStatus.d: Indicates the state of the navaid.

signalType.d: The type of signal that is affected by the operational status.

specialDateAuthority.d: Indicates that the SpecialDates associated with the related OrganisationAuthority are applicable to the schedule definition.

monitored.d: Navaid equipment is monitored or not.
