Note.d: A general text note for a feature or for one of its properties.

propertyName.d: The name of the feature property for which this note is relevant, if applicable. If no propertyName is specified, then the Note is relevant for the feature as a whole.

purpose.d: An indication of the goal which led to the provision of the free text note.

LinguisticNote.d: The note content expressed in a specific language. As a minimum, all Notes shall be expressed in English.

note.d: The text of the Note, in a specific language.

OrganisationAuthorityAssociation.d: A type of hierarchical or associative relationship between two organizations or authorities showing ownership, supervision or membership.

type.d: The kind of association between two Organisations/Authorities.

theOrganisationAuthority.d: The related organisation, authority or agency.

UnitDependency.d: Describes the operational/functional relationship between two related units.

type.d: An indicator of the kind of dependency that a related unit has in relation to the unit. For example: the related unit is an owner of the unit, the related unit is a provider of services to the unit, the related unit provides an alternate/replacement service to the unit, etc.

UnitAvailability.d: Status and scheduling information about a unit.

specialDateAuthority.d: Indicates that the SpecialDates associated with the related OrganisationAuthority are applicable to the schedule definition.

operationalStatus.d: An indicator of the operational status of a Unit in regards to its availability.

VerticalStructurePart.d: A part of the vertical structure that can be represented as point, line or polygon with vertical extent.

specialDateAuthority.d: Indicates that the SpecialDates associated with the related OrganisationAuthority are applicable to the schedule definition.

verticalExtent.d: The vertical extent of the vertical structure part.

verticalExtentAccuracy.d: Accuracy of the value of the declared vertical extent.

type.d: An indicator of the type of vertical structure part, such as building, tower, cable, etc.

constructionStatus.d: The status of construction of the man-made object that constitutes the vertical structure part.

markingPattern.d: The general layout of the external paint or another marking element, intended to increase the visibility of the vertical structure part.

markingFirstColour.d: The principal colour of the marking of the vertical structure part.

markingSecondColour.d: The secondary colour for the marking of the vertical structure part.

mobile.d: An indicator that the vertical structure part is expected to move around its nominal location.

frangible.d: An indicator that the vertical structure part is easily broken.

visibleMaterial.d: An indicator of the type(s) of material that compose the load-bearing structure and/or exterior facing of a vertical construction (for example: a building or non-building structure).

designator.d: A distinguishing label by which the vertical structure part is identified locally.

horizontalProjection_location.d: Indicates the horizontal projection of the VerticalStructurePart and the elevation of its top.

horizontalProjection_linearExtent.d: Indicates the horizontal projection of the VerticalStructurePart and the elevation of its top.

horizontalProjection_surfaceExtent.d: Indicates the horizontal projection of the VerticalStructurePart and the elevation of its top.

lighting.d: Identifies the Light Elements installed on the Vertical StructurePart.

height.d: The maximum distance from the top of the vertical structure to the ground underneath (at the same position).

VerticalStructureLightingStatus.d: The description of the operational status of the Vertical Structure lighting.

specialDateAuthority.d: Indicates that the SpecialDates associated with the related OrganisationAuthority are applicable to the schedule definition.

status.d: An indication of the operational status of the lighting for a vertical structure. For example, serviceable, unserviceable, work in progress, etc.

CirclingRestriction.d: Describes a (sub)sector used to restrict flight within a circling area.

specialDateAuthority.d: Indicates that the SpecialDates associated with the related OrganisationAuthority are applicable to the schedule definition.

sectorDescription.d: depicts the attributes that describe the geometry for the restricted area

restrictionArea.d: depicts the geometry for the restricted area

Minima.d: Vertical and horizontal visual minimums for a procedure segment conditions such as aircraft category, navigation equipment usage, procedure type, altimeter, etc.

altitude.d: The lowest altitude used in establishing compliance with obstacle clearance criteria. The lowest altitude an aircraft flies before making a decision to land or abort and take the missed approach. (Highest of the lower limit altitudes in controlling obstacles plus the altitude adjustments (operational factors))

altitudeCode.d: An indication of the meaning of the altitude value, such as obstacle clearance altitude or decision altitude.

altitudeReference.d: A code indicating the reference for the altitude.

height.d: The height value for the minimum

militaryHeight.d: The height value for the minimum used by militaries, such as DoD in United States.

radioHeight.d: The height reported by a radio altimeter. Applies to CAT II.

heightCode.d: An indication of the meaning of the height value, such as obstacle clearance height or decision height.

heightReference.d: The reference surface for the height value.

visibility.d: The minimum visibility needed to land at the airport when using the specified altitude and/or height.

militaryVisibility.d: The visibility value applicable to the military height.

remoteAltimeterMinima.d: Indicates if this minima is the primary.

adjustmentINOP.d: Minimums are adjusted when equipment is unavailable.

obstacleClearanceAltitude.d: The lowest altitude used in establishing compliance with appropriate obstacle clearance criteria.

decisionAltitude.d: A specified altitude in reference to mean sea level in an approach with vertical guidance at which a missed approach must be initiated if the required visual references to continue the approach have not been established.

minimumDescentAltitude.d: A specified altitude in a non-precision approach or circling approach below which descent must not be made without the required visual reference.

obstacleClearanceHeight.d: The lowest height above the elevation of the relevant runway threshold or the aerodrome elevation as applicable, used in establishing compliance with appropriate obstacle clearance criteria.

decisionHeight.d: A specified height in the precision approach or approach with vertical guidance at which a missed approach must be initiated if the required visual reference to continue the approach has not been established.

minimumDescentHeight.d: A specified height in a non-precision approach or circling approach below which descent must not be made without the required visual reference.

militaryCeiling.d: The minimum height of the cloud base applicable to military aircraft in relation with the minima values.

militaryMinima.d: An indication that the minima values are applicable to military operations.

runwayVisualRange.d: A minimum RVR value provided by a standardised Runway Visual Range (RVR) equipment, associated with the minima.

aircraftCategory.d: A category of aircraft, usually based on the landing performance classification, for which the Minima is provided.

EquipmentUnavailableAdjustment.d: Used to describe adjustments to minimums when equipment is not available

type.d: Indicates if the specified altitude/height is adjusted for the case when certain equipment is unavailable.

approachLightingInoperative.d: Indicates if the specified altitude/height is adjusted for the case when the approach lighting is inoperative.

EquipmentUnavailableAdjustmentColumn.d: Adjustments that need to be applied in case equipment is inoperative.

guidanceEquipment.d: The guidance equipment which is inoperative

landingSystemLights.d: Indicates if landing System Lights are available

visibilityAdjustment.d: Adjusted for the corresponding visibility value.

approachLightingInoperative.d: Indicates of the approach lighting is INOPERATIVE

TerminalArrivalAreaSector.d: Subdivision of the TAA to allow for lower altitudes. The lowest altitude will provide a minimum clearance of 300m (1000ft) above all objects located in the sector.

flyByCode.d: Indicates if the aircraft is not required to fly directly over the fix. If code is Yes, then it is a 'flyby' waypoint. If the code is No or nil, then the associated fix is a 'fly-over' waypoint. [ICAO] Waypoints are identified as either flyover or fly-by.

procedureTurnRequired.d: The attribute is used to indicate when a course reversal is not necessary/authorized when flying within a particular TAA sector.

altitudeDescription.d: A code indicating how the altitude attributes should be interpreted: 'at' the lower altitude, 'at or above' the lower altitude, 'at or below' the lower altitude or 'between' the altitudes specified in the attributes lowerAltitude and upperAltitude distances.

sectorDefinition.d: Identifies the circle sector that describes the terminal arrival area sector.

extent.d: depicts the geometry of the TAA sector geometry

significantObstacle.d: Obstacle assessment resolves the need for TAA sectors.

FASDataBlock.d: Final Approach Segment Data Block. The additional information about the Precision Final Segment. Most attributes describe the LPV path point record required for WAAS procedures.

horizontalAlarmLimit.d: (ARINC) Horizontal Alert Limit (HAL) is the radius of a circle in the horizontal plane (the local plane tangent to the WGS-84 ellipsoid), with its centre being at the true position, which describes the region which is required to contain the indicated horizontal position with the required probability for a particular navigation mode assuming the probability of a GPS satellite integrity failure being included in the position solution is less than or equal to E-4 per hour.

verticalAlarmLimit.d: (ARINC) Vertical Alert Limit (VAL) is half the length of a segment on the vertical axis (perpendicular to the horizontal plane of WGS-84 ellipsoid), with its centre being at the true position, which describes the region which is required to contain the indicated vertical position with a probability of 1-E-7 per approach, assuming the probability of a GPS satellite integrity failure being included in the position solution is less than or equal to E-4 per hour.

thresholdCourseWidth.d: The width of the lateral course at the Landing Threshold Point (LTP). This width, in conjunction with the location of the Flight Path Alignment Point (FPAP) defines the sensitivity of the lateral deviations throughout the approach.

lengthOffset.d: Distance from the stop end of the runway to the Flight Path Alignment Point

CRCRemainder.d: Hexadecimal representation of the 32-bit CRC used to check the integrity of the FAS data block.

operationType.d: Operation Type. A number from 0 to 15 that indicates the type of the final approach segment.

serviceProviderSBAS.d: SBAS Service Provider Identifier. A number from 0 to 15 that associates the approach procedure to a particular satellite based approach system service provider.

approachPerformanceDesignator.d: Approach Performance Designator. A number from 0 to 7 that identifies the type of approach.

routeIndicator.d: Route Indicator. A single alpha character (A through Z or blank, omitting I and O) used to differentiate between multiple final approach segments to the same runway or heliport.

referencePathDataSelector.d: Reference Path Data Selector (RPDS). A number (0-48) that enables automatic tuning of a procedure by LAAS avionics.

referencePathIdentifier.d: Reference Path Identifier. A four-character identifier that is used to confirm selection of the correct approach procedure.

codeICAO.d: The first two designators of the ICAO location identifier, as identified in ICAO Doc 7910.

measurementPoint.d: Indicates the point of the altitude measurement as reporting on a terminal procedure chart.

altitude.d: The calculated altitude at the indicated point.

startingMeasurementPoint.d: Indicates starting point of the vertical or horizontal measurement

endingMeasurementPoint.d: Indicates ending point of the vertical or horizontal measurement

distance.d: Calculated distanced between the start and end point.

altimeter.d: A source for determining aircraft altitude using pressure measurements. Air pressure decreases with an increase of altitude approximately one inch of mercury per 1000 ft near sea level.

requiredNavigationPerformance.d: [ICAO] Required navigation performance (RNP). [ICAO] Specifies the minimum navigation performance accuracy required in an airspace. It is the navigation performance accuracy of all the user and navigation system combinations within an airspace. Note: It is a tolerance factor for flying. The factor is taken into consideration when determining protected airspace for aircraft.

climbGradient.d: The capability of an aircraft to climb with a certain gradient in take-off configuration.

minimumSet.d: minimums may be created for a set of conditions

circlingRestriction.d: restrictions may be created for a set of conditions

aircraftCategory.d: Classification of aircraft based on 1.3 times stall speed in landing configuration at maximum certified landing mass.

landingArea.d: Minimum Final Approach Condition may apply to one or more Runway Directions;final and sidestep

altimeter.d: The altimeter that the Minimum Final Approach Condition applies to.

designSurface.d: Relationship exists when multiple RNP minimas exist

navigationAccuracy.d: The PBN navigation accuracy value associated with the minima.

landingPrecisionCategory.d: The precision of the final segment guidance system to which the associated Minima refer.

satelliteApproachType.d: The type of the final segment vertical and/or horizontal guidance in case of a GNSS procedure, to which the associated Minima refer.

specialAuthorisation.d: The associated minima can be used only with special authorisation. Note: this is a different thing from the RNP AR APCH.

minBaroVNAVTemperature.d: The airport temperature below which the use of Baro-VNAV is not authorized to the LNAV/VNAV minima.

maxBaroVNAVTemperature.d: The airport temperature above which the use of Baro-VNAV is not authorized to the LNAV/VNAV minima.

stepdownFix.d: A position on the final segment of a non-precision approach that, when positively identified, enables a lower set of minima.

NavigationAreaSector.d: Subdivision of a sector to allow for different altitudes or gradients.

sectorDefinition.d: Defines a non graphical definition describing a portion of a navigation area.

significantObstacle.d: Identifies the obstacle that control the altitude definition of the sector or would penetrate the 40:1 OCS.

extent.d: The surface extent of the navigation area sector.

sectorCriteria.d: Identifies the Sector Design defined by the Navigation Area Sector.

minimumEnrouteAltitude.d: Minimum en-route altitude (MEA). The altitude for an en-route segment that provides adequate reception of relevant navigation facilities and ATS communications, complies with the airspace structure and provides the required obstacle clearance.

minimumCrossingAtEnd.d: The lowermost vertical position at the end point, when flying on the route portion in the direction indicated in the RoutePortionUsage.

maximumCrossingAtEnd.d: The uppermost vertical position at the end point, when flying on the route portion in the direction indicated in the RoutePortionUsage.

maximumCrossingAtEndReference.d: The reference surface used for the value of the maximumCrossingAtEnd. For example, Mean Sea Level, Ground, standard pressure, etc..

engineType.d: type of aircraft engine allowed for the condition

turnDirection.d: A code indicating the direction of the turn.

turnPermitted.d: Indicates if the sector is clear for the direction of turn.

vectorHeading.d: A heading provided for use, when a departure is designed to incorporate radar vectors at the termination point, in the event ATC instructions are not received prior to or at the termination fix.

instructedAltitude.d: An altitude referenced in the holding use instructions.

instructionAltitudeReference.d: A code indicating the reference for a vertical distance. Two series of values exist: 1) real distance: from GND, from the MSL, from the WGS-84 ellipsoid 2) pressure distance: QFE, QNH, STD.

endPoint.d: An indication of a specific point role (such as ‘MAP’) in the approach procedure down to which the control timing is calculated.

time.d: The duration of the flight between the start point and the end point.

distance.d: The horizontal distance flown between the start point and the end point.

speed.d: The speed of the aircraft used to calculate the time.

speedReference.d: An indication of the speed reference (ground or air).

rateOfDescent.d: The calculated value of the vertical descent speed between the start and the end point.

FinalApproachSegmentData.d: Parameters that identify a single precision approach or APV and define its associated approach path.

approachPerformanceDesignator.d: Approach Performance Designator. A number from 0 to 7 that identifies the type of approach.

codeICAO.d: The first two designators of the ICAO location identifier, as identified in ICAO Doc 7910.

CRCRemainder.d: Hexadecimal representation of the 32-bit CRC used to check the integrity of the FAS data block.

horizontalAlarmLimit.d: (ARINC) Horizontal Alert Limit (HAL) is the radius of a circle in the horizontal plane (the local plane tangent to the WGS-84 ellipsoid), with its centre being at the true position, which describes the region which is required to contain the indicated horizontal position with the required probability for a particular navigation mode assuming the probability of a GPS satellite integrity failure being included in the position solution is less than or equal to E-4 per hour.

lengthOffset.d: Distance from the stop end of the runway to the Flight Path Alignment Point

operationType.d: Operation Type. A number from 0 to 15 that indicates the type of the final approach segment.

referencePathDataSelector.d: Reference Path Data Selector (RPDS). A number (0-48) that enables automatic tuning of a procedure by LAAS avionics.

referencePathIdentifier.d: Reference Path Identifier. A four-character identifier that is used to confirm selection of the correct approach procedure.

routeIndicator.d: Route Indicator. A single alpha character (A through Z or blank, omitting I and O) used to differentiate between multiple final approach segments to the same runway or heliport.

serviceProviderSBAS.d: SBAS Service Provider Identifier. A number from 0 to 15 that associates the approach procedure to a particular satellite based approach system service provider.

thresholdCourseWidth.d: The width of the lateral course at the Landing Threshold Point (LTP). This width, in conjunction with the location of the Flight Path Alignment Point (FPAP) defines the sensitivity of the lateral deviations throughout the approach.

verticalAlarmLimit.d: (ARINC) Vertical Alert Limit (VAL) is half the length of a segment on the vertical axis (perpendicular to the horizontal plane of WGS-84 ellipsoid), with its centre being at the true position, which describes the region which is required to contain the indicated vertical position with a probability of 1-E-7 per approach, assuming the probability of a GPS satellite integrity failure being included in the position solution is less than or equal to E-4 per hour.

airportID.d: A three- or four-letter designator used to designate an airport.

runwayLetter.d: The one-letter designator used, as necessary, to differentiate between parallel runways.

thresholdPointLatitude.d: The latitude value of the landing or fictitious threshold point.

thresholdPointLongitude.d: The longitude value of the landing or fictitious threshold point.

thresholdPointHeight.d: The height of the landing or fictitious threshold point above the WGS-84 ellipsoid.

finalPointLatitude.d: The latitude value of the flight path alignment point (FPAP).

finalPointLongitude.d: The longitude value of the flight path alignment point (FPAP).

deltaFinalPointLatitude.d: The difference of latitude of the runway FPAP from the LTP/FTP in arc seconds.

deltaFinalPointLongitude.d: The difference of longitude of the runway FPAP from the LTP/FTP in arc seconds.

thresholdCrossingHeight.d: The height of the final approach segment path above the LTP/FTP defined in the unit of measurement indicated by the thresholdCrossingHeightUnits.

thresholdCrossingHeightUnits.d: An indication of the units of measurement used to express the thresholdCrossingHeight.

glidepathAngle.d: The angle of the final approach segment path with respect to the horizontal plane tangent to the WGS-84 ellipsoid at the LTP/FTP.

thresholdOrthoHeight.d: he height of the LTP/FTP as related to the geoid and presented as an MSL elevation to a tenth of a metre with the decimal point suppressed.

finalPointOrthoHeight.d: The height of the flight path alignment point (FPAP) as related to the geoid and presented as an MSL elevation to a tenth of a metre with the decimal point suppressed.

FASDataBlock.d: The set of parameters to identify an approach and define its associated approach path in hexadecimal representation.

SegmentLegAltitudeCondition.d: An altitude condition which is established for a segment leg.

minimumEnrouteAltitude.d: Minimum en-route altitude (MEA). The altitude for an en-route segment that provides adequate reception of relevant navigation facilities and ATS communications, complies with the airspace structure and provides the required obstacle clearance.

minimumCrossingAtEnd.d: The lowermost (at or above) vertical position at the end point.

minimumCrossingAtEndReference.d: The reference surface used for the value of the minimumCrossingAtEnd. For example, Mean Sea Level, Ground, standard pressure, etc..

maximumCrossingAtEnd.d: The uppermost (at or below) vertical position at the end point.

maximumCrossingAtEndReference.d: The reference surface used for the value of the maximumCrossingAtEnd. For example, Mean Sea Level, Ground, standard pressure, etc..

engineType.d: Identifies th type of aircraft engine allowed for the condition

MinimumAltitudeAreaSector.d: An area with a specified geometry and minimum altitude values.

bufferWidth.d: Width of the secondary area used to evaluate the lowest usable altitude for obstacle assessment.

name.d: A pronounceable name that is used to identify the minimum altitude area sector.

altitude.d: The value of the minimum altitude in the area.

altitudeLowTemperature.d: A second value of the minimum altitude in the area, used below the minimum temperature.

significantObstacle.d: Obstacle assessment resolves the need for MSA sectors.

sectorDefinition.d: depicts the attributes that describe the geometry for the MSA

extent.d: depicts the geometry for the MSA

CourseGroup.d: Defines the direction in which the aircraft has to be steered.

course.d: The value of the course expressed as an angle and measured in degrees.

courseType.d: A code indicating the type of course to be observed.

courseDirection.d: Indicates the flight direction to/from the navaid providing the course guidance.

cardinalDirection.d: An indicator of the general cardinal direction of the segment.

navigationEquipment.d: A type of navigation equipment capability associated with the use of the altitude.

direction.d: An indicator of the direction of the segment.

AirspaceBorderCrossing.d: A type of traffic flow condition element which consist of crossing the common border between two adjacent airspace, when flying directly from one airspace into the other airspace.

exitedAirspace.d: The airspace the aircraft crosses from

AircraftNavigationEquipment.d: Radio navigation equipment capabilities available on board.

navigationEquipment.d: An indication of the aircraft capability for using a specified ground based, satellite based or on-board system for aerial navigation.

DesignStandard.d: A formal standard containing rules and criteria applied in the design of the flight procedures or routes.

name.d: The name by which the standard that provides the design rules is known.

version.d: A textual identifier of the exact document/version used as the design standard.

ObstacleAssessmentSurface.d: The geometry of surfaces used to evaluate the obstructions that are taken into consideration in the design of a procedure leg, a holding pattern, etc.

type.d: Indicated the type of area being assessed such as 40:1, 72:1, MA, Final, etc

sectionNumber.d: a sequence number indicating a part of an assessment area.

slope.d: The slope value of the extent

assessedAltitude.d: Highest of the minimum altitudes in controlling obstacles plus the altitude adjustments (operational factors)

slopeLowerAltitude.d: The altitude at the bottom of the assessment area

gradientLowHigh.d: Low to high gradient within the airspace

surfaceZone.d: Specifies zones within obstruction identification surfaces (OIS)

safetyRegulation.d: Identifier for the safety regulations in effect within the zone

significantObstacle.d: The obstacle that controls the altitude definition of the assessment area would penetrate the 40:1 OCS

aircraftCategory.d: Identifies the aircraft category for which the Obstacle Assessment Area is evaluated for.

surface.d: Identifies the extent of the Obstacle Assessment Area.

startingCurve.d: The curve that starts the ObstacleAssessmentArea.

CodeAircraftEngineNumber.d: A coded indication for the number of engines of an aircraft.

v.2C: Two coupled engines driving one propeller.

CodeAirspaceActivity.d: A code indicating the primary activity taking place in the airspace or the reason for its establishment.

v.AD_TFC: All traffic on the manoeuvring area of an airport/heliport and all aircraft flying in the vicinity of an airport/heliport. (Annex 11). Description: A type of special air traffic.
v.HELI_TFC: Helicopter or gyrocopter operations. Description: A type of special air traffic.
v.TRAINING: Flights conducted for the purpose of training. Description: A type of special air traffic.
v.AEROBATICS: The usage of unusual or artful flying manoeuvres for recreation, competition, or entertainment. Description: A type of special air traffic.
v.AIRSHOW: A show at which aircraft are on view and featuring aerial displays. Description: A type of special air traffic.
v.SPORT: The competition or practice by an individual or a group to achieve the best aerial performance. Description: A type of special air traffic. This could be an air race or aerobatic training or competition.
v.GLIDING: Flying a non-power-driven heavier-than-air aircraft. Description: A type of special air traffic. (ICAO derived) A glider derives its lift in flight chiefly from aerodynamic reactions on surfaces which remain fixed under given conditions of flight.
v.PARAGLIDER: Recreational and competitive flying sport using a free-flying, foot launched aircraft. Description: A type of special air traffic. When paragliding, the pilot sits in a harness suspended below a fabric wing, whose shape is formed by the pressure of air entering vents in the front of the wing. It is known in some countries as parapenting.
v.HANGGLIDING: Recreational and competitive flying sport using a small glider from which the operator is suspended in a frame and which is controlled by movements of the body. Description: A type of special air traffic.
v.PARACHUTE: Exiting a flying aircraft by an individual using a parachute. Description: A type of special air traffic. A parachute is a soft fabric device used to slow the motion through the atmosphere by generating drag.
v.AIR_DROP: The dropping of troops, supplies, bombs, etc., from an aircraft. Description: A type of special air traffic.
v.BALLOON: Flight activity involving a bag called the envelope that is capable of containing heated air, with a gondola or basket suspended beneath. Description: A type of special air traffic.
v.RADIOSONDE: The lifting of devices through the atmosphere, which are tied to a helium or hydrogen filled balloon. Description: A type of special air traffic. Radio probe and meteorological balloons are examples.
v.SPACE_FLIGHT: Vertical launch for space flight operations. Description: A type of special air traffic.
v.UAV: The operation of a powered, aerial vehicle that does not carry a human operator. Description: A type of special air traffic. (NATO derived) An Unmanned Aerial Vehicle uses aerodynamic forces to provide vehicle lift, can fly autonomously or be piloted remotely, can be expendable or recoverable, and can carry a lethal or non-lethal payload.
v.AERIAL_WORK: Operations in which an aircraft is used for specialized services. Description: A type of special air traffic. Services such as agriculture, construction, photography, surveying, observation and patrol, search and rescue, aerial advertisement, etc. are examples.
v.CROP_DUSTING: Spraying crops with fertilizers, pesticides, and fungicides from an agricultural aircraft. Description: A type of special air traffic.
v.FIRE_FIGHTING: Intense fire fighting activity involving chemical agents being laid down from fire fighting aircraft. Description: A type of special air traffic.
v.MILOPS: The execution of operations by the military. Description: A type of military activity (usually).
v.REFUEL: Transfer of fuel between aircraft in the air. Description: A type of military activity (usually).
v.JET_CLIMBING: Climb-out of jet aircraft via predefined and common tracks. Description: A type of military activity (usually).
v.EXERCISE: Intercepting and destroying of hostile aircraft or conducting similar training activities. Description: A type of military activity (usually).
v.TOWING: Drawing or pulling through the air a target for aerial shooting practice. Description: A type of military activity (usually).
v.NAVAL_EXER: Naval forces (for example: vessels or aircraft) conduct firing and/or munitions exercises. Description: Distinguished from areas where Naval forces conduct general operations and manoeuvres.
v.MISSILES: The launch, transit, and targeting of guided missiles. Description: A type of military activity (usually). (NATO) A guided missile is an unmanned self-propelled vehicle whose trajectory or course, while in flight, is controlled.
v.AIR_GUN: The delivery of air to air or air to ground weapons for the destruction of a target. Description: A type of military activity (usually).
v.ARTILLERY: The discharge of a projectile into the air for the destruction of a target. Description: A type of military activity (usually).
v.SHOOTING: The discharge of a gun or bow to propel arrows, bullets, etc swiftly or violently direct and sharply in specified directions. Description: A type of military activity (usually). This could be a shooting range or hunting area.
v.BLASTING: Controlled use of explosives to excavate or remove rock. Description: A type of hazard.
v.WATER_BLASTING: The action or an act of forcing out or emitting something suddenly underwater. Description: A type of hazard. Usually involving violence and noise.
v.ANTI_HAIL: The use of small rockets to protect crops by seeding clouds with small particles that prevent hailstorms from forming. Description: A type of hazard.
v.BIRD_MIGRATION: A high number of bird species as they fly instinctual routes based on breeding or diverse environmental urges. Description: A type of hazard. For Example: Large scale movements of migrating birds occur during various months in the European-Mediterranean and UK areas. There are also large concentrations of nesting, breeding, and wintering birds, often numbering in the millions.
v.FIREWORK: Launching of pyrotechnic devices. Description: A type of hazard. .
v.HI_RADIO: Electromagnetic fields produced by high intensity radio transmission. Description: A type of hazard.
v.HI_LIGHT: Non-navigational lights with high visibility potential. Description: A type of hazard.
v.LASER: The emission of photons in a coherent beam by an optical source. Description: A type of hazard. Laser stands for Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation. An example is a laser light show.
v.NATURE: Wildlife, flora, fauna or features of geological or other special interest which is reserved and managed for conservation. Description: A type of protection. This is given a protective status. This could provide special opportunities for study or research. For example, a national park. .
v.FAUNA: The animals or animal life of a given area, habitat, or epoch which is easily and dangerously aroused by excessive aerial noise such as from an aircraft. Description: A type of protection. Examples include mink or turkey farms and zoos.
v.NO_NOISE: Airspace in which special procedures or other precautionary measures are established for reducing noise. Description: A type of protection.
v.ACCIDENT: Airspace needing a protective status due to an investigation of a flight catastrophe. Description: A type of protection.
v.POPULATION: An area with a high concentration of inhabitants. Description: A type of protection.
v.VIP: The presence of an individual of renowned status and considered as a very important person. Description: A type of protection.
v.VIP_PRES: The presence of an individual with status of head of state. Description: A type of protection.
v.VIP_VICE: The presence of an individual with status of Vice-Head of State. Description: A type of protection.
v.OIL: An area in which oil occurs in quantities worthy of exploitation. Description: A type of industrial hazard.
v.GAS: Pumping natural gas from the ground or converting gasoline into vapour. Description: A type of industrial hazard.
v.REFINERY: A facility where petroleum and/or petroleum products are refined. Description: A type of industrial hazard.
v.CHEMICAL: A facility utilizing a chemical process for manufacturing. Description: A type of industrial hazard.
v.NUCLEAR: An installation which provides power, derived from fission or fusion of atomic nuclei. Description: A type of industrial hazard.
v.TECHNICAL: Generic technical activity affecting air traffic. Description: A type of industrial hazard. .
v.ATS: Custom specific flight information service, alerting service, air traffic advisory service, air traffic control service, area control service, approach control service, or airport control service is provided. Description: A type of procedure/service. This could be a service in the air or on the ground.
v.PROCEDURE: Special procedures established for use by operational personnel in execution of their flight. Description: A type of procedure/service. An overhead approach is an example of a special procedure.
v.UAS: An aircraft and its associated elements which are operated with no pilot on board.
v.NIGHT_VISION_OPS: Night vision device operations, aircraft lights out.

CodeAircraftCategory.d: A code indicating the type of an aircraft

v.UA: Unmanned aircraft. An aircraft intended to be flown without a pilot on board. It can be remotely and fully controlled from another place (ground, another aircraft, space) or pre-programmed to conduct its flight without intervention.

CodeFireFighting.d: A code specifying the category of fire fighting service provided at the airport/heliport.

v.H1: H1 [(Helicopter) rescue and fire category 1.] [note: (ICAO) Up to but not including 15m in length.]
v.H2: H2 [(Helicopter) rescue and fire category 2.] [note: (ICAO) From 15m up to but not including 24m in length.]
v.H3: H3 [(Helicopter) rescue and fire category 3.] [note: (ICAO) From 24m up to but not including 35m in length.]
v.A1: A1 [(Aircraft) rescue and fire category 1.] [note: (ICAO, NATO) 0 up to but not including 9m over-all length and 2m maximum fuselage width.]
v.A2: A2 [(Aircraft) rescue and fire category 2.] [note: (ICAO, NATO) 9m up to but not including 12m over-all length and 2m maximum fuselage width.]
v.A3: A3 [(Aircraft) rescue and fire category 3.] [note: (ICAO, NATO) 12m up to but not including 18m over-all length and 3m maximum fuselage width.]
v.A4: A4 [(Aircraft) rescue and fire category 4.] [note: (ICAO, NATO) 18m up to but not including 24m over-all length and 4m maximum fuselage width.]
v.A5: A5 [(Aircraft) rescue and fire category 5.] [note: (ICAO, NATO) 24m up to but not including 28m over-all length and 4m maximum fuselage width.]
v.A6: A6 [(Aircraft) rescue and fire category 6.] [note: (ICAO, NATO) 28m up to but not including 39m over-all length and 5m maximum fuselage width.]
v.A7: A7 [(Aircraft) rescue and fire category 7.] [note: (ICAO, NATO) 39m up to but not including 49m over-all length and 5m maximum fuselage width.]
v.A8: A8 [(Aircraft) rescue and fire category 8.] [note: (ICAO, NATO) 49m up to but not including 61m over-all length and 7m maximum fuselage width.]
v.A9: A9 [(Aircraft) rescue and fire category 9.] [note: (ICAO, NATO) 61m up to but not including 76m over-all length and 7m maximum fuselage width.]
v.A10: A10 [(Aircraft) rescue and fire category 10.] [note: 76m up to but not including 90m over-all length and 8m maximum fuselage width.]

CodeFuel.d: A code indicating the category of fuel available at an airport/heliport.

v.JPTS: Jet JP fuel with higher thermal stability.
v.JP8_HIGHER: Jet JP-8 with higher thermal stability.
v.F18: F-18 [(NATO) aviation gasoline (low lead) - equivalent AVGAS 100LL.]
v.F34: F-34 [(NATO) jet aviation fuel with FSII - equivalent JP-8.]
v.F35: F-35 [(NATO) jet aviation fuel - equivalent JET A-1.]
v.F40: F-40 [(NATO) jet aviation fuel with FSII - equivalent JP-4.]
v.F44: F-44 [(NATO) jet aviation fuel with FSII - equivalent JP-5.]
v.AVGAS_VLL: AVGAS 100 VLL [Octane 100 Very Low Lead aviation gasoline].

CodeOil.d: A code indicating the category of oil available at an airport/heliport.

CodeDMEChannel.d: A code indicating the channel of a DME.

CodeMLSChannel.d: A code indicating the channel of an MLS.

CodeTACANChannel.d: A code indicating the channel of a TACAN.

CodeHelicopterPerformance.d: A code indicating the performance class of a helicopter.

CodeMarkerBeaconSignal.d: A code indicating the class of a radio marker.

CodeNDBUsage.d: A code indicating the class of an NDB.

v.L: Locator - low powered NDB used as an aid for final approach (also known as a compass locator).

CodeColour.d: A code indicating a colour. The list of allowable values comprises 'named' colours, not colours being only describable using the RGB or the CYMK or another colour system combination.

CodeTimeEventCombination.d: A code indicating which event in a list of events in time should be given precedence over the others. E.g. the earliest or the latest.

CodeSurfaceComposition.d: A code indicating the composition of a surface. For example, asphalt, concrete etc..

v.GRASS: Grass including portions of turf or bare earth.
v.BITUM: Bituminous tar or asphalt and/or oil or bitumen bound, mix-in-place surfaces (often referred to as "earth cement"). [note: A bituminous tar or asphalt surface is prepared by digging up the surface, mixing the material with bitumen or oil binder, and surfacing the surface with the resulting mixture. Bitumen is the family name for tar which is derived from coal, or asphalt which is derived from oil. .]
v.MACADAM: A macadam or tarmac surface consisting of water-bound crushed rock.
v.LATERITE: Laterite - a high iron clay formed in tropical areas.
v.MEMBRANE: A protective laminate usually made of rubber.
v.MATS: Landing mat portable system usually made of aluminium.

CodeSurfaceCondition.d: A code indicating the condition of a surface, such as a runway, taxiway, the marking of a threshold, etc..

v.GOOD: Some cracking of the pavement. Cracks are generally spaced more than 15 m (50 feet) apart. Less than 10% of the cracks and joints need sealing. There is minimal or slight raveling. There is no distortion, and the patches are in good condition.
v.FAIR: Some cracking and raveling. Cracks are generally spaced less than 15 m (50 feet) apart. Joint and crack sealing is needed on 10% to 25% of the cracks and joints. There is isolated alligator cracking, the patches are in poor condition, and/or there are crack settlements up to 2.5 cm (1 inch).
v.POOR: Widespread, open, unsealed cracks and joints. There are cracks over 1 cm (½-inch) wide with raveling in 25% of the cracks. Cracks are generally spaced 1.5 m to 15 m (5 to 50 feet) apart with surface and slab spalling. Alligator cracking or patches are in poor condition and cover up to 20% of the surface or there is vegetation through the cracks and joints.
v.EXCELLENT: New pavement or pavement with no cracks or a few hairline cracks.
v.FAILED: Widespread severe cracking and distortion over 5 cm (2 inches). Alligator cracking over 20% or more and widespread vegetation growth in the pavement cracks. Slabs are extensively cracked and shattered with severe spalling and faulting over 1 cm (1/2 inch).

CodeDay.d: A code indicating a particular day. For example, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday, the day preceding a holiday, a legal holiday, the day following a holiday, the day preceding a working day, a working day, the day following a working day.

v.WORK_DAY: Working Day. This value indicates any day which is neither a Legal Holiday nor a weekly non-working day.
v.BEF_WORK_DAY: The day preceding a working day.
v.AFT_WORK_DAY: The day after a working day.
v.HOL: Legal Holiday. The value does not include the weekly non-working days (for example, Saturday and Sunday in most European States).
v.BEF_HOL: The day preceding a legal holiday.
v.AFT_HOL: The day after a legal holiday.
v.BUSY_FRI: Formally declared as 'Busy Friday' by the authority responsible for aeronautical information provision in the area concerned, in order to activate special traffic management arrangements.
v.MON_FRI: All days from Monday through Friday including legal holidays.
v.SUN_THU: All days from Sunday through Thursday including legal holidays.
v.SAT_WED: All days from Saturday through Wednesday including legal holidays.
v.SAT_THU: All days from Saturday through Thursday including legal holidays.

CodeAltitudeUse.d: A code indicating, in situations where both an upper and a lower altitude may be specified, how the altitude information should be interpreted.

v.ABOVE_LOWER: At or above the lower altitude.
v.BELOW_UPPER: At or below the higher altitude.
v.BETWEEN: Between the specified lower and upper limit.
v.RECOMMENDED: The specified lower limit is recommended.
v.AS_ASSIGNED: To be assigned at the time of operations (for example, by ATC)
v.AT_OR_ABOVE: At or above the specified lower limit.
v.AT_OR_BELOW: At or below the specified upper limit.
v.EXPECTED: The specified lower limit can be expected but may be modified by ATC.
v.BY_ATC: The procedure altitude/height will be assigned at the time of operations by ATC.

CodeDirection.d: A code indicating a 1-dimensional direction, for example, forward or backward.

CodeDirectionReference.d: A code indicating a direction with regard to a reference point, e.g. to or from.

CodeDirectionTurn.d: A code indicating the direction of a turn.

CodeVerticalReference.d: A code indicating the reference for a vertical distance. Two series of values exist: 1) real distance: from GND, from the MSL, from the WGS-84 ellipsoid; 2) distance based on a difference of pressures, according to the standard atmosphere.

v.SFC: The distance measured from the surface of the Earth (equivalent to AGL - Above Ground Level).
v.MSL: The distance measured from mean sea level (equivalent to altitude).
v.W84: The distance measured from the WGS84 ellipsoid.
v.STD: The vertical distance is measured with an altimeter set to the standard atmosphere.

CodeRadioEmission.d: A code indicating the type of emission, as defined at the 1979 ITU World Administrative Radio Conference. For example, A3E, NONA2a, G1D.

v.J3E: AM double side-band suppressed carrier telephony.
v.NONA1A: Unmod trans. morse ident. carrier emission interrupted.
v.NONA2A: Unmod. trans. morse ident. carrier emission continuous.
v.A8W: AM (unkeyed) plus ON/OFF keying of ident tone.
v.A9W: Composite AM/FM (unkeyed) plus ON/OFF keying of ident tone.

CodeFlowConditionOperation.d: A coded value used to indicate a type of operation combining an elementary flow condition or a previously defined combination of flow conditions with another elementary flow condition or previously defined combination.

v.ANDNOT: 1st condition fulfilled AND 2nd condition NOT fulfilled.
v.SEQ: 1st condition is fulfilled BEFORE 2nd condition is fulfilled.
v.NONE: No operation (used for flows identified by a single condition).

CodeFlightStatus.d: A code indicating status of a flight.

v.HEAD: Head of state.
v.STATE: State aircraft. (Other than head of state).
v.EMERGENCY: The aircraft has declared an emergency situation.

CodeFlight.d: A code indicating the type of a flight.

v.ALL: Both Operational and General Air Traffic.

CodeProcedureFixRole.d: A code indicating the role of a fix within an instrument approach procedure. Examples: initial approach fix, final approach fix, missed approach point, etc.

v.IF_IAF: Intermediate Fix or an Initial Approach Fix
v.FAF: Final approach fix for non-precision approach.
v.VDP: (FAA AIM) Visual descent point. The VDP is a defined point on the final approach course of a non precision straight-in approach procedure from which normal descent from the MDA to the runway touchdown point may be commenced, provided visual reference required by 14 CFR Section 91.175(c)(3) is established.
v.FTP: The Fictitious Threshold Point (FTP) is a point over which the final approach segment path passes at a relative height specified by the reference datum height (RDH). The FTP replaces the LTP when the final approach course is not aligned with the runway extended centre line or when the threshold is displaced from the actual runway threshold. For non-aligned approaches the FTP lies on the intersection of the perpendicular from the FAS to the runway threshold. The FTP elevation is the same as the actual runway threshold elevation.
v.FROP: Final Rollout Point - Where a course change is required within the Final Approach Segment (FAS), the point that the aircraft rolls to a wings-level attitude aligned with the runway centreline extended is considered the FROP. FROP is used in an RNP AR procedure when a turn is required in the final between the FAF and the threshold.
v.LTP: The Landing Threshold Point (LTP) is a point over which the glide path passes at a relative height specified by the reference datum height (RDH). The LTP is normally located at the intersection of the runway centre line and the threshold.
v.FEEDER_FIX: The fix depicted on Instrument Approach Procedure Charts which establishes the starting point of the feeder route.
v.PFAF: Precision Final Approach Fix - An RNP final approach is 3-D. The final approach fix for all 3-D approach procedures is the point that the glidepath intercepts the intermediate segment minimum altitude.
v.FAP: Final Approach Point - the position where the precision segment starts, that is, the intersection of the nominal glide path and the minimum altitude specified for the preceding segment.
v.DP: Descent point - A point defined by track and distance from the MAPt to identify the point at which the helicopter may descend below the OCA/H on a visual descent to the heliport/landing location.
v.FHP: Fictitious heliport point - is a point over which the PinS final approach segment path passes at a relative height defined as the fictitious heliport point crossing height (FHPCH). It is defined by the WGS-84 latitude, longitude and ellipsoid height. The FHP replaces the FTP for PinS approaches. The FHP elevation is the same as the actual landing heliport elevation.
v.IDF: Initial departure fix - The terminal fix for the visual segment and the fix where the instrument phase of the PinS departure begins.
v.MATF: Missed approach turning fix (MATF) is a fix different from MAPt that marks a turn in the missed approach segment.
v.PRP: Point-in-space reference point for the point-in-space approach as identified by the latitude and longitude of the MAPt.

CodeAircraftICAO.d: A coded aircraft type designator assigned by ICAO to all aircraft heavier than micro-/ultra-light.

CodeAirportHeliportDesignator.d: A coded identifier for an Aerodrome/Heliport. The rules according to which this identifier should be formed are as follows: 1) If the AD/HP has an ICAO four letter location indicator, this will become the CODE_ID for the Aerodrome/Heliport; 2) If the AD/HP does not have an ICAO four letter location indicator but has an IATA three letter code, then this will become the CODE_ID for the Aerodrome/Heliport; 3) If the AD/HP does not have either an ICAO four letter location indicator or an IATA three letter code, an artificially generated code will be used. This will contain a group of letters and a number. The group of letters could be the 2 letter code of the State responsible for the Aerodrome/Heliport (or one of these, if there are more than one, like ED and ET for Germany) and the number could be an integer between 0001 and 9999.

CodeSpecialNavigationChainDesignator.d: The coded identifier of a special navigation system chain.

CodeDesignatedPointDesignator.d: The coded identifier of a designated point or transition identification of a Procedure.

CodeLevelTableDesignator.d: A code identifying the table of discreet cruising levels. For example, ICAO IFR, ICAO VFR, ICAO RVSM, etc..

v.IFR_RVSM: ICAO IFR in areas with RVSM
v.IFR_METRES_RVSM: ICAO IFR in meters in areas with RVSM
v.VFR_RVMS: ICAO VFR in areas with RVSM.
v.VFR_METRES_RVSM: ICAO VFR in meters in areas with RVSM.
v.VFR_RVSM: ICAO VFR in areas with RVSM.

CodeNavaidDesignator.d: The coded identifier of a radio navigation aid.

CodeOrganisationDesignator.d: The coded identifier of an organisation, authority, agency or unit.

CodeFlightRestrictionDesignator.d: A coded value which uniquely identifies a traffic flow restriction.

CodeRouteOrigin.d: Code indicating if a route is international or domestic.

CodeLightIntensity.d: A code indicating the intensity level of a light source. For example, LIL, LIM, LIH, etc.

v.LIL_LIH: Low intensity for night use; high intensity for day use, as determined by a photo-cell.
v.PREDETERMINED: A predetermined intensity step, in the approach lighting system that takes precedence for air-to-ground radio control over the runway lighting system which is set, based on expected visibility conditions.

CodeLanguage.d: A 3-letter code indicating a language (according to ISO 639-2)

CodeIATA.d: The three letter coded location identifier of an airport/heliport according to the IATA Resolution 763.

CodeICAO.d: The four letter coded location identifier as published in the ICAO DOC 7910 - Location Indicators.

CodeAviationStandards.d: A code indicating the standard referred to by a list of values, in case where different aviation authorities use different categorisation criteria.

v.ICAO: The values refer to ICAO standards.
v.IATA: The values refer to IATA standards.
v.NATO: The values refer to NATO military standards.
v.FAA: The values refer to US FAA standards.

CodeLevel.d: A code indicating the level: upper airspace, lower airspace or both.

CodeMilitaryStatus.d: A code distinguishing between military and civil status.

CodeAirspaceAggregation.d: An 'operator' in coded form according to which two 'operands' will be 'associated' in order to produce a result.

v.BASE: 'Parent' airspace is the basis for subsequent operations.
v.UNION: 'Parent' airspace is second operand in a union operation.
v.INTERS: 'Parent' airspace is second operand in intersection operation.
v.SUBTR: 'Parent' airspace is second operand in subtraction operation.

CodeFlightOrigin.d: A coded list of values indicating the source of a flight (local, national, international, etc.)

v.HOME_BASED: The flight is operated with an aircraft currently stationed at the airport in question.

CodePCNMethod.d: A code indicating the method used in the evaluation of a PCN number.

CodePCNTyrePressure.d: A code indicating the maximum allowable tyre pressure category related to a PCN number.

v.X: Medium: Pressure limited to 1.5 MPa (217 psi).
v.Y: Low: Pressure limited to 1.00 MPa (145 psi).
v.Z: Very low: Pressure limited to 0.50 MPa (73 psi).

CodePCNSubgrade.d: A code indicating the sub-grade strength category related to a PCN number.

CodePCNPavement.d: A code indicating the pavement behaviour (rigid or flexible) used for the ACN determination.

CodeProcedurePhase.d: A code indicating a phase of a SID, STAR or IAP.

CodeSurfacePreparation.d: A code indicating the preparation technique for a surface area.

v.NON_GROOVED: This covers such items as 'APSHALT NON GROOVED' .
v.WIRE_COMB: Wire Comb or Wire Tine Surface Treatment.

CodeApronSection.d: A code indicating a location on the surface of an apron. For example: apron edge.

CodePositionInILS.d: A code indicating a position in the ILS system. For example, outer, middle, inner, backcourse.

CodeSide.d: A code describing a position, relative to an axis. For example: left/right of runway centreline.

v.LEFT: On the left side of the axis.
v.RIGHT: On the right side of the axis.
v.BOTH: Distributed on both sides of the axis.

CodeRunwaySection.d: A code indicating the position of an item on a surface of a runway. Eg: THR, runway end, runway centre line, TDZ, etc.

v.1_THIRD: The first third of the runway, starting from the threshold with the lower designation number.
v.2_THIRD: The second third of the runway, starting from the threshold with the lower designation number.
v.3_THIRD: The last third of the runway, starting from the threshold with the lower designation number.
v.LAHSO: Designates the Land and Hold Short Operation on a runway.

CodeTLOFSection.d: A code indicating the position of an item on the surface of a Touch Down and Lift-off Area.

CodeTaxiwaySection.d: A code indicating the position of an item on the surface of a taxiway.

CodeFlightPurpose.d: A coded list of values indicating the nature of a flight (scheduled, non-scheduled, private, etc.)

v.SCHEDULED: A commercial flight (carrying passenger or cargo for a pay) that takes place in accordance with an airlines published regular timetable, as opposed to a charter flight or special flight.
v.NON_SCHEDULED: A commercial charter or special flight executed by an airline, not published in a regular timetable.
v.PRIVATE: A flight executed for the benefit of the aircraft owner and not for commercial purpose.
v.AIR_TRAINING: A flight executed in order to develop or test the flying skills of the crew on board the aircraft.
v.AIR_WORK: Operations in which an aircraft is used for specialized services.
v.PARTICIPANT: Aircraft participating in a specified activity.

CodeLocationQualifier.d: A code qualifying a location (such as an airspace, airport/heliport, point, etc.) in relation with a flight or with its availability.

CodeATCReporting.d: A code indicating the type of position report required by an ATC Unit. Eg.: compulsory or on request.

CodeRNP.d: A code indicating the value of the required navigation performance.

CodeRouteAvailability.d: A code indicating the route segment availability.

v.OPEN: the route segment may be flown according to its timetable.
v.COND: Conditional use, depending on special circumstances or specific permissions.

CodeRVSMPointRole.d: A code indicating that the point has a specific role in the RVSM context.

CodeSpecialDate.d: A code indicating the type of a special date, such as 'holiday', 'busy Friday', etc.

v.BUSY_FRI: Busy Friday. note: The main usage is related to conditional weekend routes, when early access is allowed on Friday these routes. Such 'busy Fridays' are typically declared in AIP Supplements.

CodeSpeedReference.d: A code indicating the reference system for a speed value.

CodeTimeEvent.d: A code indicating an event occurrence during any day. For example, sunrise, sunset.

v.BMCT: Beginning of morning civil twilight, which is the time when the centre of the sun’s disc is 6 degrees below the horizon.
v.EECT: End of evening civil twilight, which is the time when the centre of the sun’s disc is 6 degrees below the horizon.

CodeTimeReference.d: A coded indication of a time reference system - UTC or local.

CodeAircraft.d: A code indicating the type of an aircraft

CodeAircraftEngine.d: A code indicating the type of aircraft engine (for example, jet, piston, turbo).

CodeAirportHeliport.d: A code specifying whether a particular entity occurrence is an airport or heliport.

CodeAirportHeliportCollocation.d: A code indicating the extent of collocation between two airports/heliports.

v.FULL: Full collocation, there is only one airport/heliport.
v.RWY: The two aerodromes share all their RWYs and TWYs, but not their aprons.
v.PARTIAL: The two airport/heliports share all their RWYs and TWYs, but not their aprons.
v.UNILATERAL: Unilateral co-location, the RWYs, the TWYs and the aprons of the 1st airport/heliport are available to traffic on the 2nd airport/heliport.
v.SEPARATED: Separated. Even if it is physically possible for an aircraft to taxi between the two airport/heliport manoeuvring areas, this is not operationally allowed.

CodeGroundLighting.d: A code indicating a type of aeronautical ground light. For example, Marine, RWY BCN, ABN, IBN, etc.

v.HAZ_BCN: An aeronautical beacon used to designate a danger to air navigation.

CodeApproachLighting.d: A regional or organisation specific classification of the Runway approach lighting system equipment. Could also be a brand name.

v.ALSAF: 3000 Foot high intensity Approach Lighting System with Sequenced Flashing Lights.
v.MALS: 1400 Foot Medium Intensity Approach Lighting System.
v.MALSR: 1400 Foot Medium Intensity Approach Lighting System with Runway Alignment Indicator Lights.
v.SSALR: Simplified Short Approach Lighting System with Runway Alignment Indicator Lights.
v.AFOVRN: US Air Force Overrun 1000 Foot Standard Approach Lighting System.

CodeBearing.d: A code indicating the type of angle: magnetic, bearing, VOR radial.

CodeAirspace.d: A coded list of values that indicates a type of airspace.

v.NAS: National Airspace System. [note: The airspace within which a State provides Air Traffic Services is usually composed of:1) the territories over which the State has jurisdiction;2) those portions of the airspace over the high seas or in airspace of undetermined sovereignty where the provision of ATS are provided as determined by regional agreements. It can usually be determined by the UNION of FIRs (including, where appropriate, NO-FIRs) of the UNION of NAS-P. .]
v.FIR: Flight information region. Airspace of defined dimensions within which flight information service and alerting service are provided. Description: ICAO Recognized. Might, for example, be used if service provided by more than one unit.
v.UIR: Upper flight information region. An upper airspace of defined dimensions within which flight information service and alerting service are provided. Description: Non-ICAO Recognized. Each state determines its definition for upper airspace.
v.UIR_P: Part of a UIR. [note: Might, for example, be used if more than one Unit provide service in different parts of a UIR .]
v.CTA: Control area. A controlled airspace extending upwards from a specified limit above the earth. Description: ICAO Recognized.
v.OCA: Oceanic control area. A Control Area extending upwards in the upper airspace. Description: Non-ICAO Recognized.
v.UTA: Upper control area. A Control Area extending upwards in the upper airspace. Description: Non-ICAO Recognized.
v.TMA: Terminal control area. Control area normally established at the confluence of ATS routes in the vicinity of one or more major airport/heliports.
v.CTR: Control zone. A controlled airspace extending upwards from the surface of the earth to a specified upper limit. Description: ICAO Recognized.
v.SECTOR: Control sector. A subdivision of a designated control area within which responsibility is assigned to one controller or to a small group of controllers. Description: ICAO Recognized.
v.TSA: Temporary segregated area (FUA). Airspace of pre-defined dimensions within which activities require the reservation of airspace for the exclusive use of specific users during a predetermined period of time. Description: (NATO) An area in which there are special restrictive measures employed to prevent or minimize interference between friendly forces. An area under military jurisdiction in which special security measures are employed to prevent unauthorized entry.
v.CBA: Cross border area (FUA). Airspace of defined dimensions, above the land areas or territorial waters of more than one state. Description: Non-ICAO Recognized. Mainly used in Europe under the Flexible Use of Airspace concept.
v.RCA: Reduced co-ordination area (FUA). Portion of airspace of defined dimensions within which general aviation traffic is permitted "off-route" without requiring general aviation traffic controllers to initiate co-ordination with OAT controllers. Description: Non-ICAO Recognized. Mainly used in Europe under the Flexible Use of Airspace concept.
v.AWY: Airway (corridor). A control area or portion thereof established in the form of a corridor.
v.MTR: Military Training Route buffer. A control area or portion thereof, established in the form of a corridor around a military training route in order to protect it from other traffic.
v.P: Prohibited area. Airspace of defined dimensions, above the land areas or territorial waters of a State, within which the flight of aircraft is prohibited. Description: ICAO Recognized.
v.R: Restricted area. Airspace of defined dimensions, above the land areas or territorial waters of a State, within which the flight of aircraft is restricted in accordance with certain specified conditions. Description: ICAO Recognized.
v.D: Danger area. Airspace of defined dimensions within which activities dangerous to the flight of aircraft may exist at specified times. Description: ICAO Recognized.
v.ADIZ: Air Defence Identification Zone. Special designated airspace of defined dimensions within which aircraft are required to comply with special identification and/or reporting procedures additional to those related to the provision of air traffic services (ATS). Description: ICAO Recognized.
v.NO_FIR: Airspace for which not even an FIR is defined. [note: There are parts in the world for which there is neither an FIR nor any other airspace-type is defined. These airspaces will be marked as NO-FIR .]
v.PART: Part of an airspace (used in airspace aggregation).
v.D_OTHER: Activities of dangerous nature (other than a danger area).
v.TRA: Temporary reserved area (FUA). Airspace of pre-defined dimensions within which activities require the reservation of airspace during a predetermined period of time. Description: Non-ICAO Recognized. Mainly used in Europe under the Flexible Use of Airspace concept.
v.A: Alert area. Airspace which may contain a high volume of pilot training activities or unusual type of aerial activity, neither of which is hazardous to aircraft. Description: Non-ICAO Recognized. Mainly used in contiguous United States and its territories.
v.W: Warning area. A non-regulatory airspace of defined dimensions designated over international waters that contains activity which may be hazardous to aircraft not participating in the activity. The purpose of such warning areas is to warn non participating pilots of the potential danger. Description: Non-ICAO Recognized. Mainly used in contiguous United States and its territories.
v.PROTECT: Airspace protected from specific air traffic.
v.AMA: Minimum altitude area. The lowest altitude to be used under instrument meteorological conditions (IMC) which will provide a minimum vertical clearance of 300 m (1 000 ft) or in designated mountainous terrain 600 m (2 000 ft) above all obstacles located in the area specified. Description: ICAO Recognized. Published by many States as rectangles of 1 x 1 degree on the ENR 6 charts. Note - In the exact calculation 984 feet can be used as an equivalent to 300 metres.
v.ASR: Altimeter setting region. Airspace of defined dimensions within which standardized altimeter setting procedures apply. Description: Non-ICAO Recognized. For example, during flight the altimeter shall be set to the current altimeter setting of the nearest station along the route of flight.
v.ADV: Advisory Area. An area of defined dimensions within which air traffic advisory service is available. Description: ICAO Recognized. Air traffic control service provides a much more complete service than air traffic advisory service; advisory areas and routes are therefore not established within controlled airspace, but air traffic advisory service may be provided below and above.
v.UADV: Upper Advisory Area. An area of defined dimensions in upper airspace within which air traffic advisory service is available. Description: ICAO Recognized. Air traffic control service provides a much more complete service than air traffic advisory service; advisory areas and routes are therefore not established within controlled airspace, but air traffic advisory service may be provided below and above.
v.ATZ: Airport Traffic Zone. Airspace of defined dimensions established around an airport for the protection of airport traffic. Description: ICAO Recognized.
v.ATZ_P: Part of an airport traffic zone
v.NAS_P: A part of a national airspace system
v.NTZ: No transgression zone. A corridor of airspace of defined dimensions located centrally between the two extended runway centre lines, where a penetration by an aircraft requires a controller intervention to manoeuvre any threatened aircraft on the adjacent approach in the context of independent parallel approaches.
v.NOZ: Normal operating zone. Airspace of defined dimensions extending to either side of an ILS localizer course and/or MLS final approach track used in the context of independent parallel approaches.

CodeAuthority.d: A code indicating the type of responsibility that one organisation/authority has for an aeronautical feature (for example, an airspace).

v.OWN: An authority has the legal right of possession and proprietorship over the feature.
v.DLGT: An authority is assigned or entrusted with the responsibility for that feature.
v.AIS: The organization is responsible for the provision of aeronautical information in relation with that feature.

CodeAirspacePointRole.d: A code indicating the type of association between a significant point and an airspace. For example, entry point, exit point, etc..

v.ENTRY: The first reporting point, determined by reference to a significant point, over which an aircraft passes or is expected to pass upon entering an airspace.
v.EXIT: Exit point. The last reporting point, determined by reference to a significant point, over which an aircraft passes or is expected to pass before leaving an airspace.
v.ENTRY_EXIT: Entry/exit point. The first or the last reporting point, determined by reference to a significant point, over which an aircraft passes or is expected to pass upon entering or before leaving an airspace.

CodeOrganisationHierarchy.d: The values indicating the type of association between two organisations/authorities.

v.MEMBER: Child ORG is a member of the parent ORG.
v.OWNED_BY: Indicates that the current feature is hierarchically positioned immediately below the parent organisation.
v.SUPERVISED_BY: Indicates that the current feature is under the supervision of the parent organisation.

CodeMLSAzimuth.d: A code indicating the type of azimuth equipment: normal or backward.

CodeCourse.d: A code indicating the type of course to be observed. For example, true track, magnetic track, heading, VOR radial, true bearing, magnetic bearing.

v.TRUE_TRACK: True track. The projection on the earth’s surface of the path of an aircraft, the direction of which path at any point is expressed in degrees from true North. (Source: ICAO Doc 8168, Vol. II, Definitions)
v.MAG_TRACK: Magnetic Track. The projection on the earth’s surface of the path of an aircraft, the direction of which path at any point is expressed in degrees from magnetic North.(Source: ICAO Doc 8168, Vol. II, Definitions)
v.TRUE_BRG: True bearing. The direction of the aircraft position to / from a reference position (e.g. a NAVAID, a SignificantPoint, etc.), expressed in degrees from true North.
v.MAG_BRG: Magnetic bearing. The direction of the aircraft position to / from a reference position (e.g. a NAVAID, a SignificantPoint, etc.), expressed in degrees from magnetic North..
v.RDL: Radial. The direction (bearing) indicated by the VOR signal at a given point, expressed in degrees, from the position of the VOR. (Source: adaptation of ICAO Annex 10, Vol. I, App. C, 3.7.2 a)
v.TRUE_COURSE: True course. The intended direction of travel of an aircraft, expressed in degrees from true North. (Source: ICAO Doc 8168, Vol. II, Definitions)
v.MAG_COURSE: Magnetic course. The intended direction of travel of an aircraft, expressed in degrees from magnetic North.(Source: ICAO Doc 8168, Vol. II, Definitions)
v.TRUE_HDG: True heading. The direction in which the longitudinal axis of an aircraft is pointed, expressed in degrees from true North. (Source: ICAO Doc 8168, Vol. II, Definitions)
v.MAG_HDG: Magnetic heading. The direction in which the longitudinal axis of the aircraft is pointed, expressed in degrees from magnetic North. (Source: ICAO Doc 8168, Vol. II, Definitions)

CodeDeclaredDistance.d: A code indicating the type of conventional declared distance for a runway. For example, TORA, TODA, LDA, etc...

v.DTHR: Threshold displacement (from the physical start of the runway direction).

CodeDesignatedPoint.d: A code indicating a specific type of designated point, in direct relation with the designator allocated to that point.

v.COORD: Point with identifier derived from its geographical coordinates.
v.CNF: Computer Navigation Fix as specified in the FAA Order 8260.19I.
v.DESIGNED: A point with bearing/distance designator used as control point for procedure design, which is not published.
v.MTR: Point used on a military training route.
v.TERMINAL: Point with a designator consisting of a maximum of five alphanumeric characters, which is unique in the context of the terminal area where it is used and which may not be globally unique.
v.BRG_DIST: Point with a five-alphanumeric name-code, composed according to the rules provided by the ARINC 424 Specification for unnamed bearing/distance reference waypoints.
v.VRP: A Visual Reference Point for which the designator is derived from a named geographical location or composed according to local rules, sometimes based on its relative position from an airport/heliport or from a geographical location.

CodeDME.d: A code indicating the type of UHF distance measuring equipment.

v.PRECISION: DME/P, improved accuracy compared to DME/N

CodeFlightRule.d: Flight rules to be observed by aircraft. For example, VFR and/or IFR.

CodeGeoBorder.d: The type of geographical border. The most common situation is the border between two countries.

CodeHoldingUsage.d: A code indicating the type of holding procedure. For example, en-route holding, terminal area holding.

CodeLightSource.d: A code indicating a type of light source, such as strobe or flood.

v.FLOOD: Flood light. [note: This indicates that the light source contains a large powerful lamp that produces a strong broad beam of artificial light and is used to illuminate the outside at night. .]
v.STROBE: Strobe light. [note: This indicates that the light source contains a high intensity flashing beam of light produced by charging a capacitor to a very high voltage then discharging it as a high-intensity flash of light in a tube. .]

CodeMilitaryOperations.d: A code indicating in terms of civil or military, the type of operations.

v.CIVIL: Only Civil Air traffic is concerned.
v.MIL: Only Military Air traffic is concerned.
v.JOINT: Both Civil and Military air traffic are concerned.

CodeRadioFrequencyArea.d: A code indicating the type of radio navigation aid limitation.

v.COV: The volume of airspace within which the radio signal is reliably received to the level specified by the applicable standards.
v.T_COV: Theoretical coverage range (not flight checked). Equivalent to Standard Service Volume.
v.RES: Restricted (use is restricted to defined sectors).
v.UUS: Un-usability (use is not permitted in the defined sectors).
v.ESV: Extended Service Volume. Reception limits which are usable for unpublished route navigation and which are flight checked to confirm these limits of coverage (source: FAA Flight Inspection Handbook).
v.DOC: Designated Operational Coverage. the airspace where the frequency assignment planning process provides protection from other assignments (source EUR DOC 7754 - EUR ANP, VOLUME II, FASID).
v.SSV: Standard Service Volume. Defines the reception limits of unrestricted navaid which are usable for random/unpublished route navigation.
v.ASV: Approach Service Volume. Designates sectors of circle aligned with the final approach paths, where the signal satisfies the applicable standards.

CodeNitrogen.d: A code describing the type of nitrogen supplies for aviation usage.

v.LHNG: Low and high pressure nitrogen servicing.
v.NG: Indicates nitrogen servicing when type of servicing is unspecified.

CodeNorthReference.d: A code indicating the type of the North reference used.

v.GRID: The direction of the north-south lines of the Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM) grid imposed on topographic maps by the United States and NATO.

CodeOrganisation.d: A code indicating the type of an Organisation/Authority. For example, State, Association of States, International Organisation, etc..

CodeOxygen.d: A code describing the type of oxygen supplies for aviation usage.

v.LHOX: Low and high pressure oxygen servicing.
v.OX: Indicates oxygen servicing when type of servicing is unspecified.

CodeSegmentPath.d: A code that defines a specific type of flight path and a specific type of termination of that flight path. Although we agree with the ARINC idea that procedures should be designed with the aim to permit FMS equipped aircraft to fly tracks instead of procedural headings, for the time being we must allow all representation of these procedures (especially reversal procedures) as they are published by the States. This is the explanation of the differences between the allowable values for attributes in this domain and the ARINC leg types.

v.AF: (ARINC) constant DME arc to a fix.
v.HF: (ARINC) hold pattern terminating at a fix after one circuit.
v.HA: (ARINC) hold pattern term. at fix after reach. an altitude.
v.PI: (ARINC) procedure turn followed by a course to a fix (CF).
v.PT: (non ARINC) timed outbound leg to a procedure turn.
v.CI: (ARINC) course to next leg followed by course oriented leg.
v.DF: (ARINC) Computed track direct to a fix.
v.FA: (ARINC) course from a fix to an altitude.
v.FC: (ARINC) course from a fix to a distance.
v.FT: (non ARINC) course from a fix during a specified time.
v.FM: (ARINC) course from a fix to a manual termination.
v.FD: (ARINC) course from a fix to a DME distance.

CodeRunwayProtectionArea.d: A code indicating the type of protection area for a runway For example, clearway, obstacle free zone, ILS protection area, etc..

v.IOFZ: Inner Obstacle free zone or surface
v.ILS: ILS protection area. Protects ILS signal distortion by forbidding large objects in the area.
v.VGSI: Visual Glide Slope Indicator (VGSI) protection area. Protects VGSI signal coverage by forbidding objects in the area.
v.STOPWAY: A defined rectangular area on the ground at the end of take-off run available prepared as a suitable area in which an aircraft can be stopped in the case of an abandoned take-off.

CodeFlightRestriction.d: A code indicating if the restriction is an interdiction or a mandatory routing.

v.CLSD: Closed for cruising. [note: It is allowed to climb or descend through the levels associated with the restriction but it is not allowed to fly straight and level on the said levels, in any part of the route. .]
v.ALLOWED: Flight that comply with the condition are explicitly permitted to use the associated routings, even if other more general flight restrictions forbid the routings (for the same flight conditions).

CodeRouteNavigation.d: The type of the route from the navigation point of view. For example, conventional, RNAV, etc..

CodeRouteSegmentPath.d: A code indicating the type of segment path.

CodeAircraftGroundService.d: A code indicating a type of service provided to aircraft on the ground.

CodeSpecialNavigationStation.d: A code indicating the type of service provided by a station in a special navigation system chain, depending on the type of the system.

v.MASTER: Master station of a LORAN or DECCA chain.
v.RED_SLAVE: Red slave station of a DECCA chain.
v.GREEN_SLAVE: Green slave station of a DECCA chain.
v.PURPLE_SLAVE: Purple slave station of a DECCA chain.

CodeSpecialNavigationSystem.d: A code indicating a type of special navigation system. For example, LORAN, DECCA, GNSS, etc.

v.DECCA: Short and medium range (area) navigation system DECCA.

CodeAircraftStand.d: A code indicating the type of stand. For example, parking position on the apron, isolated aircraft stand, terminal building gate, etc..

CodeTaxiway.d: A code indicating a type of taxiway. For example, normal taxiway, apron taxiway, air taxiway, etc..

v.CHANNEL: A defined path on a water aerodrome, intended for the use of taxing seaplanes.
v.TURNING_BASIN: A water area used for the water taxi maneuvering of seaplanes along shoreline facilities and at the ends of a narrow water runway.

CodeUnit.d: A unit providing particular ATS services.

v.BOF: Briefing office (note: Note ICAO listed by nonetheless used.)
v.MIL: Military station/unit (or military office in general).
v.MILOPS: Planning/briefing office for military flight operations.

CodeILSBackCourse.d: A code indicating the usability of the localizer signal in the back-course sector.

CodeVASIS.d: A code indicating a type of visual approach slope indicator system. For example, VASIS, AVASIS, 3-BAR VASIS, PAPI, APAPI, etc..

v.AVASIS: Abbreviated visual approach slow indicator system.
v.PVASI: Pulsating/steady burning visual approach slope indicator, normally a single light unit projecting two colours.
v.TRCV: Tri-colour visual approach slope indicator, normally a single light unit projecting three colours.
v.ILU: A number of identical light units.
v.OLS: Optical landing system for strip decks and aircraft carriers (sometimes available on ground air bases for training purposes).
v.LCVASI: Low cost visual approach slope indicator: 3 sets of 4 white lights on 3 mounts usually on only one side of the runway.

CodeUsageLimitation.d: A code indicating whether a limitation is of type permission, interdiction or exclusive usage.

v.CONDITIONAL: Permission but with additional instructions. Failure to comply with the additional instructions invalidates the permission.

CodeYesNo.d: A code for a logical value: Yes or No.

CodeStatusConstruction.d: A code indicating the status of the construction of a Vertical Structure.

v.IN_DEMOLITION: Work in progress to remove the item.
Work in progress to remove the item.

v.DOWNGRADED: The system is theoretically able to work at a higher level of service, but it is currently limited to the level described.
