CodeVerticalStructure.d: A code indicating the type of vertical structure.

v.COMPRESSED_AIR_SYSTEM: The components of a compressed air system. AirMAT.
v.CONTROL_MONITORING_SYSTEM: The components of an electronic monitoring and control system (EMCS) including cables, devices, and so on. AirMAT.
v.ELECTRICAL_EXIT_LIGHT: The components of an electrical exterior lighting system including cables, switches, devices, transformers, and so on. Does not include field, navaid, or approach lighting. AirMAT.
v.ELECTRICAL_SYSTEM: The components of an electrical distribution system including cables, switches, devices, motors, transformers, and so on. AirMAT.
v.FUEL_SYSTEM: The components of a fuel distribution system consisting of pipes, fittings, fixtures, pumps, tanks, and so on. AirMAT.
v.GATE: Area of a fence which may be opened for passage through the fence or closed to prevent passage through the fence.
v.GENERAL_UTILITY: The components of utility system which are universal in use and purpose and do not belong to a specific utility. AirMAT.
v.HEAT_COOL_SYSTEM: The components of a heating and cooling distribution system consisting of pipes, fittings, fixtures, and so on. AirMAT.
v.INDUSTRIAL_SYSTEM: The components of an industrial waste collection system including pipes, fittings, fixtures, tanks, lagoons, and so on. AirMAT.
v.NATURAL_GAS_SYSTEM: The components of a natural gas distribution system consisting of pipes, fittings, fixtures, and so on. AirMAT.
v.SALTWATER_SYSTEM: The components of a salt water collection system. AirMAT.
v.STORM_SYSTEM: The components of a storm drainage collection system including pipes, fittings, fixtures, and so on. AirMAT.
v.WASTEWATER_SYSTEM: The components of a wastewater collection system including pipes, fittings, fixtures, treatment plants, collection locations, and so forth. AirMAT.
v.WATER_SYSTEM: The components of a water system including pipes, fittings, fixtures, treatment plants, and so on. AirMAT.
v.RECREATIONAL_STRUCTURE: Recreational structure (roller coaster, water slide, ferris wheel).
v.TELEPHONE_LINE: Telegraph or telephone line (when a landmark).

CodeVerticalStructureMarking.d: A code indicating the type and pattern of markings on a vertical structure.

v.MONOCOLOUR: Markings painted as a single colour.
v.CHEQUERED: Markings painted in a chequered pattern.
v.MARKERS: Marks attached to cables or wires.

CodeCardinalDirection.d: An angle expressed as compass directions.

CodeFreeFlight.d: Code classifying entry and exit points for free flight zones.

v.PITCH: The free flight PITCH point indicating the start of free flight.
v.CATCH: Free flight CATCH point indicating the end of free flight.

v.MLS_DME: MLS with collocated DME. See NavaidComponent collocationGroup
v.NDB_MKR: Non-Directional Radio Beacon and Marker Beacon

v.EGM_96: (ICAO Doc 9674) Earth gravitational model 1996. ICAO recommended vertical datum.

CodeRouteDesignatorPrefix.d: (ICAO) A prefix for route designators. Note: Includes a non-ICAO value, used for military TACAN routes.

CodeRVSM.d: A code indicating that reduced vertical separation minima is applied in the column or not.

CodeRouteDesignatorLetter.d: (ICAO) A one character designator for the route.

CodeRouteDesignatorSuffix.d: (ICAO) A suffix for the route designator.

v.F: (ICAO) Advisory service only is provided on a portion of the route.
v.G: (ICAO) Flight information service only on a portion of the route.

CodeStatusAirspace.d: A coded list of values indicating the activation status of an Airspace.

v.ACTIVE: The airspace is active (but it might not be in use yet).
v.IN_USE: The airspace is actually used inside the activation period.
v.INTERMITTENT: The Airspace is active but with periods of no real usage.

CodeRunwayPointRole.d: Role of the Runway Centreline Point.

v.START: Physical start of a runway direction.
v.MID: The mid point of the runway
v.END: Physical end of a runway direction
v.LAHSO: Point indicating Land And Hold Short Operation location
v.ABEAM_GLIDESLOPE: The point perpendicular to the Glideslope Antenna on the Runway Centreline. Also known as the Aiming Point.
v.ABEAM_PAR: The point perpendicular to the Precision Approach Radar (PAR) Antenna on the Runway Centreline.
v.ABEAM_ELEVATION: The point perpendicular to the Elevation Antenna on the Runway Centreline.
v.ABEAM_TDR: The point perpendicular to the Touchdown Reflector (TDR) on the Runway Centreline.
v.ABEAM_RER: The point perpendicular to the Runway End Reflector (RER) on the Runway Centreline.

CodeRunway.d: A code that makes a distinction between runways for airplanes and FATO for helicopters.

v.FATO: Final Approach and Take Off Area for helicopters
v.WATER_RWY: A defined rectangular area on a water aerodrome, intended for the landing and take-off of seaplanes along its length.

CodeMarkingStyle.d: A coded list of values indicating styles of painted lines.

CodeFinalGuidance.d: Codes describing the guidance used on the final approach segment of an instrument approach procedure.

v.LPV: An LPV approach is classified as an APV procedure based on the lateral OCS dimensions of the precision approach trapezoid, with vertical guidance provided by the WAAS where the VAL is greater than 12 and less than or equal to 50 meters. These procedures are published on RNAV Global Positioning System (GPS) approach charts as the LPV minima line.
v.LNAV: Lateral navigation (LNAV) . The lateral navigation without positive vertical guidance. This type of navigation is associated with nonprecision approach procedures.
v.ILS_DME: Instrument landing system with Direction measuring equipment
v.ILS_PRM: Instrument landing system using a Precision runway monitor
v.LDA_DME: Localizer Type Directional Aid with Distance Measuring Equipment.
v.LOC_DME_BC: Localizer with Distance Measuring Equipment Back Course.
v.MLS_DME: Microwave Landing System with Distance Measuring Equipment.
v.NDB_DME: Non-Directional Beacon with Distance Measuring Equipment.
v.VOR_DME: VHF Omnidirectional Radio with Distance Measuring Equipment.
v.VORTAC: VHF Omnidirectional Radio with UHF Tactical Air Navigation beacon
v.LP: A Localizer Performance (LP) approach is an RNAV non-vertically guided approach procedure evaluated using the lateral obstacle evaluation area dimensions of the precision localizer trapezoid, with adjustments specific to the WAAS. These procedures are published on RNAV GPS approaches as the LP minima line.

v.SECONDARY: An alternate missed approach to be used instead of primary.
v.ALTERNATE: A missed approach to be used when directed by ATC.
v.TACAN: A missed approach to be used when using TACAN guidance.
v.TACANALT: An alternate missed approach to be used instead of TACAN missed approach when directed by ATC.
v.ENGINEOUT: Missed Approach to be used when Engine Out

CodeApproachPrefix.d: Code indicating the prefix used in support of current approach procedure naming conventions

v.HI: Approach procedures with segments such as a high altitude teardrop penetration that are within the high airspace stratum, requested by Military. Normally C, D and E Minimums only.
v.CONVERGING: Parallel or joining operation with parallel or joining ILS courses

CodeApproach.d: A code describing the type of instrument approach procedure.

v.ILS_DME: Instrument landing system with Direction measuring equipment
v.ILS_PRM: Instrument landing system using a Precision runway monitor
v.LDA_DME: Localizer Type Directional Aid with Distance Measuring Equipment.
v.LOC_DME_BC: Localizer with Distance Measuring Equipment back course
v.MLS_DME: Microwave Landing System with Distance Measuring Equipment.
v.NDB_DME: Non-Directional Beacon with Distance Measuring Equipment.
v.VOR_DME: VHF Omnidirectional Radio with Distance Measuring Equipment.
v.VORTAC: VHF Omnidirectional Radio with UHF Tactical Air Navigation beacon
v.DME_DME: Distance Measuring Equipment with Distance Measuring Equipment.

CodeDesignStandard.d: A code indicating the rules used to design and evaluate terminal procedures

CodeApproachEquipmentAdditional.d: A code indicating the additional equipment needed to fly the procedure not listed in approachType

v.SPECIAL: al aircraft and aircrew certification required
v.DUALADF_DME: DME and dual ADF required for LOC approach

CodeEquipmentUnavailable.d: A code to indicate the type of unavailable equipment

CodeHoldingUse.d: A code to identify the holding is used by a segment

v.PT: The holding pattern is used as a procedure turn. (Commonly referred to as Holding in Lieu of Procedure Turn.)
v.ARRIVAL: Arrival holding. A holding pattern provided at any Initial Approach Fix (IAF) and should be aligned with the initial segment track.
v.MISSED_APPROACH: Missed Approach Holding. A holding pattern provided at the end of the missed approach
v.CLIMB: A holding pattern used in conjunction with climb and hold instructions.
v.ATC: A holding pattern defined specifically for ATC use.

CodeProcedureDistance.d: Indicates the distance and altitude type associated with an approach procedure.

CodeMinimaFinalApproachPath.d: Code indicating final approach path type for establishing valid set of minima on a procedure.

v.STRAIGHT_IN: Final approach path is straight in to a landing surface (S 9R). [FAAO 8260.3] A descent in an approved procedure where the navigation facility alignment is normally on the runway centreline, and glide slope (GS) information is provided.
v.CIRCLING: Final approach path is circling above the airport. [ICAO] Circling approach. An extension of an instrument approach procedure which provides for visual circling of the airport/heliport prior to landing.
v.SIDESTEP: [FAAO 8260.19] A sidestep manoeuvre is the visual alignment manoeuvre, required by a pilot executing an approach to one runway and cleared to land on a parallel runway.

CodeMinimumAltitude.d: A code classifying altitudes for approach procedure minima.

v.OCA: [ICAO] Obstacle clearance altitude (OCA). The lowest altitude used in establishing compliance with appropriate obstacle clearance criteria.
v.DA: Decision altitude (DA). [FAAO 8260.3] A specified altitude in reference to mean sea level in an approach with vertical guidance at which a missed approach must be initiated if the required visual references to continue the approach have not been established.
v.MDA: [ICAO] Minimum descent altitude (MDA). A specified altitude in a non-precision approach or circling approach below which descent must not be made without the required visual reference.

CodeMinimumHeight.d: A code classifying heights for approach procedure minima.

v.DH: [ICAO] Decision height. A specified height in the precision approach or approach with vertical guidance at which a missed approach must he initiated if the required visual reference to continue the approach has not been established.
v.OCH: [ICAO] Obstacle clearance height (OCH). The lowest height above the elevation of the relevant runway threshold or the aerodrome elevation as applicable, used in establishing compliance with appropriate obstacle clearance criteria.
v.MDH: [ICAO] Minimum descent height. A specified height in a nonprecision approach or circling approach below which descent must not be made without the required visual reference.

CodeProcedureCodingStandard.d: Code indicating the standard used to encode the approach procedure.

CodeSafeAltitude.d: A code indicating the type of altitude used, MSA or ESA.

CodeObstacleAssessmentSurface.d: A code indicating the type of surface assessment. Used for indicating assessment surfaces used in design and evaluation activities such as approach procedure design.

v.VISUAL: Visual area (typically 20:1 or 34:1 surfaces in TERPS, the slope is defined by the ObstacleAssessmentSurface slope element).
v.OCS: Obstacle Clearance Surface (the slope is defined by the ObstacleAssessmentSurface slope element).
v.OIS: Obstacle Identification Surface - Eliminated Obstacles (typically a 7:1 surface in TERPS, the slope is defined by the ObstacleAssessmentSurface slope element).
v.PDA: Preliminary Decision Altitude area. A level surface in the Final Approach areas of an LNAV/VNAV approach.
v.SEGMENT: A segment area (includes primary and secondary areas) assessed to determine the minimum obstruction clearance altitude.
v.SECTOR: A sector surface (used for MSA/ESA, TAA areas) assessed to determine the minimum obstruction clearance altitude.
v.SECTION_1_OCS: The initial Obstacle Clearance Surface of a missed approach (typically ends when an aircraft would be at 400 ft AGL).
v.SECTION_2_OCS: The Obstacle Clearance Surface of a missed approach that follows Section 1.
v.VISUAL_20_1: VISUAL_20_1 (20:1 = 5.00% slope) (assessment applies to all aircraft categories for straight-in approaches).
v.VISUAL_34_1: VISUAL_34_1 (34:1 = 2.94% slope) (assessment applies to all aircraft categories).
v.VISUAL_BUFFER_OIS: Visual segment buffer Obstacle Identification Surface (OIS).

CodeAltitudeAdjustment.d: A code indicating the type of adjustment used to produce a usable altitude.

v.HAA: Minimum required HAA (height above airport) calculated, round to a reportable value, and applied for charted
v.MA: Missed approach due to obstacle penetration of missed approach slope (segment assessment area)
v.GS: Glideslope - adjustment to set altitude at glideslope intercept
v.SA: Secondary area (also X/y surfaces, transition areas)
v.AAO: Adverse Assumption Obstruction. Designates adjustment to a terrain value to account for natural vegetation growth, uncharted cell phone towers, buildings, and other man-made obstructions.
v.VA: Vegetation Allowance. Designates an adjustment to a terrain value to account for natural vegetation growth.

CodeTAA.d: Indicates one of the three area types of the Terminal Arrival Area.

CodeArcDirection.d: A code indicating the direction of an arc (clockwise or counterclockwise).

CodeLevelSeries.d: A series of predefined levels. For example Odd, Even.

v.ODD_HALF: Intermediate flight levels, above odd levels (15, 35, 55, 75, ...)
v.EVEN_HALF: Intermediate flight levels, above even levels (5, 25, 45, 65, ...)

CodeSegmentTermination.d: A code indicating the end point of a terminal procedure segment leg.

v.ALTITUDE: Leg is terminated when reaching the altitude conditions specified in the segment leg.
v.DISTANCE: Leg is terminated when the distance has passed.
v.DURATION: Leg is terminated when the duration has passed.
v.INTERCEPT: Leg is terminated when reaching the limiting angle indication.
v.ALTITUDE_AND_DISTANCE: Used to indicate that the leg has a conditional altitude termination, meaning the SegmentLeg ends as specified by the distance or at or above the altitude specified, under the condition indicated. Condition is whichever is later (altitude and reaching DME distance/flight distance).
v.ALTITUDE_OR_DISTANCE: Used to indicate that the leg has a conditional altitude termination, meaning the SegmentLeg ends as specified by the distance or at or above the altitude specified, under the condition indicated. Condition is whichever is earlier (altitude or reaching DME distance/flight distance).
v.DME_DISTANCE: Leg is terminated when reaching the limiting distance indication defined by a DME associated with the leg.

CodeReferenceRole.d: A list describing the valid Point Reference makeups for use by navigation receivers.

v.INTERSECTION: An intersection is where two or more "things" cross. An intersection will be the intersection of two angle indications or two distance indications (DME/DME fix). The indications must reference different navaids.
v.RECNAV: The recommended navaid providing information for the segment. Used for ARINC leg types that need navaid information other then what is supplied by standard angle and distance indications.
v.ATD: Along Track Distance. Defined the distance along the guidance course to/from another significant point.
v.RAD_DME: Defined by a bearing (angle indication) and a distance (distance Indication) from a navaid.

CodeTrajectory.d: A code classifying the trajectory of a segment path.

CodeRunwayMarking.d: Type of runway marking related to landing categories such as precision, non-precision and basic.

v.PRECISION: Markings appropriate for precision approach runway. Precision Instrument runway marking elements include markings for Runway Designation, Centreline, Threshold, Aiming Point, Touchdown Zone and Side Stripes.
v.NONPRECISION: Markings appropriate for non-precision approach runway. Non-Precision Instrument runway marking elements include markings for Runway designation, Centreline, threshold and Aiming Point.
v.BASIC: Basic (or Visual) runway marking elements include markings for Runway Designation, Centreline, Threshold (On runways sued or intended to be used by international commercial transports) and Aiming Point (On runways 4000 ft (1200M) or longer used by jet aircraft).
v.RUNWAY_NUMBERS: The only runway marking element present is the Runway Designation.
v.NON_STANDARD: Runway marking elements such as Runway Designation, Centreline, Threshold and Aiming Point may be present, but they are Not standard markings.
v.HELIPORT: Heliport specific marking elements are present.
v.BUOY: Marking buoys (for waterways and seaplane bases).

CodeRVRReading.d: A code indicating the position where the RVR reading is reported.

CodeStatusNavaid.d: The operational status of a Navaid or NavaidEquipment

v.PARTIAL: Operating with limited capabilities. For example, used when just the DME part of a VOR/DME is working.
v.CONDITIONAL: Operative subject to published limitations or conditions.
v.FALSE_INDICATION: Giving false indication, do not use.
v.FALSE_POSSIBLE: False indication possible, use with caution.
v.UNRELIABLE: Risk of both signal interruption and false information being provided
v.RAIM_NOT_AVBL: Risk of both signal interruption and false information being provided

CodeOperationAirportHeliport.d: A coded identifier indicating an operation executed by an aircraft in relation with an airport/heliport.

CodeDistanceIndication.d: Coding indicating the type of distance indication.

CodeObstacleArea.d: A code indicating the type of obstacle coverage area, according to ICAO Annex 15 or FAA .

v.AREA1: ICAO Area 1: entire territory of a State.
v.AREA2: ICAO Area 2: Obstacles within Area 2 that are assessed as being a hazard to air nav igation (not covered by ICAO Area 2a-d).
v.AREA3: ICAO Area 3: The area bordering an aerodrome movement area that extends horizontally from the edge of a runway to 90 m from the runway centre line and 50 m from the edge of all other parts of the aerodrome movement area.
v.AREA4: ICAO Area 4: The area extending 900 m prior to the runway threshold and 60 m each side of the extended runway centre line in the direction of the approach on a precision approach runway, Category II or III.
v.FAR77: FAA Regulations Part 77 Obstacle Limitation Surfaces.
v.MANAGED: A 'virtual' area containing the VerticalStructures included in the data collection exercise, which do not qualify yet as Obstacles in any specific Area
v.AREA2A: ICAO Area 2a: A rectangular area around a runway that comprises the runway strip plus any clearway that exists.
v.AREA2B: ICAO Area 2b: An area extending from the ends of Area 2a in the direction of departure, with a length of 10 km and a splay of 15 per cent to each side.
v.AREA2C: ICAO Area 2c: An area extending outside Area 2a and Area 2b at a distance of not more than 10 km from the boundary of Area 2a.
v.AREA2D: ICAO Area 2d: An area outside Areas 2a, 2b and 2c up to a distance of 45 km from the aerodrome reference point, or to an existing terminal control area (TMA) boundary, whichever is nearest.
v.AREA2_HAZARD: An area similar to Area 2, but which is used for identifying obstacles that have been assessed as being a hazard to air navigation and which do not match the criteria for being collected as obstacles in Area 2 A/B/C/D.
v.TAKE_OFF_FLIGHT_PATH_AREA: A quadrilateral area starting from the end of a runway or of the clearway, on the surface of the earth lying directly below, and symmetrically disposed about, the take-off flight path.
v.OLS_CONICAL_SURFACE: A surface sloping upwards and outwards from the periphery of the inner horizontal surface.
v.OLS_INNER_HORIZONTAL_SURFACE: A surface located in a horizontal plane above an aerodrome and its environs.
v.OLS_APPROACH_SURFACE: An inclined plane or combination of planes preceding the threshold.
v.OLS_INNER_APPROACH_SURFACE: A rectangular portion of the approach surface immediately preceding the threshold.
v.OLS_TRANSITIONAL_SURFACE: A complex surface along the side of the strip and part of the side of the approach surface, that slopes upwards and outwards to the inner horizontal surface.
v.OLS_INNER_TRANSITIONAL_SURFACE: A surface similar to the transitional surface but closer to the runway.
v.OLS_BALKED_LANDING_SURFACE: An inclined plane located at a specified distance after the threshold, extending between the inner transitional surface.
v.OLS_TAKE_OFF_CLIMB_SURFACE: An inclined plane or other specified surface beyond the end of a runway or clearway.

CodeAirspaceClassification.d: A coded list of values that which determines the operating rules, flight requirements, and services provided in an airspace. According to Annex 11, Appendix 4.

v.A: Class of Airspace per ICAO Annex 11. Appendix 4. IFR flights only are permitted; all flights are provided with air traffic control service and are separated from each other.
v.B: Class of Airspace per ICAO Annex 11. Appendix 4. IFR and VFR flights are permitted; all flights are provided with air traffic control service and are separated from each other.
v.C: Class of Airspace per ICAO Annex 11. Appendix 4. IFR and VFR flights are permitted; all flights are provided with air traffic control service and IFR flights are separated from other IFR flights and from VFR flights. VFR flights are separated from IFR flights and receive traffic information.
v.D: Class of Airspace per ICAO Annex 11. Appendix 4. IFR and VFR flights are permitted and all flights are provided with air traffic control service, IFR flights are separated from other IFR flights and receive traffic information in respect of VFR flights, VFR flights receive traffic information in respect of all other flights.
v.E: Class of Airspace per ICAO Annex 11. Appendix 4. IFR and VFR flights are permitted; IFR flights are provided with air traffic control service and are separated from other IFR flights. All flights receive traffic information as far as is practical. Class E shall not be used for control zones.
v.F: Class of Airspace per ICAO Annex 11. Appendix 4. IFR and VFR flights are permitted, all participating IFR flights receive an air traffic advisory service and all flights receive flight information service if requested. Description: Where air traffic advisory service is implemented, this is considered normally as a temporary measure only until such time as it can be replaced by air traffic control.
v.G: Class of Airspace per ICAO Annex 11. Appendix 4. IFR and VFR flights are permitted and receive flight information service if requested.

CodeApronElement.d: A code indicating the type of Apron.

v.RAMP: Access pavement between maintenance hangers opening to the apron and the apron edge. (AirMAT)
v.CARGO: Cargo Loading Area used for loading and unloading cargo. (AirMAT)
v.HARDSTAND: Area for parking a single aircraft more temporary than a parking area (AirMAT)
v.LOADING: Passenger loading area used for loading/unloading of passengers (AirMAT)
v.TAXILANE: Area where plane is still under terminal control (airline dispatched) as opposed to tower control. (AirMAT)
v.TURNAROUND: Area for aircraft to turn around (AirMAT)
v.SNOW_COLLECTION: Apron area where snow collection from other parts of the airport is acceptable.

CodeRunwayElement.d: A code indicating the type of Runway or Taxiway element.

v.INTERSECTION: Intersection element - with a runway or with a taxiway.
v.DISPLACED: The element between the start of the runway and the position of the displaced threshold.

CodeAuthorityRole.d: A code indicating the role of the OrganisationAuthority for the aeronautical feature.

v.SUPERVISE: The OrganisationAuthority exercises regulatory role over the facility.

CodeVOR.d: A code indicating the type of path to the next point. For example, great circle, clockwise arc, counter clockwise arc, etc.

CodeApproachLightingICAO.d: Classification of the approach lighting system using as criteria the ICAO Annex 14 standards and recommended practices.

v.SIMPLE: Simple approach lighting system (ICAO Annex 14, Vol 1, 5.3.4.2)
v.CAT1: Precision approach category I lighting system (ICAO Annex 14, Vol 1, 5.3.4.10)
v.CAT23: Precision approach category II and III lighting system (ICAO Annex 14, Vol 1, 5.3.4.22)
v.CIRCLING: Circling guidance lighting system (ICAO Annex 14, Vol 1, 5.3.6)
v.LEADIN: Runway lead-in lighting system (ICAO Annex 14, Vol 1, 5.3.7)
v.NONE: Does not classify as an ICAO type

CodeLightingJAR.d: Classification of the approach lighting system using as criteria JAR-OPS 1 - Subpart E, Appendix 1 to 1.430]

v.FALS: Full approach light facilities; comprise runway markings, 720 m or more of high/medium intensity approach lights, runway edge lights, threshold lights and runway end lights.
v.IALS: Intermediate approach light facilities; comprise runway markings, 420 to 720 m of high/medium intensity approach lights, runway edge lights, threshold lights and runway end lights.
v.BALS: Basic approach light facilities; comprise runway markings, less than 420 m of high/medium intensity approach lights (or any length of low intensity approach lights), runway edge lights, threshold lights and runway end lights.
v.NALS: None or insufficient approach light facilities; comprise runway markings, runway edge lights, threshold lights, runway end lights or no lights at all.

CodeWorkArea.d: A code indicating the type of work performed in the work area.

v.CONSTRUCTION: The work area is used for construction. Used for AMDB (DO272/ED99) Construction Area.
v.SURFACEWORK: The work area is used for surface improvements.
v.PARKED: Parked or disabled aircraft or machinery.

CodeVerticalStructureMaterial.d: A coded list of values indicating the type(s) of material that could compose the load-bearing structure and/or exterior facing of a vertical construction.

v.ADOBE_BRICK: Brick made of adobe clay and straw, dried in the sun rather than by oven firing (as are standard bricks). Larger than standard bricks, adobe bricks require a type of clay that contains between 25 and 45 percent aluminium salts.
v.ALUMINIUM: A light silvery ductile and malleable metal, not readily tarnished by air, which is a chemical element, atomic number 13. (Symbol Al)
v.BRICK: Clay kneaded, moulded, and baked or sun-dried, used as a building material.
v.CONCRETE: A heavy-duty building material made from a mixture of broken stone or gravel, sand, cement and water, that forms a stonelike mass on hardening.
v.FIBREGLASS: Any material consisting of glass filaments woven into a textile or paper, or embedded in plastic, for use as a construction or insulation material.
v.GLASS: A substance made by fusing soda and/or potash with other ingredients. Usually transparent, lustrous, hard, and brittle.
v.IRON: A malleable, magnetic, readily oxidizable metal which is a chemical element of the transition series, atomic number 26. (Symbol Fe) Occurs abundantly in certain ores and in meteorites, and is widely used, chiefly in alloys such as steel.
v.MASONRY: Building materials (for example: stone, brick, concrete, hollow-tile, concrete block, gypsum block, or other similar building units or materials and/or combination of the same) bonded together with mortar to form a structure (for example: a wall, a pier).
v.METAL: Any of the class of substances that are characteristically lustrous, ductile, fusible, malleable solids and are good conductors of heat and electricity. For example, gold, silver, copper, iron, lead, tin, and certain alloys (as brass and bronze).
v.MUD: Constructed principally from mud applied to a structural scaffold of plant material (for example: wooden posts). Effective only in extremely dry climates and usually must be resurfaced on a regular basis (for example: yearly) otherwise the structure steadily disintegrates under the effect of weather.
v.PLANT: Plant material (for example: straw and/or tall coarse grass), possibly also containing the slices of soil to which the plant material is attached. For example, used in thatching or sodding a roof.
v.PRESTRESSED_CONCRETE: Reinforced concrete in which internal stresses have been introduced to reduce potential tensile stress in the concrete resulting from loads.
v.REINFORCED_CONCRETE: Poured concrete containing steel bars or metal netting to increase its tensile strength.
v.SOD: A usually square or oblong piece or slice of earth together with the grass growing on it.
v.STEEL: Any of numerous artificially produced alloys of iron containing up to 3 per cent of other elements (including less than about 2.2 per cent carbon) and having great strength and malleability. Able to be tempered to many different degrees of hardness. Used for making tools, weapons, and/or machinery.
v.STONE: Pieces of rock or mineral substance (other than metal) of definite form and size, usually artificially shaped, and used for some special purpose. Used, for example, for building, for paving, or in the form of a block, slab, or pillar set up as a memorial and/or a boundary-mark.
v.TREATED_TIMBER: A timber that has been impregnated with chemicals (for example: creosote oil) to reduce damage from wood rot and/or insects. Often used for the portions of a structure that are likely to be in ongoing contact with soil and/or water.
v.WOOD: The hard, compact, fibrous substance of which the roots, trunks, and branches of trees and shrubs consist. Consists largely of secondary xylem, which forms the strengthening and water-transporting tissue of the plant.

CodeGuidanceLine.d: A code indicating the type of guidance line.

v.RWY: Taxi line on a runway surface, leading between the runway and other airport surfaces.
v.TWY: Taxi line on a taxiway surface, leading between the taxiway and other airport surfaces.
v.APRON: Taxi line on the apron surface.
v.GATE_TLANE: Taxi line on the apron surface, leading to a gate/stand.
v.AIR_TLANE: A virtual taxi line in the air, used by helicopters.

CodeAirportWarning.d: A code indicating a reason for caution in airport operations. For example, work in progress on a runway.

v.RUBBER_REMOVAL: Removal of rubber deposits from runways.
v.PARKED_ACFT: Parked or Disabled Aircraft located on the surface.
v.INSPECTION: Presence of people or equipment due to ground facilities inspection work in progress.
v.GRASS_CUTTING: Presence of people or equipment due to grass cutting work in progress.
v.CALIBRATION: Presence of people or equipment due to calibration work for ground facilities.

CodeProtectAreaSection.d: A code indicating the location of the Protect Area lighting.

CodeRoute.d: The route classification as ATS route or North Atlantic Tracks.

v.ATS: ATS Route as described in ICAO Annex 11.
v.NAT: North Atlantic Track (part of Organized Track System)

CodeAirspacePointPosition.d: A code indicating the location of a significant point in relation to airspace. Description: Ex: In, Out, On Border.

v.BORDER: Situated on the border of the airspace.

CodeContamination.d: An enumeration of substance types, which can contaminate airport/heliport movement areas.

v.FROST: Rime or Frost covered (depth less than 1 mm)
v.DRY_SNOW: Snow which can be blown if loose or, if compacted by hand, will fall apart again upon release; specific gravity: up to but not including 0.35.
v.WET_SNOW: Snow which, if compacted by hand, will stick together and tend to or form a snowball; specific gravity: 0.35 up to but not including 0.5.
v.SLUSH: Water-saturated snow which with a heel-and-toe slapdown motion against the ground will be displaced with a splatter; specific gravity: 0.5 up to 0.8. Note.- Combinations of ice, snow and/or standing water may, especially when rain, rain and snow, or snow is falling, produce substances with specific gravities in excess of 0.8. These substances, due to their high water/ice content, will have a transparent rather than a cloudy appearance and, at the higher specific gravities, will be readily distinguishable from slush.
v.COMPACT_SNOW: Snow which has been compressed into a solid mass that resists further compression and will hold together or break up into lumps if picked up; specific gravity: 0.5 and over.
v.DRY: Surface free of visible moisture and not contaminated.
v.STANDING_WATER: More than 3 mm of water on the surface.
v.SLIPPERY_WET: The surface friction characteristics of have been determined to be degraded on a significant portion of the surface. EASA terminology.
v.PREPARED_WINTER_RWY: A dry frozen surface of compacted snow and/or ice which has been treated with sand or grit or has been mechanically treated to improve friction. EASA terminology.
v.WET: Surface is covered by any visible dampness or water up to and including 3 mm deep.
v.WET_ICE: Ice with water on top of it or ice that is melting.
v.DRIFTING_SNOW: An ensemble of snow particles raised by the wind to small heights above the ground.

CodeMeteoConditions.d: A code indicating whether the meteorological conditions allow visual or instrumental operations.

v.IMC: [Instrument Meteorological Conditions] Weather conditions that normally require pilots to fly primarily by reference to instruments, and therefore under Instrument Flight Rules (IFR).
v.VMC: [Visual Meteorological Conditions] Weather conditions in which visual flight rules (VFR) flight is permitted. That is, conditions in which pilots have sufficient visibility to fly the aircraft maintaining visual separation from terrain and other aircraft.

CodeValueInterpretation.d: A code indicating how a value needs to be interpreted when used as a filter or condition. For example: above the value or below the value.

v.AT_OR_ABOVE: Equal or higher than the value.
v.AT_OR_BELOW: Equal or lower than the value.

CodeNavigationArea.d: code indicating the type of navigation area

CodeProcedureAvailability.d: A code indicating the availability of a procedure for use.

v.USABLE: The procedure may be flown according to its timetable. Is active and can be used.
v.UNUSABLE: Temporarily suspended because, for example, a temporary obstacle makes the procedure unsafe

CodePilotControlledLighting.d: A list to indicate the standard with which the pilot controlled lighting service complies.

CodeIntensityStandBy.d: Enumeration to indicate the intensity level of the lighting when not in use.

CodeTelecomNetwork.d: Codelist containing the Telecom Networks that can be used to address an organisation.

v.AFTN: The data interchange in the AFS is performed by the Aeronautical Fixed Telecommunications Network, AFTN. This is a message handling network running according to ICAO Standards documented in Annex 10 to the ICAO Convention
v.AMHS: Aeronautical Message Handling System. A standard for aeronautical ground-ground communications (e.g. for the transmission of NOTAM, Flight Plans or Meteorological Data) based on X.400 profiles. It has been defined by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO)
v.INTERNET: The Internet is a worldwide, publicly accessible series of interconnected computer networks that transmit data by packet switching using the standard Internet Protocol (IP)
v.ACARS: Aircraft Communications Addressing and Reporting System. A datalink system that enables ground stations (airports, aircraft maintenance bases, etc.) and commercial aircraft to communicate without voice using a datalink system.

CodeFlightDestination.d: A coded list of values that designate the intentions of a flight in relation with a location, such as arrival, departure or over-flight.

CodeServiceInformation.d: A list of codes used to designate information provision services.

v.AFIS: Airport/heliport flight information service, as defined in the ICAO Annex 11.
v.AIS: Aeronautical information service, as defined in the ICAO Annex 15.
v.ATIS: Automated terminal information service, as defined in the ICAO Annex 11.
v.FIS: A service provided for the purpose of giving advice and information useful for the safe and efficient conduct of flights.
v.OFIS_VHF: VHF operational flight information service (OFIS) broadcasts, as defined by the ICAO Annex 11.
v.OFIS_HF: HF operational flight information service (OFIS) broadcasts, as defined by the ICAO Annex 11.
v.NOTAM: Provision of NOTAM service, as defined by ICAO Annex 15.
v.INFO: Limited ad-hoc information provision, about a specific activity at a particular location.
v.SIGMET: Information issued by a meteorological watch office concerning the occurrence or expected occurrence of specified en-route weather phenomena which may affect the safety of aircraft operations.
v.VOLMET: Meteorological information for aircraft in flight broadcast service.

CodeServiceATFM.d: A list of codes used to designate flight planning and air traffic flow management services.

v.FPL: A service that provides flight planning acceptance and distribution to the ATC Units concerned.
v.FPLV: A service that provides flight planning validation.
v.CLEARANCE: A service providing permissions (entry, landing, overflying, exit, etc.) for a given location.

CodeServiceATC.d: A list of codes used to designate flight separation and ground control services.

v.ACS: En-route area control service (same as ARTCC service in US)
v.APP: Approach area control service (includes departure and arrival).

CodeServiceSAR.d: A list of codes used to designate services in relation with search and rescue.

CodeCommunicationChannel.d: A codified value that indicates a pair of frequencies or a band used for radio communications.

CodePassengerService.d: A code indicating a type of service provided to passengers at the airport.

CodeServiceGroundControl.d: A code indicating the type of ground traffic control service.

CodeStatusService.d: A coded list of values that indicate the operational capability of a service.

CodeCommunicationMode.d: A coded indicator for the type of communication channel.

v.VDL1: Legacy VHF data link protocol employing CSMA. Being replaced by VDL2
v.VDL2: VHF data link protocol employing CSMA but much more efficient than VDL1.
v.VDL4: VHF data link protocol using TDMA; being considered for use by ADS-B.
v.AMSS: Aeronautical Mobile Satellite Service, currently used by ACARS.
v.ADS_B: Automatic Dependent Surveillance - Broadcast: standard mode.
v.ADS_B_VDL: Automatic Dependent Surveillance - Broadcast: extended mode, using VDL 4.
v.VHF_833: Very High Frequency radio voice channel with 8.33 KHz spacing.

CodeCommunicationDirection.d: A coded indicator for the directionality of a communication channel.

CodeCheckpointCategory.d: The position of the checkpoint; airborne or ground

v.SIGN: Lighted sign on the side of the holding position.

v.RUNWAY_GUARD_LIGHT: Provide signal to prevent unintended incursion of an active runway by an aircraft, consisting of a pair of unidirectional yellow lights which flash continuously.

CodeNavigationAreaRestriction.d: Indicates the type of restricted area that aircraft should avoid

CodeWakeTurbulence.d: A coded indication of the wake turbulence category of the aircraft.

v.LIGHT: An aircraft type with a maximum certified take-off mass of 7 000 kg or less.
v.HEAVY: An aircraft type with a maximum certified take-off mass of 136 000 kg or more, with the exception of aircraft types listed in Doc 8643 in the SUPER category.
v.SUPER: An aircraft type specified as such in Doc 8643, Aircraft Type Designators.

v.GROUP_B: An aircraft type with a maximum certified take-off mass of 136 000 kg or more, and a wing span less than or equal to 74.68 m but greater than 53.34 m.
v.GROUP_C: An aircraft type with a maximum certified take-off mass of 136 000 kg or more, and a wing span less than or equal to 53.34 m but greater than 38.1 m.
v.GROUP_D: An aircraft type with a maximum certified take-off mass of less than 136 000 kg but more than 18 600 kg, and a wing span greater than 32 m.
v.GROUP_E: An aircraft type with a maximum certified take-off mass of less than 136 000 kg but more than 18 600 kg, and a wing span less than or equal to 32 m but greater than 27.43 m.
v.GROUP_F: An aircraft type with a maximum certified take-off mass of less than 136 000 kg but more than 18 600 kg, and a wing span less than or equal to 27.43 m.
