v.TPN19: Built by Raytheon. Described in some sources as launching control, having two Radars; Surveillance and PAR. TPN-24 and TPN-25.

CodePrimaryRadar.d: Type of Radar System (not to be confused with the component list)

v.ASR: Airport Surveillance Radar system. Airport Surveillance Radar (ASR) is a category of surveillance radars. ASR is designed to provide relatively short-range coverage in the general vicinity of an airport and to serve as an expeditious means of handling terminal traffic through observation of precise aircraft locations on a radarscope. The ASR can also be used as an instrument approach aid.
v.ARSR: Air Route Surveillance Radar system. Air Route Surveillance Radar (ARSR) or Route Surveillance Radar (RSR) is a system of remotely located, long-range radars that primarily provides a display of aircraft locations over large areas to air route traffic control centres

CodeRadarService.d: A list of service types for Radar Systems.

v.PAR: Precision Approach Radar Precision Approach Radar (PAR) is designed for use as a landing aid rather than an aid for sequencing and spacing aircraft to provide lateral and vertical guidance to an aircraft pilot for landing up to the missed approach point. PAR equipment may be used as a primary landing aid or it may be used to monitor other types of approaches. It is designed to display range, azimuth, and elevation information. It is similar to an instrument landing system (ILS) but requires control instructions. One type of instrument approach that can make use of PAR is the ground-controlled approach (GCA).
v.ARSR: Air Route Surveillance Radar Air Route Surveillance Radar (ARSR) or Route Surveillance Radar (RSR) is a system of remotely located, long-range radars that primarily provides a display of aircraft locations over large areas to air route traffic control centres
v.ASR: Airport Surveillance Radar Airport Surveillance Radar (ASR) is a category of surveillance radars. ASR is designed to provide relatively short-range coverage in the general vicinity of an airport and to serve as an expeditious means of handling terminal traffic through observation of precise aircraft locations on a radarscope. The ASR can also be used as an instrument approach aid.
v.SSR: Secondary Surveillance Radar or ATCRBS (Air Traffic Control Radar Beacon System) Secondary Surveillance Radar (SSR) (aka Secondary Radar (SECRA) or ATC Radar Beacon System (ATCRBS)) is a radar system in which the object to be detected is fitted with the cooperative equipment in the form of a radio receiver/transmitter (transponder). Radar pulses transmitted from the searching transmitter/receiver (interrogator) site are received in the cooperative equipment and used to trigger a distinctive transmission from the transponder. This reply transmission, rather than a reflected signal, is then received back at the transmitter/receiver site for processing and display at an air traffic control facility.

CodeReflector.d: Type of Reflector associated to the PAR.

v.RUNWAY_END: Reflector placed off the end of the runway

CodeStandbyPower.d: Type of power used when the radar is required to operate on standby.

CodeTransponder.d: A code indicating a transponder mode.

v.MODE_1: Mode 1 provides 2-digit 5-bit mission code. (military only - cockpit selectable)
v.MODE_2: Mode 2 provides 4-digit octal unit code. (military only - set on ground for fighters, can be changed in flight by transport aircraft)
v.MODE_3A: Mode 3/A provides a 4-digit octal identification code for the aircraft, assigned by the air traffic controller. (military and civilian)
v.MODE_4: Mode 4 provides a 3-pulse reply to crypto coded challenge. (military only)
v.MODE_5: Mode 5 provides a cryptographically secured version of Mode S and ADS-B GPS position. (military only)
v.MODE_C: Mode C provides 4-digit octal code for aircraft's pressure altitude. (military and civilian)
v.MODE_S: Mode S provides multiple information formats to a selective interrogation. Each aircraft is assigned a fixed 24-bit address. (military and civilian) Mode S, or mode select, despite also being called a transponder radar system replacement for Air Traffic Control Radar Beacon System (ATCRBS), is actually a data packet protocol which can be used to augment ATCRBS transponder positioning equipment (radar and TCAS). Mode S is designed to fully interface with ATCRBS systems: mode S SSRs can interrogate ATCRBS transponders, and AIS-P transponders will also reply to older ATCRBS and TCAS interrogations.

CodeAirspaceDependency.d: A code indicating the extent of dependency relation between an AirspaceVolume and another Airspace.

v.FULL_GEOMETRY: The overall geometry of the Airspace is used.
v.HORZ_PROJECTION: The horizontal projection of the Airspace is inherited.

CodeUnitDependency.d: A list of coded values that indicate the kind of dependency between a Unit and a RelatedUnit.

v.OWNER: The Unit is owned by (subordinated to) the RelatedUnit.
v.PROVIDER: In the provision of its services, the Unit uses the services of the RelatedUnit.
v.ALTERNATE: The RelatedUnit provide an alternate/replacement service to the current Unit.

CodeVisualDockingGuidance.d: A coded list of values that indicate types of systems used at aircraft stands in order to help the pilot align and position the aircraft.

v.AGNIS: Azimuth Guidance for Nose-In Stand, providing centreline guidance only by using two coloured lights mounted side by side.
v.PAPA: Parallax Aircraft Parking Aid consisting of a large grey/black box that uses the effect of perspective in order to indicate the relative position of the aircraft along the centreline.
v.SAFE_GATE: A type of A-VDGS that uses an aircraft symbol on a display indicating the relative position along the centreline.
v.SAFE_DOC: Safe dock allows aircraft to park up to an accuracy of 10 cm using lasers to attain the aircraft's position.
v.APIS: Aircraft Positioning and Information System that shows azimuth information using a series of parallel and black bars which kink at their midpoint.
v.A_VDGS: (Generic) Advanced Visual Docking Guidance System that features electronic displays which perform the functions of an AGNIS/PAPA installation, although with much greater accuracy. They may also provide collision avoidance from static objects.
v.AGNIS_STOP: AGNIS system complemented with a simple stop light, on the side of the AGNIS display.
v.AGNIS: Azimuth Guidance for Nose-In Stand, providing centreline guidance only by using two coloured lights mounted side by side.
v.AGNIS_STOP: AGNIS system complemented with a simple stop light, on the side of the AGNIS display.

CodeMarkingCondition.d: A coded list of values that indicate the status of the painted surface marking elements.

CodeNavaidPurpose.d: A coded list of values indicating the intended usage of a navaid (enroute or airport)

v.TERMINAL: Intended for usage in the terminal area, in particular for approach, landing and departure procedures

CodeRuleProcedure.d: An open coded list of values indicating the purpose of a rule or procedure.

v.RULE: A prescribed guide for conduct or action.
v.LAW: A binding rule, enforced by the national/international legislation.
v.PROCEDURE: A particular way of accomplishing something or of acting
v.PRACTICE: The usual way of doing something, even if it is not formally prescribed
v.ICAO_DIFF: A difference between the national rules/procedures and the ICAO Standards, Recommended Practices and Procedures.

CodeRuleProcedureTitle.d: An open list of values indicating a general heading by which a rule or procedure is usually identified in the Aeronautical Information Publications (AIP) or similar/related documents.

v.ENTRY_TRANSIT_DEPARTURE_OF_AIRCRAFT: Rules and procedures governing the entry, transit and departure of aircraft.
v.ENTRY_TRANSIT_DEPARTURE_SCHEDULED: Rules and procedures governing the entry, transit and departure of scheduled flights.
v.ENTRY_TRANSIT_DEPARTURE_NON_SCHEDULED: Rules and procedures governing the entry, transit and departure of non-scheduled flights.
v.ENTRY_TRANSIT_DEPARTURE_PRIVATE: Rules and procedures governing the entry, transit and departure of private flights.
v.PUBLIC_HEALTH_MEASURES_AIRCRAFT: Public health measures applied to arriving, departing or transit aircraft.
v.CUSTOMS_REQUIREMENTS: Customs formalities for passengers and crew.
v.IMMIGRATION_REQUIREMENTS: Immigration formalities for passengers and crew.
v.PUBLIC_HEALTH_MEASURES_PASSENGERS: Public health measures applied to disembarking or departing passengers and crew.
v.ENTRY_TRANSIT_DEPARTURE_CARGO: Regulations concerning entry, transit and departure of cargo.
v.AIRCRAFT_INSTRUMENTS_EQUIPMENT_FLIGHT_DO: Aircraft instruments, equipment and flight documents to be carried on aircraft.
v.INTERNATIONAL_AGREEMENTS_CONVENTIONS: International agreements in which the State is part and which affect air navigation.
v.DIFFERENCES_ICAO_STANDARDS_RECOMMENDED_P: Significant differences between national regulations and practices of the State and related ICAO provisions.
v.MEASURING_SYSTEM_AIRCRAFT_MARKINGS_HOLID: A table of units of measurement, calendar, time systems, geodetic reference system, EGM-96 and public holidays.
v.ABBREVIATIONS_AIS_PUBLICATIONS: A list of alphabetically arranged abbreviations used by the State in its AIP.
v.AERODROME_HELIPORT_CHARGES: Type of charges which may be applicable at airports/heliports.
v.AIR_NAVIGATION_SERVICES_CHARGES: Charges which may be applicable to air navigation services provided for international use, approach control, route air navigation services.
v.FLIGHT_RULES_GENERAL: General flight rules as applied within the State.
v.VISUAL_FLIGHT_RULES: Visual flight rules as applied within the State.
v.INSTRUMENT_FLIGHT_RULES: Instrument flight rules as applied within the State.
v.ATS_AIRSPACE_CLASSIFICATION: Description of ATS airspace classes as applied within the State.
v.HOLDING_ APPROACH_DEPARTURE_PROCEDURES: The criteria on which holding, approach and departure procedures are established for arriving flights and departing flights from any aerodrome/heliport.
v.ATS_SURVEILLANCE_SERVICES_PROCEDURES: Primary radar services and procedures, secondary surveillance radar (SSR) operating procedures and automatic dependent surveillance - broadcast (ADS-B) coverage.
v.ALTIMETER_SETTING_PROCEDURES: Altimeter setting procedures in use, containing procedures applicable to operators and cruising levels.
v.REGIONAL_SUPPLEMENTARY_PROCEDURES: Regional supplementary procedures (SUPPS) affecting the entire area of State responsibility.
v.AIR_TRAFFIC_FLOW_MANAGEMENT: ATFM structure types of flow messages and procedures applicable for departing flights, flight plan requirements and slot allocations.
v.FLIGHT_PLANNING: Procedures for the submission of a flight plan; repetitive flight plan system; and changes to the submitted flight plan.
v.ADDRESSING_FLIGHT_PLAN_MESSAGES: Addresses allocated to flight plans, showing: category of flight (IFR, VFR or both), route and message address.
v.INTERCEPTION_CIVIL_AIRCRAFT: Interception procedures and visual signals to be used.
v.UNLAWFUL_INTERFERENCE: Procedures to be applied in case of unlawful interference.
v.AIR_TRAFFIC_INCIDENTS: Definition of air traffic incidents, use of the "Air Traffic Incident Reporting Form", reporting procedures and purpose of reporting and handling of the form.
v.AERODROME_HELIPORT_AVAILABILITY: The general conditions of the State's designated authority responsible for airports and heliports availability.
v.LOCAL_TRAFFIC_REGULATIONS: Standard routes for taxiing aircraft, parking regulations, school and training flights and similar but excluding flight procedures.
v.NOISE_ABATEMENT_PROCEDURES: Detailed description of noise abatement procedures established at the aerodrome.
v.AERODROME_FLIGHT_PROCEDURES: The conditions and flight procedures, including radar and low visibility procedures at the airport/heliport and associated equipment authorized for use under these conditions.
v.AERODROME_BIRD_CONCENTRATION: Indication of the bird concentrations at the airport/heliport.
v.HOLDING_APPROACH_DEPARTURE_PROCEDURES: The criteria on which holding, approach and departure procedures are established for arriving flights and departing flights from any aerodrome/heliport.
v.INDEPENDENT_PARALLEL_APPROACHES: Simultaneous approaches to parallel or near-parallel instrument runways where separation minima are not prescribed.
v.DEPENDENT_PARALLEL_APPROACHES: Simultaneous approaches to parallel or near-parallel instrument runways where separation minima are prescribed.
v.INDEPENDENT_PARALLEL_DEPARTURES: Simultaneous departures from parallel or near-parallel instrument runways.
v.SEGREGATED_PARALLEL_OPERATIONS: Simultaneous operations on parallel or near-parallel instrument runways in which one runway is used exclusively for approaches and the other runway is used exclusively for departures.
v.STRATEGIC_LATERAL_OFFSET: Strategic Lateral Offset Procedures allowing aircraft to fly on a parallel track to the right of the centre line of route/track.

CodeGradeSeparation.d: A list of coded values that indicate the placement of an element at a different height from another element.

v.UNDERPASS: The current element is in a tunnel below another element.
v.OVERPASS: The current element is on a bridge above another element.

CodeTaxiwayElement.d: A code list of values indicating a component of the taxiway surface.

v.INTERSECTION: Intersection element - with a runway or with a taxiway.
v.HOLDING_BAY: A defined area, on the side of a taxiway, where aircraft can be held, or bypassed, to facilitate efficient surface movement of aircraft.

CodeAuralMorse.d: The sequence of dot/dash characters that corresponds to an aural Morse code.

CodeRadioSignal.d: A coded indicator for the type of information transmitted by a navaid or other radio emission source.

v.AZIMUTH: The signal supports the provision/calculation of horizontal angle information.
v.DISTANCE: The signal supports the provision/calculation of linear separation information.
v.BEAM: The signal provides a directional guidance, in the horizontal or vertical planes.
v.VOICE: The signal provides a carrier for voice information.
v.DATALINK: The signal provides a carrier for data.

CodeSignalPerformanceILS.d: A coded value indicating the signal performance level in space corresponding to the precision of an ILS or MLS system according to ICAO Annex 10, Volume I, Chapter 3.

v.IIIA: ILS Cat III with the operational performances A (DH < 100', RVR >= 175m)
v.IIIB: ILS Cat III with the operational performances B (DH < 50', 50m <= RVR < 175m)
v.IIIC: ILS Cat III with the operational performances C (DH = 0, RVR = 0m)

CodeCourseQualityILS.d: A coded value indicating the signal quality of the ILS course structure based on the location the precision signal is usable to, according to ICAO Annex 10, Volume I, Chapter 3.

v.A: Usable up to a point on the ILS glide path measured along the extended runway centre line in the approach direction to a distance of 7.5km (4NM) from the threshold.
v.B: Usable up to a point on the ILS glide path measured along the extended runway centre line in the approach direction to a distance of 1050m (3500ft) from the threshold.
v.C: Usable up to a point through which the downward extended straight portion of the nominal ILS glide path passes at a height of 30m (100ft) above the horizontal plane containing the threshold.
v.D: Usable up to a point 4m (12ft) above the runway centre line and 900m (3000ft) from the threshold in the direction of the localizer.
v.E: Usable up to a point 4m (12ft) above the runway centre line and 600m (2000ft) from the stop end of the runway in the direction of the threshold.
v.T: Usable up to a point at a specified height located above the intersection of the runway centre line and the threshold and through which the downward extended straight portion of the ILS glide path passes.

CodeIntegrityLevelILS.d: A coded value indicating the quality which relates to the trust which can be placed in the correctness of the information supplied by the ILS facility, according to ICAO Annex 10, Volume I, Attachment C.

CodeHoldingCategory.d: A coded list of values that indicates the type of precision approach for which that holding position is designed.

CodeNotePurpose.d: A code list of values that indicate the goal with which a free text Note is provided.

v.DESCRIPTION: A summary of the feature or property characteristics in a human readable form.
v.REMARK: Additional information about the feature or property, to be considered by a human operator.
v.WARNING: A notice that announces a hazard in relation with the feature or property characteristics.
v.DISCLAIMER: A denial or disavowal of legal claim with regard to the feature or property information.

CodeNavigationEquipment.d: A coded list if values indicating the aircraft capability to use a certain ground based, satellite based or on-board system for aerial navigation.

v.ADF: Automatic direction finder (ADF). An aircraft radio-navigation instrument that automatically and continuously displays the relative bearing from aircraft to a suitable radio station, including NDB.
v.DME_DME_IRU: Navigation using Distance Measuring Equipment (DME) ranging from at least two DME facilities to determine position along with use of an integrated Inertial Reference Unit (IRU).
v.FMS_RF: Flight Management System with Radius to Fix (RF) navigation capability.

CodeNavigationSpecification.d: A coded list of values that indicate a set of aircraft and flight crew requirements needed to support performance-based navigation operations within a defined airspace. There are two kinds of navigation specifications: RNP (includes the requirement for performance monitoring and alerting) and RNAV (does not include the requirement for performance monitoring and alerting).

v.RNAV_10: RNAV 10 (RNP 10) capability - for oceanic and remote continental navigation applications.
v.RNAV_5: RNAV 5 capability - for en-route and terminal navigation applications.
v.RNAV_2: RNAV 2 capability - for en-route and terminal navigation applications.
v.RNAV_1: RNAV 1 capability - for en-route and terminal navigation applications.
v.RNP_4: RNP 4 capability - for oceanic and remote continental navigation applications.
v.RNP_2: RNP 2 capability (specification to be developed by ICAO) - for various phases of flight.
v.BASIC_RNP_1: Basic RNP 1 capability - for various phases of flight.
v.ADVANCED_RNP_1: Advanced RNP 1 capability (specification to be developed by ICAO) - for various phases of flight.
v.RNAV: RNAV navigation specification (does not include the requirement for performance monitoring and alerting).
v.RNP: RNP navigation specification (includes the requirement for performance monitoring and alerting).
v.RNP_1: RNP with 1 NM navigation accuracy capability.
v.RNP_0_3: RNP with 0.3 NM navigation accuracy capability.

CodeEquipmentAntiCollision.d: A coded list if values indicating the aircraft equipment with an anti-collision system.

v.ACAS_I: Airborne Collision Avoidance System - version I, implemented as Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) I.
v.ACAS_II: Airborne Collision Avoidance System - version II, implemented as Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) II version 7.

v.AND: The result is true only when all operands are true.
v.OR: The result is true if any operand is true.
v.NOT: The result is the opposite of the operands true/false state (it applies to a single operand).

CodeStatusAirport.d: A coded list of values that indicates the availability of an airport/heliport facility for specific flight operations.

v.NORMAL: The facility operates with nominal parameters.
v.LIMITED: The facility operates below its nominal parameters, with additional usage restrictions.
v.EXTENDED: The facility operates with extended parameters.

CodeOperationManoeuvringArea.d: A coded list of values that indicates a type of activity on an airport/heliport manoeuvring area element.

v.TOUCHGO: Aircraft landing followed by an immediate take-off, without deceleration.
v.TAXIING: Aircraft taxiing along an element of the airport/heliport movement area.
v.CROSSING: Crossing an element of the airport/heliport manoeuvring area, as opposed to taxiing along that element.
v.AIRSHOW: Air show and aircraft display activities.

CodeRelativePosition.d: A coded list of values indicating a relative position, in relation with a reference point situated along a given trajectory.

v.BEFORE: A location in advance of the reference point.
v.AT: A location at the reference point.
v.AFTER: A location following the reference point

CodeBuoyDesignator.d: A designator for marking buoys on seaplane landing areas

CodeICAOCountry.d: The one or two letter country code identifier as published in the ICAO DOC 7910 - Location Indicators.

CodeReferencePathIdentifier.d: A four-character identifier that is used to confirm selection of the correct approach procedure in FAS Data Block.

CodeRouteIndicator.d: A single alpha character used to differentiate between multiple final approach segments to the same runway or heliport.

CodeAircraftFieldLength.d: A coded value representing the highest value of the aeroplane reference field lengths of the aeroplanes for which the runway is intended.

v.2: 800 m up to but not including 1 200 m.
v.3: 1 200 m up to but not including 1 800 m.

CodeAirportSign.d: Signs that situate on or near airport movement to convey a mandatory instruction, information on specific location or destination on a movement area or to provide information to meet Surface Movement Guidance & Control System (SMGCS) requirements.

v.APRON: An Inbound destination sign for general parking, servicing, and loading areas. Source: FAA AC 150/5340-18G.
v.CARGO: An Inbound destination sign for areas set aside for cargo handling. Source: FAA AC 150/5340-18G.
v.CAT_HOLD: A category I, II or III holding position sign shall be located on each side of the runway-holding position marking facing the direction of the approach to the critical area. The inscription on a category I, II, III, joint II/III or joint I/II/III holding position sign shall consist of the runway designator followed by CAT I, CAT II, CAT III, CAT II/III or CAT I/II/III, as appropriate. Source: ICAO Annex 14 p 5.4.2.15. Note FAA sign has ILS instead of CAT.
v.CIVIL: An Inbound destination sign for areas set aside for civil aircraft. Source: FAA AC 150/5340-18G.
v.FBO: An Inbound destination sign for areas fixed-base operator. Source: FAA AC 150/5340-18G.
v.FUEL: An Inbound destination sign for areas where aircraft are fueled or serviced. Source: FAA AC 150/5340-18G.
v.INFO_NAVAID: The inscription on the sign shows the facility identification, channel, radial selected (published) for the check, and the plotted distance from the antenna (when applicable). Source: ICAO Annex 14.
v.INFO_VEH: Generic sign for vehicles. Source ED99D.
v.INT_TKOF: An intersection take-off sign should be provided when there is an operational need to indicate the remaining take-off run available (TORA) for intersection take-offs. The inscription on an intersection take-off sign shall consist of a numerical message indicating the remaining take-off run available in meters plus an arrow, appropriately located and oriented, indicating the direction of the take-off. Source ICAO Annex 14.
v.INTL: An Inbound destination sign for areas set aside for handling international flights. Source: FAA AC 150/5340-18G.
v.MIL: An Inbound destination sign for areas set aside for military aircraft. Source: FAA AC 150/5340-18G.
v.MIL_HOLD: The inscription on a holding position sign located at the intersection of a taxiway or designated runway and a military landing zone/assault strip that does not have a runway designation is: “MIL LZ”. Source: FAA AC 150/5340-18G.
v.NO_ENTRY: A NO ENTRY sign shall be provided when entry into an area is prohibited. A NO ENTRY sign shall be located at the beginning of the area to which entrance is prohibited on each side of the taxiway as viewed by the pilot. Source: ICAO Annex 14.
v.OUTBOUND_DEST: Outbound destination signs identify directions to takeoff runways. These routes usually begin at the entrance to a taxiway from an apron area. The inscription is the runway number plus an arrow indicating the direction. More than one runway number, separated by a dot, may be shown where the taxiing route is common to both runways. The outbound destination sign should always direct the pilot to the beginning of a takeoff runway. Source: FAA AC 150/5340-18G.
v.PAX: An Inbound destination sign for areas set aside for passenger handling. Source: FAA AC 150/5340-18G.
v.RWY_APCH_DEP_HOLD: The inscription on a sign for a runway approach/departure area is the associated and complete runway designation followed by a dash and the abbreviation “## APCH-## DEP”. The sign is installed on taxiways located in approach/departure areas where an aircraft on a taxiway would either enter or penetrate the airspace required for the approach or departure runway (including clearway). Source AC 150/5340-18G.
v.RWY_CRITICAL: This sign identifies either the boundary of the ILS critical area, or the POFZ, or the holding position for CAT II/III operations. The sign has a black inscription that depicts the ILS holding position marking on a yellow background. This sign is used at controlled airports on taxiways where the controller commonly asks pilots to report, “clear of the ILS critical area” when exiting these areas. The pilot can use the sign as a guide in deciding when to report back to the controller. Source: FAA AC 150/5340-18G.
v.RWY_DIST_REMAIN: Runway distance remaining signs are used to provide distance remaining information to pilots during takeoff and landing operations. The sign has a white numeral inscription on a black background. Source: FAA AC 150/5340-18G.
v.RWY_EXIT: A runway exit sign shall be provided where there is an operational need to identify a runway exit. The inscription on a runway exit sign shall consist of the designator of the exit taxiway and an arrow indicating the direction to follow. Source: ICAO Annex 14.
v.RWY_INT_HOLD: The inscription on a holding position sign at a taxiway/runway intersection is the runway number(s), such as “15-33”. The runway numbers are separated by a dash, and their arrangement indicates the direction to the corresponding runway threshold. Source: FAA AC 150/5340-18G.
v.RWY_LOCATION: This sign is located to clearly identify the runways for pilots and only contains the runway designation for the one runway end. Source: ICAO Annex 14.
v.RWY_VACATED: A runway vacated sign shall be provided where the exit taxiway is not provided with taxiway center line lights and there is a need to indicate to a pilot leaving a runway the perimeter of the ILS/MLS critical/sensitive area or the lower edge of the inner transitional surface, whichever is farther from the runway center line. The inscription on a runway vacated sign shall depict the pattern A runway-holding position marking. Source: ICAO Annex 14.
v.TERM: An Inbound destination sign for gate positions at which aircraft are loaded or unloaded. Source: FAA AC 150/5340-18G.
v.TWY_DIRECTION: A direction sign shall be provided when there is an operational need to identify the designation and direction of taxiways at an intersection. The inscription on a direction sign shall comprise an alpha or alphanumeric message identifying the taxiway(s) plus an arrow or arrows appropriately oriented. Source: ICAO Annex 14.
v.TWY_END: This marker sign indicates that a taxiway does not continue beyond an intersection. FAA AC 150/5340-18G.
v.TWY_LOCATION: Sign identifies the taxiway on which an aircraft is located. Source: ICAO Annex 14.
v.VEH_STOP: Stop signs located on the airfield and are intended solely for vehicle operators. Source AC 150/5340-18G.
v.VEH_YIELD: Yield signs located on the airfield and are intended solely for vehicle operators. Source AC 150/5340-18G.

CodeApproachPrecisionCategory.d: A categorisation of the final approach leg of an Instrument Approach Procedure based on the precision of the 3D guidance systems used.

v.CAT_II_AUTOPILOT: Precision Approach Category II flown with autopilot.
v.GP_INOP: Localizer Approach (lateral guidance only, no vertical guidance). Also known as “GP-INOP” in the base of a ILS system.

CodeCourseQualityGBAS.d: A coded identifier indicating a GBAS service volume by means of a named location along the nominal approach and/or along the runway. Source: ICAO Annex 10, Vol I, Attachment D, 7.1.4.2.1

v.A: GBAS Point ‘A’. A point on a GBAS final approach segment measured along the extended runway centre line in the approach direction a distance of 7.5 km (4 NM) from the threshold.
v.B: GBAS Point ‘B’. A point on the GBAS final approach segment measured along the extended runway centre line in the approach direction a distance of 1 050 m (3 500 ft) from the threshold.
v.C: GBAS Point ‘C’. A point through which the downward extended straight portion of the nominal GBAS final approach segment passes at a height of 30 m (100 ft) above the horizontal plane containing the threshold.
v.D: GBAS Point ‘D’. A point 3.7 m (12 ft) above the runway centre line and 900 m (3 000 ft) from the threshold in the direction of the GNSS azimuth reference point (GARP).
v.E: GBAS Point ‘E’. A point 3.7 m (12 ft) above the runway centre line and 600 m (2 000 ft) from the stop end of the runway in the direction of the threshold.
v.S: GBAS Point ‘S’. A point 3.7 m (12 ft) above the runway centre line at the stop end of the runway.
v.T: GBAS reference datum (Point ‘T’). A point at a height specified by TCH located above the intersection of the runway centre line and the threshold.

CodeDataAssessmentStatus.d: A coded value indicating if the data provided for the feature was not subject to the regular data quality assurance process.

v.VERIFIED: The data has passed the processes for validation and verification.
v.NOT_VERIFIED: The data is provided without having passed the processes for validation and verification and could be inaccurate.

CodeDataLinkStandard.d: A coded value representing the standard used for Controller-Pilot Data-Link Communication (CPDLC) .

v.FANS1_A_PLUS: Future Air Navigation System 1/A+ (an updated standard).
v.ACARS_ATS: Aircraft Communications Addressing and Reporting System (ACARS) Air Traffic Services (ATS).

CodeDistanceVerticalUom.d: A code indicating the unit of measurement used for vertical distances.

v.FL: Flight level in hundreds of feet.
v.SM: Standard metric level (in tens of meters).

CodeGangway.d: A code indicating a type of gangway.

v.WATER: A gangway that exists on water or a floating dock site.
v.GROUND: A gangway that exists on the ground.

CodeGBASApproachService.d: A coded identifier designating an approach service type supported by a GBAS service.

CodeLightDirection.d: A coded value representing the direction in which lighting element emits light.

v.UNIDIRECTIONAL: Emits light in a single direction.

CodeLightingTechnology.d: A coded value representing the technology used to emit light.

CodeRelativeLocation.d: A code indicating the relative position of a resource in relation with a given place .

CodeRouteDirection.d: A code indicating a 1-dimensional direction of route, for example, forward or backward.

CodeRunwayLight.d: A code indicating types of runway lighting.

v.LAHSO_LIGHT: Indicates a Land and Hold Short position on the runway.
v.POSITION_LIGHT: Designates a specific position/border of the runway.
v.RUNWAY_INTERSECTION_LIGHT: Provides signal to aircraft on a runway that there is high speed traffic operating on the intersecting runway.
v.TAKEOFF_HOLD_LIGHT: Provide signal to aircraft in position for takeoff or rolling that it is unsafe to takeoff because the runway is occupied or about to be occupied by another aircraft or ground vehicle.
v.TWY_CL_LEAD_ON_LIGHT: Provide visual guidance to aircraft entering the runway.
v.TWY_CL_LEAD_OFF_LIGHT: Provide visual guidance to aircraft exiting the runway.

CodeSatelliteApproach.d: A categorisation of the final segment vertical and/or horizontal guidance in case of a GNSS procedure.

v.LPV: Localizer performance with vertical guidance (LPV). The label to denote minima lines associated with APV-I or APV-II performance on approach charts.
v.LNAV: Lateral navigation (LNAV) . The lateral navigation without positive vertical guidance. This type of navigation is associated with non-precision approach procedures.
v.LP: Localizer performance (LP). The label to denote minima lines associated with the lateral element of APV-1 performance on approach charts.
v.GLS: GBAS landing system (GLS). A system for approach and landing operations utilizing GNSS, augmented by a ground-based augmentation system (GBAS), as the primary navigational reference.

CodeSatelliteNavigationService.d: A coded identifier designating a type of aircraft operation (such as en-route navigation, initial approach, APV-I, etc.) supported by a satellite navigation system in a specified service area

v.TERMINAL: Terminal Area navigation, also supporting en-route navigation.
v.NPA: Non-precision approach (NPA), also supporting Initial approach, Intermediate approach, Departure.
v.APV_I: GNSS approach and landing operations with vertical guidance, level I.
v.APV_II: GNSS approach and landing operations with vertical guidance, level II.

CodeSatelliteSystem.d: A coded identifier indicating the type of the satellite system service.

v.GNSS: A core satellite constellation that provides a worldwide position and time determination system.
v.SBAS: Satellite-based augmentation system (SBAS). A wide coverage augmentation system in which the user receives augmentation information from a satellite-based transmitter.

CodeSegmentedCircle.d: A code indicating the availability of segmented circle markers.

v.NO: Segmented circle marker is not available.
v.YES_LIGHTED: Lighted segmented circle marker is available.

CodeSignalPolarization.d: A coded identifier indicating a characteristic of a radio signal based on the geometrical orientation of the oscillations in relation with the direction of the wave.

CodeSpeedInterpretationUse.d: A code indicating how a speed values should be interpreted.

CodeTaxiHoldingPosition.d: The categorisation of the designated positions intended for traffic control at which taxiing aircraft and vehicles shall stop and hold until further cleared to proceed.

v.RUNWAY_HOLDING_POSITION: Runway entrance holding position on a taxiway or on another runway (when used for taxiing).
v.TAXI_HOLD_POSITION: Holding position, taxi hold spot, hold circle, or aircraft hold point.
v.ILS_HOLDING_POSITION: Holding position for Instrument Landing System operations.

CodeTaxiwayMarking.d: A code indicating types of taxiway marking.

v.DIRECTION: Provides directional guidance at an intersection.
v.LOCATION: Identifies the taxiway upon which the aircraft is located.
v.VOR_CHECKPOINT: Designates the spot at which an aircraft can check the reception of a correct VOR signal.
v.MANDATORY_INSTRUCTION: Identifies a location beyond which an aircraft taxiing or vehicle shall not proceed unless authorized by the airport control tower.

CodeTelephoneSystem.d: A coded list of voice communication enabling technologies.

v.MOBILE: Mobile (cellular) phone communications such as: GSM, LTE, 4/5G etc.

CodeUpperAlphanumeric.d: An uppercase letter or a digit.

CodeWeatherSource.d: A code indicating a kind of weather sensor or a device that can be used to asses meteorological conditions at its location.

v.ALTIMETER: A barometric device that provides the relative distance between its location and the Mean Sea Level.
v.WIND: A device that provides information about wind (speed, direction, etc.) at its location.
v.TEMPERATURE: A device that provides information about the air temperature at its location.
v.CAMERA: A device that provides live or recorded images that can be used to asses the meteorological situation at its location.

CodeWeekDay.d: A code indicating a week day.

CodeAircraftLandingCategory.d: Classification of aircraft that provides a standardised basis for relating aircraft manoeuvrability to specific instrument approach procedures, according to PANS-OPS, VOL II, Part 1, Section 4 or to supplementary military standards.

v.A_B_C_D: Category A, B, C and D.
v.A_B_C_D_DL: Category A, B, C, D and DL.

CodePointUsage.d: A code indicating the type of association between a significant point and an airspace. For example, entry point, exit point, etc..

v.ENTRY: An initial significant point through which an aircraft may pass upon entering the associated airspace.
v.EXIT: A final significant point through which an aircraft may pass when leaving the associated airspace.
v.ENTRY_EXIT: An initial or final significant point through which an aircraft may pass upon entering or leaving the associated airspace.
v.INTERMEDIATE: A significant point within the associated airspace through which an aircraft may pass when flying through.
v.ARRIVAL: A significant point through which an aircraft may pass when flying through the associated airspace and planning to land at a specified airport/heliport.
v.DEPARTURE: A significant point through which an aircraft may pass when flying through the associated airspace after departing from a specified airport/heliport.
v.OCEANIC_ENTRY_EXIT: A significant point through which an aircraft may pass when entering or leaving the associated airspace and leaving or entering an oceanic area.
v.EN_ROUTE: The significant point is used in the route structure within the airspace.
v.TERMINAL: The significant point is used in a terminal area within the airspace.
v.MILITARY: The significant point is used by military flights within the airspace.
v.VFR: The significant point is used by VFR flights within the airspace.

CodeAdditionalEquipment.d: A code indicating a ground service or equipment either required or that can be used as an alternative to an on-board navigation capability in order to fly the procedure.

v.RADAR_DME: Radar assistance may be used as an alternative to DM.
v.RADAR_GNSS: Radar assistance may be used as an alternative to GNSS.
v.RADAR_RNAV: Radar assistance may be used as an alternative to RNAV navigation capabilities.

CodeRunwayApproachGuidance.d: A coded classification of runways based on the available visual aids and non-visual aid(s) intended for landing operations.

v.NON_INSTRUMENT: A runway intended for the operation of aircraft using visual approach procedures or an instrument approach procedure to a point beyond which the approach may continue in visual meteorological conditions.
v.NON_PRECISION: Non-precision approach runway. A runway served by visual aids and non-visual aid(s) intended for landing operations following an instrument approach operation type A and a visibility not less than 1 000 m.
v.PRECISION_CAT_I: Precision approach runway, category I. A runway served by visual aids and non-visual aid(s) intended for landing operations following an instrument approach operation type B with a decision height (DH) not lower than 60 m (200 ft) and either a visibility not less than 800 m or a runway visual range not less than 550 m.
v.PRECISION_CAT_II: Precision approach runway, category II. A runway served by visual aids and non-visual aid(s) intended for landing operations following an instrument approach operation type B with a decision height (DH) lower than 60 m (200 ft) but not lower than 30 m (100 ft) and a runway visual range not less than 300 m.
v.PRECISION_CAT_III: Precision approach runway, category III. A runway served by visual aids and non-visual aid(s) intended for landing operations following an instrument approach operation type B with a decision height (DH) lower than 30 m (100 ft), or no decision height and a runway visual range less than 300 m, or no runway visual range limitations.
v.PRECISION_CAT_IIIA: Precision approach runway, category III-A. A runway served by visual aids and non-visual aid(s) intended for landing operations following an instrument approach operation type B to and along the surface of the runway and intended for operations with a decision height (DH) lower than 30 m (100 ft), or no decision height and a runway visual range not less than 175 m.
v.PRECISION_CAT_IIIB: Precision approach runway, category III-B. A runway served by visual aids and non-visual aid(s) intended for landing operations following an instrument approach operation type B to and along the surface of the runway and intended for operations with a decision height (DH) lower than 15 m (50 ft), or no decision height and a runway visual range less than 175 m but not less than 50 m.
v.PRECISION_CAT_IIIC: Precision approach runway, category III-C. A runway served by visual aids and non-visual aid(s) intended for landing operations following an instrument approach operation type B to and along the surface of the runway and intended for operations with no decision height (DH) and no runway visual range limitations.

CodeHelicopterPerformanceClass.d: A code indicating the performance class of a helicopter.

CodePavementStrengthMethod.d: A code indicating the method used in the evaluation of the pavement strength according to the standard applied.

CodePavementBehaviour.d: A code indicating the pavement behaviour (rigid or flexible) used for determining the pavement strength according to the method or standard applied.

CodePavementSubgrade.d: A code indicating the pavement subgrade strength category according to the method or standard applied.

CodeTyrePressure.d: A code indicating the maximum allowable tyre pressure category related to a the pavement strength method or standard applied.

CodeFinalSegmentPoint.d: A code indication a conventional position in the final approach segment of an instrument approach procedure.

CodeNavigation.d: The type of air navigation (conventional or PBN).

CodeAreaAltitude.d: The coded identifier of a type of minimum altitude in relation with a specific category of flight operations to which it applies.

v.AMA_1: Area Minimum Altitude with 1 degree gridded sectors
v.AMA_05: Area Minimum Altitude with 0.5 degree gridded sectors

CodeTDMAEightSlots.d: A coded identifier indicating the time division multiple access (TDMA) slots allocated to a transmission signal in the case of a 8-slots configuration.

Ana.d: Radio navigation aid at Aerodrome / Heliport

Fda.d: Approach lighting system for FATO direction

Fdn.d: Approach and take-off direction of a FATO

Plc.d: Column of a table of cruising level

Rcp.d: Position on the centre line of a RWY

Rdd.d: Declared distance for a RWY direction

Tcp.d: Position on the centre line of a TWY

codeAcftEngineNo.d: A coded indication for the number of engines of an aircraft.

codeActivity.d: code indicating the primary activity taking place in the airspace or the reason for its establishment

codeCatAcft.d: Classification of aircraft based on 1.3 times stall speed in landing configuration at maximum certified landing mass. Category A: - less than 169 km/h (91 kt) IAS Category B: - 169 km/h (91 kt) or more but less than 224 km/h (121 kt) IAS Category C: - 224 km/h (121 kt) or more but less than 261 km/h (141 kt) IAS Category D: - 261 km/h (141 kt) or more but less than 307 km/h (166 kt) IAS Category E: - 307 km/h (166 kt) or more but less than 391 km/h (211 kt) IAS Category E: - helicopter (the stall speed method of calculating aircraft category does not apply) Category H: - helicopter (the stall speed method of calculating aircraft category does not apply) (IAS = indicated air speed)

codeCatFireAd.d: A code indicating the category of the fire fighting service provided at the aerodrome/heliport.

codeCatFuel.d: A code indicating the category of fuel available at an aerodrome/heliport.

codeCatLdgAid.d: A code indicating the category of a landing aid.

codeCatOil.d: A code indicating the category of oil available at an aerodrome/heliport.

codeChannelDme.d: A code indicating the channel of an MLS.

codeChannelMls.d: A code indicating the channel of an MLS.

codeChannelTacan.d: A code indicating the channel of a TACAN.

codeCivRte.d: Code indicating if a route is available for civil aviation or not.

codeClassAcft.d: Code of the class of aircraft that may use the route (e.g., jet, heli, prop).

codeClassAs.d: One letter code for the type of airspace according to Annex 11, Appendix 4.

codeClassHel.d: A code indicating the performance class of a helicopter.

codeClassMkr.d: A code indicating the class of a radio marker.

codeClassNdb.d: A code indicating the class of an NDB.

codeClassUnit.d: A code indicating a class of unit (depending on the service provided).

codeColour.d: A code indicating a colour. The list of allowable values comprises 'named' colours, not colours being only describable using the RGB or the CYMK or another colour system combination.

codeCombTimeEvent.d: A code indicating which event in a list of events in time should be given precedence over the others. E.g. the earliest or the latest.

codeComponentTacan.d: A code indicating one of the two components of a TACAN facility.

codeCompositionSfc.d: A code indicating the composition of a surface. Eg. asphalt, concrete etc..

codeCondSfc.d: A code indicating the condition of a RWY, TWY, SWY, FATO, TLOF or APRON surface.

codeDatum.d: A code indicating the geodetic datum in which the geographical co-ordinates are expressed (list of allowable based on the ICAO WGS-84 Manual; abbreviations based on ARINC 424, Attachment 2).

codeDay.d: A code indicating a particular day. E.g. : Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday, the day preceding a holiday, a legal holiday, the day following a holiday, the day preceding a working day, a working day, the day following a working day.

codeDayPeriod.d: A code indicating a time period within a day. E.g. day or night.

codeDescrDistVer.d: A code indicating if a waypoint should be crossed 'at', 'at or above', 'at or below' a specific altitude or 'between' two specified altitudes.

codeDir.d: A code indicating a 1-dimensional direction, e.g. forward or backward.

codeDirRef.d: A code indicating a direction with regard to a reference point, e.g. to or from.

codeDirTurn.d: A code indicating the direction of a turn.

codeDistVer.d: A code indicating the reference for a vertical distance. Two series of values exist: 1) real distance: from GND, from the MSL, from the WGS-84 ellipsoid 2) pressure distance: QFE, QNH, STD.

codeEmRdo.d: A code indicating the type of emission, as defined at the 1979 ITU World Administrative Radio Conference. E.G. : A3E, NONA2a, G1D.

codeFltStatus.d: A code indicating status of a flight.

codeFltType.d: A code indicating the type of a flight.

codeIapFix.d: A code indicating the role of a fix within an instrument approach procedure. Examples: initial approach fix, final approach fix, missed approach point, etc.

codeIcaoAircraftType.d: A coded aircraft type designator assigned by ICAO to all aircraft heavier than micro-/ultra-light and published in ICAO DOC 8643.

codeIdAdHp.d: A coded identifier for an Aerodrome/Heliport. The rules according to which this identifier should be formed are as follows: 1) If the AD/HP has an ICAO four letter location indicator, this will become the CODE_ID for the Aerodrome/Heliport; 2) If the AD/HP does not have an ICAO four letter location indicator but has an IATA three letter code, then this will become the CODE_ID for the Aerodrome/Heliport; 3) If the AD/HP does not have either an ICAO four letter location indicator or an IATA three letter code, an artificially generated code will be used. This will contain a group of letters and a number. The group of letters could be the 2 letter code of the State responsible for the Aerodrome/Heliport (or one of these, if there are more than one, like ED and ET for Germany) and the number could be an integer between 0001 and 9999.

codeIdAs.d: A coded value allowing the unique identification of the airspace in question.

codeIdChainSpecNav.d: The coded identifier of a special navigation system chain.

codeIdDesigPt.d: The coded identifier of a designated point.

codeIdIlsMls.d: The coded identifier of an ILS or MLS.

codeIdLvlClmn.d: A code identifying the column within a table of discreet cruising levels. E.g. east (000 to 179 degrees) or west (180 to 359 degrees) even.

codeIdLvlTbl.d: A code identifying the table of discreet cruising levels. Ex: ICAO IFR, ICAO VFR, ICAO RVSM, etc..

codeIdMkr.d: The coded identifier of a marker. Ex: Dots, Dashes, Dot/Dash.

codeIdNavAid.d: The coded identifier of a radio navigation aid.

codeIdOrg.d: The coded identifier of the organisation, authority, agency or unit.

codeIdRestr.d: A coded value which uniquely identifies a traffic flow restriction.

codeIntlRte.d: Code indicating if a route is international or domestic.

codeIntstLgt.d: A code indicating the light intensity. Eg: LIL, LIM, LIH, etc.

codeLang.d: A code indicating a language (according to ISO 639).

codeLocIndIata.d: The three letter coded location identifier of an aerodrome/heliport according to the IATA Resolution 763.

codeLocIndIcao.d: The four letter coded location identifier of an aerodrome/heliport based on the ICAO DOC 7910/78 - Location Indicators.

codeLovReference.d: A code indicating the standard referred to by a list of values, in case where different aviation authorities use different categorisation criteria.

codeLvl.d: A code indicating the level: upper airspace, lower airspace or both.

codeMil.d: A code distinguishing between military and civil status.

codeOpr.d: An 'operator' in coded form according to which two 'operants' will be 'associated' in order to produce a result.

codeOprAs.d: An 'operator' in coded form according to which the geometry of an airspace will contribute to the geometry of an aggregated airspace.

codeOrigin.d: A code indicating the origin with regard to international borders.

codePcnEvalMethod.d: A code indicating the method used in the evaluation of a PCN number.

codePcnPavementType.d: A code indicating the pavement behaviour (rigid or flexible) used for the PCN determination.

codePcnPavementSubgrade.d: A code indicating the subgrade strength category related to a PCN number.

codePcnMaxTirePressure.d: A code indicating the maximum allowable tire pressure categoryrelated to a PCN number.

codePhaseProc.d: A code indicating a phase of a SID, STAR or IAP. Note: Some of the values apply only for a SID, other apply only for a STAR and other apply only for an IAP (the 'A' value).

codePreparationSfc.d: A code indicating the preparation technique for a surface area.

codePsnApron.d: A code indicating a location on the surface of an apron.

codePsnIls.d: A code indicating a position in the ILS system. E.g. outer, middle, inner, backcourse.

codePsnRelAxis.d: A code indicating a position, relative to the an axis. For example: left/right of a runway centreline.

codePsnRwy.d: A code indicating the position of an item on a surface of a runway. Eg: THR, runway end, runway centre line, TDZ, etc.

codePsnTlof.d: A code indicating the position of an item on the surface of a Touch Down and Lift-off Area.

codePsnTwy.d: A code indicating the position of an item on the surface of a taxiway.

codePurpose.d: A code indicating the purpose of a flight.

codeRefOch.d: A code indicating the reference position for the obstacle clearance height.

codeRepAtc.d: A code indicating the type of position report required by an ATC Unit. Eg.: compulsory or on request.

codeRnp.d: A code indicating the value of the required navigation performance.

codeRteAvbl.d: A code indicating the route segment availability whether within the Flexible Use of Airspace concept or not.

codeRvsmPoint.d: A code indicating that the point has a specific role in the RVSM context.

codeSourceSer.d: A code indicating the source of the service type. The list of allowable values is open-ended.

codeSpecialDate.d: A code indicating the type of a special date, such as 'holiday', 'busy Friday', etc.

codeSpeedRef.d: A code indicating the reference system for a speed value.

codeStrengthSfc.d: [Deprecated] A code indicating the convention used to measure the strength of a surface. Eg: PCN, SIWL, etc..

codeStsSfc.d: A code indicating the operational status of a runway, taxiway, gate, parking position, FATO etc.. Eg: serviceable, unserviceable, closed, work in progress, etc..

codeTimeEvent.d: A code indicating an event occurrence during any day. Ex: sunrise, sunset.

codeTimeRef.d: A code indicating the time reference system: UTC or 'UTC adjustable for summer time'(the specified time is applicable during winter; during the summer time - daylight saving time - the value must be decreased by one hour).

codeTypeAcft.d: A code indicating the type of an aircraft

codeTypeAcftCap.d: A code indicating the type of equipment and certification of an aircraft for a specified capability; i.e.: RNAV, RVSM, etc.

codeTypeAcftEngine.d: A code indicating the type of aircarft engine (e.g., jet, piston, turbo).

codeTypeAddress.d: A code indicating the address type. Ex: postal address, phone number, fax number, AFS address, E-mail address, telex number, etc..

codeTypeAdHp.d: A code specifying whether a particular entity occurrence is an Aerodrome or a Heliport.

codeTypeAdHpClc.d: A code indicating the extent of collocation between an aerodrome and a heliport.

codeTypeAeroLgt.d: A code indicating a type of aeronautical ground light. Eg: Marine, RWY BCN, ABN, IBN, etc.

codeTypeAirspaceVertex.d: A code indicating the type of path to the next point of an airspace vertex, which is always a closed path. E.g. great circle, rhumbline, geoidal line, clockwise arc, counter clockwise arc, etc.

codeTypeAlsFato.d: A code indicating the type of approach lighting system of a FATO direction. Eg: ICAO CAT I, ICAO CAT II, simple approach lighting system.

codeTypeAlsRwy.d: A code indicating the type of approach lighting system of a runway direction. Eg: ICAO CAT I, ICAO CAT II, simple approach lighting system.

codeTypeAngleBrg.d: A code indicating the type of angle: magnetic, bearing, VOR radial.

codeTypeApchProc.d: A code indicating a type of approach procedure. Eg: straight-in, circling, straight-in CAT I, etc..

codeTypeAssocAs.d: The values indicating the type of association between two airspaces.

codeTypeAssocOrg.d: The values indicating the type of association between two organisations/authorities.

codeTypeAssocUnit.d: The values indicating the type of association between two units.

codeTypeAsAuth.d: A code indicating the type of the responsability that one organisation/authority has for an airspace. Ex: The airspace is under the jurisdiction of Organization/Authority or the airspace is delegated to the Organization/Authority for the provision of air traffic services.

codeTypeAsSignpnt.d: A code indicating the type of association between a significant point and an airspace. E.g. entry point, exit point, etc..

codeTypeAzm.d: A code indicating the type of azimuth equipment: normal or backward.

codeTypeBorderVertex.d: A code indicating the type of path to the next point of a geographical border vertex (open polyline).

codeTypeClineVertex.d: A code indicating the type of path to the next point of a centreline, such as great circle or rhumbline.

codeTypeCourse.d: A code indicating the type of course to be observed. E.g. true track, magnetic track, heading, VOR radial, true bearing, magnetic bearing.

codeTypeDeclDistFato.d: A code indicating the type of conventional declared distance for a Final Approach and Take-Off Direction. Eg: LDAH, RTODAH, etc..

codeTypeDeclDistRwy.d: A code indicating the type of conventional declared distance for a runway. Eg: TORA, TODA, LDA, etc..

codeTypeDesigPt.d: A code indicating a specific type of designated point whether published by the State, published by ICAO or created by another agency for convenience of identification.

codeTypeDme.d: A code indicating the type of UHF distance measuring equipment.

codeTypeFltRule.d: Flight rules to be observed by aircraft. E.g. VFR and/or IFR.

codeTypeFreq.d: Type of special frequency used by a service.

codeTypeGeoBdr.d: The type of geograpfical border. The most common situation is the border between two countries.

codeTypeHoldProc.d: A code indicating the type of holding procedure. E.g. en-route holding, terminal area holding.

codeTypeHrNavAid.d: A code indicating the type of schedule a timesheet is describing. E.g. working hours, un-monitored hours.

codeTypeIap.d: A code indicating the type of the Instrument Approach Procedure. E.g. Approach Transition, VOR/DME Approach, Instrument Landing System (ILS), NDB Approach, GPS Approach.

codeTypeLight.d: A code indicating a type of light source, such as strobe or flood.

codeTypeMilOps.d: A code indicating if a facility is to be used for military, civil or both types of operations.

codeTypeNavAidLimit.d: A code indicating the type of radio navigation aid limitation.

codeTypeNavCkPt.d: A code indicating the type of navigation system for which the checkpoint has been established. E.g. INS, VOR, GNSS, etc..

codeTypeNitrogen.d: A code describing the type of nitrogen supplies for aviation usage.

codeTypeNorth.d: A code indicating the type of the North reference used.

codeTypeOpsRwy.d: A code indicating the type of operation performed using a runway direction. E.g. approach or take-off.

codeTypeOrg.d: A code indicating the type of an Organisation/Authority. Ex: State, Association of States, International Organisation, etc..

codeTypeOxygen.d: A code describing the type of oxygen supplies for aviation usage.

codeTypePaxFac.d: A code indicating a type of passenger facility available. E.g. hotels, restaurants, transportation, medical service, etc.

codeTypeProcPath.d: A code that defines a specific type of flight path and a specific type of termination of that flight path. Although we agree with the ARINC idea that procedures should be designed with the aim to permit FMS equipped aircraft to fly tracks instead of procedural headings, for the time being we must allow all representation of these procedures (especially reversal procedures) as they are published by the States. This is the explanation of the differences between the allowable values for attributes in this domain and the ARINC leg types.

codeTypeProtectAreaFato.d: A code indicating the type of protection area for a FATO. E.g. clearway, ILS protection area, safety area, etc..

codeTypeProtectAreaRwy.d: A code indicating the type of protection area for a runway E.g. clearway, obstacle free zone, ILS protection area, etc..

codeTypeRelAs.d: A code indicating how the two airspace are associated together.

codeTypeRestr.d: A code indicating if the restriction is an interdiction or a mandatory routing.

codeTypeRte.d: The type of the route from the navigation point of view. E.g. conventional, RNAV, etc..

codeTypeSegPath.d: A code indicating the type of segment path.

codeTypeSer.d: Type of a service such as Flight Information etc.

codeTypeSerAd.d: A code indicating the type of ground service at an aerodrome/heliport. E.g. customs, immigration, health and sanitation, handling, security, de-icing, hangaring, repairing, rescue, disabled aircraft removal, fire fighting, clearing, fuelling.

codeTypeSerSpecNav.d: A code indicating the type of service provided by a station in a special navigation system chain, depending on the type of the system.

codeTypeSid.d: A code indicating a type of Standard Instrument Departure (SID). E.g. SID, RNAV SID, Engine out SID or FMS SID.

codeTypeSpecNavSys.d: A code indicating a type of special navigation system. E.g. LORAN, DECCA, GNSS, etc.

codeTypeStand.d: A code indicating the type of stand. E.g. parking position on the apron, isolated aircraft stand, terminal building gate, etc..

codeTypeStar.d: A code indicating a type of Standard Arival Route (STAR): convetional, RNAV, FMS.

codeTypeTimetable.d: A code indicating the type of timetable (working hours, activation hours) associated with a specific activity.

codeTypeTlofVertex.d: A code indicating the type of path to the next point of a TLOF related area. E.g. line, circle, clockwise arc, counter clockwise arc, etc.

codeTypeTwy.d: A code indicating a type of taxiway. E.g. normal taxiway, apron taxiway, air taxiway, etc..

codeTypeUnit.d: A unit providing particular ATS services.

codeTypeUseBackIls.d: A code indicating the usability of the localizer signal in the back-course sector.

codeTypeVasis.d: A code indicating a type of visual approach slope indicator system. Eg: VASIS, AVASIS, 3-BAR VASIS, PAPI, APAPI, etc..

codeTypeVertex.d: A code indicating the type of path to the next point. E.g. great circle, rhumbline, geoidal line, clockwise arc, counter clockwise arc, etc.

codeTypeVor.d: A code indicating the type of VOR, e.g. conventional VOR or Doppler VOR.

codeUsageLimitation.d: A code indicating whether a limitation is of type permission, interdiction or exclusive usage

codeYesNo.d: A code for a logical value: Yes or No.

dateMonthDay.d: A date value without year indication. Same each year. E.g. 15-02, 29-04.

dateYear.d: A date for which only the year value is significant.

time.d: A time (hours and minutes) value with a resolution of 1 minute. E.g.: 12:45, 14:30, 00:00.

timeLap.d: A lapse (length or portion) of time expressed in number of minutes. It may be positive or negative. E.g. 10 min, 300 min, -20 minutes.

txtAddress.d: A full free text address. E.g. +32(2)-729 3326, edgr@eurocontrol.be, LABBYOYX, etc..

txtDesigIap.d: The textual designator of a SID, STAR or IAP (instrument approach procedure).

txtDesigRte.d: The textual designator of an en-route route.

txtName.d: The official name of a State, an aerodrome, a unit, etc..

uomDistHorz.d: A unit of measurement for a horizontal distance. E.g. metres, feet, nautical miles, kilometres, etc. .

uomDistVer.d: A unit of measurement for a vertical distance. E.g. Flight Level, metres, feet.

uomDur.d: A unit of measurement for time. E.g. seconds, minutes, hours.

uomElev.d: A unit of measurement for an elevation. E.g. metres or feet.

uomFreq.d: A unit of measurement for a frequency. E.g. Hz, kHz, MHz,GHz.

uomPressure.d: A unit of measurement for pressure values.

uomSpeed.d: A unit of measurement for speed.

uomT.d: A unit of measurement for temperature.

uomWeight.d: A unit of measurement for weight values.

valAngleBrg.d: The value of a bearing indication (at a given point) measured as the angle between the direction and either True North or Magnetic North (this should appear explicitly or implicitly). The angle is measured clockwise from 0 degrees up to and including 360 degrees. The value can also be a VOR radial. For example, “westward” is expressed as 270.

valAngleMagVar.d: The value of an angle (at a given point) between the direction of Magnetic North and the direction of Geographical North. A positive value indicates that Magnetic North is East of Geographical North. A negative value indicates that Magnetic North is West of Geographical North.

valAngleMagVarChg.d: The value of the annual rate of change of the magnetic variation. The unit of measurement would be degrees/year and can be positive or negative, i.e qualified by EAST (E) or WEST (W).

valDistVer.d: A vertical distance value. E.g.: Upper and lower limis of an airspace, an ATS route, FL100, 600M, 300 FT, etc..

valDur.d: A duration value or elapsed time period. E.g. 5 minutes, 200 seconds, etc..

valFl.d: A value expressed in flight levels (FL).

valFreq.d: The frequency value of a navigation system.

v.A: Class of Airspace per ICAO Annex 11. Appendix 4. IFR flights only are permitted; all flights are provided with air traffic control service and are separated from each other.
v.B: Class of Airspace per ICAO Annex 11. Appendix 4. IFR and VFR flights are permitted; all flights are provided with air traffic control service and are separated from each other.
v.C: Class of Airspace per ICAO Annex 11. Appendix 4. IFR and VFR flights are permitted; all flights are provided with air traffic control service and IFR flights are separated from other IFR flights and from VFR flights. VFR flights are separated from IFR flights and receive traffic information.
v.D: Class of Airspace per ICAO Annex 11. Appendix 4. IFR and VFR flights are permitted and all flights are provided with air traffic control service, IFR flights are separated from other IFR flights and receive traffic information in respect of VFR flights, VFR flights receive traffic information in respect of all other flights.
v.E: Class of Airspace per ICAO Annex 11. Appendix 4. IFR and VFR flights are permitted; IFR flights are provided with air traffic control service and are separated from other IFR flights. All flights receive traffic information as far as is practical. Class E shall not be used for control zones.
v.F: Class of Airspace per ICAO Annex 11. Appendix 4. IFR and VFR flights are permitted, all participating IFR flights receive an air traffic advisory service and all flights receive flight information service if requested. Description: Where air traffic advisory service is implemented, this is considered normally as a temporary measure only until such time as it can be replaced by air traffic control.
v.G: Class of Airspace per ICAO Annex 11. Appendix 4. IFR and VFR flights are permitted and receive flight information service if requested.
